SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
S.1, Special Branch
REPORT
Date August 3, 1937.
Subject. National salvation Leaders Released.
Made by. D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by. C. Simpson
The seven national salvation leaders, Messrs.
Sung Chun-dz, Tsang Nai-chi, So Chien Li, Li Kung Poh, Tseu
Tao Fung, Wong Zao Dz and Miss Sz Lieng, who have been under
detention since November 23, 1936, on a charge of being
reactionaries, were released on bail on July 31, 1937. They
arrived here from Soochow by rail at 11.30 a.m. August 1,
and were welcomed by some 30 relatives and intimate friends
at the Shanghai North Railway Station.
At 1.15 p.m. August 1, these seven people were
entertained to luncheon at the Dinty Moore Restaurant, No.35
Ningpo Road, by some fifty persons, including Messrs. Tsang
Ts-zang (張志讓), lawyer, Pang Vung-ying (彭文應), professor
of the Shanghai Law College, who claimed to be the
representative of the various local national salvation
associations. A small number of students from the Liang
Zai Supplementary School, Continental Emporium Building,
Nanking Road, also attended the luncheon. Speeches were
delivered by the seven guests in which they asserted that
they would continue their efforts in the cause of national
salvation and what the organization stood for.
At 3.20 p.m. the lunchoen finished and the students
of the Liang Zai Supplementary School took their departure,
the remaining people, composed of relatives and friends, staying
to dinner in the Restaurant.
At 11 p.m. August 2, the seven national salvation
leaders left Shanghai for Nanking by rail to receive their
instructions from the National Government.
Pan Lien-pih

报告
日期 1937年8月3日。
主题：救国会领导人获释。
制作人：潘连璧侦探督察 呈报人：C. Simpson
七位救国会领导人，即沈钧儒、章乃器、沙千里、李公朴、邹韬奋、王造时和施良女士，自1936年11月23日起因涉嫌为反动分子而被拘留，于1937年7月31日保释出狱。他们于8月1日上午11时30分乘火车从苏州抵达此处，在上海北站受到约30名亲属和密友的欢迎。
8月1日下午1时15分，这七人在宁波路35号丁蒂摩尔餐厅（Dinty Moore Restaurant）参加由约五十人举办的午宴，其中包括律师张志让（Tsang Ts-zang）、上海法政学院教授彭文应（Pang Vung-ying），后者声称代表各地各类救国会。南京路大陆商场（Continental Emporium Building）良才补习学校的一小部分学生也参加了午宴。七位宾客相继发表演讲，宣称将继续致力于救国事业及其组织宗旨。
下午3时20分，午宴结束，良才补习学校的学生离去，其余由亲友组成的人员留在餐厅用晚餐。
8月2日晚11时，七位救国会领导人乘火车离开上海前往南京，以接受国民政府的指示。
潘连璧

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS. SUNDAY. AUGUST 1 1937

SALVATION LEADERS
BAILED OUT

Exiled Writer Also Returns
from Abroad

Coincident with the return of the
exiled "left wing" writer, Mr. Kuo
Mei-shu, the seven leaders of the
Federation of National Salvation
Association, who have been detained
in Soochow since November last year,
have been released on bail.
Mr. Kuo left China for Japan ten
years ago. The warrant for his
arrest was only cancelled a few days
ago at a Government meeting held in
Nanking. Leaving his Japanese wife
and five children at home in the out-
skirts of Tokyo Mr. Kuo boarded the
Empress of Japan at Kobe unnoticed.
It was reported that Mr. Kuo's move-
ments were watched by the Japanese
gendarmes during his sojourn in
Japan.
The seven leaders of the salvation
association, including Mr. Shen Chun-
ju, who have been advocating armed
resistance against Japan, were charged
by the High Court in Soochow with
undermining the security of the Chi-
nese Republic. After their release,
they are planning to visit Nanking.
The families of the seven leaders left
here for Soochow to meet them yes-
terday morning.
The ban on "national salvation"
songs, which have been considered
radical, has also been lifted. These
are now allowed to be broadcast.

G.J.J.Lx

《字林西报》，1937年8月1日，星期日

救国会领导人
获保释

流亡作家亦从海外归来

随着“左翼”流亡作家郭沫若先生的归来，去年11月以来被拘留在苏州的全国救国会联合会七位领导人也已获保释。
郭先生十年前离开中国前往日本。直到几天前在南京举行的一次政府会议上，对他的逮捕令才被撤销。郭先生将日本妻子和五个孩子留在东京郊区的家中， unnoticed 地在神户登上了“日本皇后号”轮船。据报道，郭先生在日期间，其行动一直受到日本宪兵的监视。
包括沈钧儒先生在内的七位救国会领导人一直主张武装抗日，被苏州高等法院指控危害中华民国安全。获释后，他们计划访问南京。七位领导人的家属于昨天上午从这里出发前往苏州迎接他们。
此前被视为激进而被禁止的“救亡”歌曲禁令也已解除。现在允许广播这些歌曲。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, AUGUST 1, 1937
7 Salvationists Freed·
To Pay Visit In Nanking
The seven All-China National
Salvation Association leaders were
released from the detention
house in Soochow yesterday
afternoon. They were released
on bail through the bond of
four influential Soochow citizens.
These leaders, who were ar-
rested in Shanghai last year
charged with undermining the
security of the State are:
Mr. Shen Chun-ju, lawyer;
Mr. Chang Nai-chi, banker; Mr.
Tsou Tao-fen, editor of Life
Weekly; Mr. Li Kung-po,
educator; Mr. Wang Chao-shih,
author; Mr. Sho Chien-li, lawyer;
and Miss Sse Liang, lawyer.
Upon hearing of their release
yesterday, friends and relatives
streamed to Soochow High Court
to "welcome" them. Many of
them made long-distance tele-
phone calls to congratulate them.
For their release, each of the
seven leaders was requested to
pay $200 as guarantee in accord-
ance with law.
At present they are staying
at Soochow, making calls on
some local officials. Then they
plan to visit Nanking before
coming to Shanghai. Mr. Shen
Chun-ju, one of the seven, said
that he would continue his work
for the salvation of the country.

《大美晚报》，1937年8月1日，星期日
7名救国会成员获释·
拟往南京拜访

全中国救国会七位领导人昨天下午从苏州拘留所获释。他们在四位有影响力的苏州市民的担保下获得保释。
这些领导人去年在上海被捕，被控危害国家安全，他们是：
律师沈钧儒先生；银行家章乃器先生；《生活周刊》编辑邹韬奋先生；教育家李公朴先生；作家王造时先生；律师沙千里先生；以及律师施良女士。
昨天得知他们获释的消息后，朋友和亲属涌向苏州高等法院“欢迎”他们。许多人打长途电话向他们表示祝贺。
根据法律规定，七位领导人每人需缴纳200元作为保证金以获得释放。
目前他们住在苏州，拜访一些地方官员。然后他们计划在来上海之前先访问南京。七人之一的沈钧儒先生表示，他将继续为国家救亡工作。

THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, AUGUST 2, 1937
23293

7 Salvationist
Leaders Here
From Soochow

Big Welcome Given
Group Long Held
In Prison

AWAIT REPLY
FROM CHIANG

Shen Chun-ju Looks
Pale; Miss Liang
Gained Weight

Looking none the worse for their eight-month detention in Soochow since last December, the seven All-Chinese National Salvation Association leaders, whose arrest last year caused a sensation in Shanghai, arrived here from Soochow at eleven o'clock yesterday morning.

The seven Salvationist leaders, headed by Mr. Shen Chun-ju, aged lawyer, were released on bail by the Soochow high court Saturday. It was announced that they would proceed to Nanking first before returning to Shanghai, and their unexpected arrive here yesterday morning was known to only a few of their relatives and friends beforehand.

Stepping off their train, the Salvationists found that a large crowd of their local followers were waiting at the station to welcome them. On the station platform, they spoke briefly and joined in shouting patriotic slogans.

Not Dampen Patriotism

At 1 o'clock, the seven salvation leaders, whose case for allegedly attempting to undermine the security of the state is still pending before the High Court, were entertained at luncheon, at which some 330 people were present. In turn, the seven guests of honor spoke, pledging that their arrest and long detention will not put a damper on their active patriotism.

Mr. Shen, the oldest member of the group who wears a bushy black beard and goatee, was looking slightly pale. He was dressed in a white linen gown, while his companions were attired in foreign clothes.

Miss Sze Liang, well-known local woman lawyer, appeared to have added some weight during her eight-month stay in the detention house. She was wearing a natty foreign style dress made of Chinese cotton material.

Shortly after their arrival, a joint statement was issued to the press, which revealed that they were waiting for a reply wire from Gen. Chiang Kai-shek, President of the Executive Yuan, before proceeding to Nanking. A telegram was sent to the Generalissimo immediately after they were released from the detention house in Soochow, asking for an interview.

Commenting on the current situation, the Salvationists were of the belief that two major issues now confront the nation: national consolidation and resistance against Japan.

They believe that under the guidance of the Central Government, a momentous war for China's racial independence will be fought, in which the final victory will be on the Chinese side.

（批：8/2 DR）
（批：G.D.S.L C 3/4 ↓ 8/5 8/8）

《大美晚报》，1937年8月2日，星期一
23293

7位救国会
领导人抵沪
来自苏州

长期囚禁的团体
受到热烈欢迎

等待蒋介石
回复

沈钧儒面色苍白；施良女士
体重增加

七位全中国救国会领导人自去年12月以来在苏州被拘留八个月，看起来并未因此受损，他们于昨天上午11点从苏州抵达此处，去年他们的逮捕曾在上海引起轰动。

这七位救国会领导人由年长的律师沈钧儒先生率领，于周六由苏州高等法院保释。此前宣布他们将先前往南京，然后再返回上海，因此只有少数亲友事先知道他们昨天上午意外抵达此处。

走下火车，救国会成员发现大批本地追随者在车站等候欢迎他们。在站台上，他们简短发言并一起高呼爱国口号。

爱国热情未减

下午1点，这七位救国会领导人（其涉嫌企图危害国家安全的案件仍在高等法院审理中）出席午宴，约有330人参加。七位贵宾依次发言，保证他们的逮捕和长期拘留不会削弱他们积极的爱国热情。

沈先生是这群人中最年长的，留着浓密的黑胡子和山羊胡，脸色略显苍白。他身穿白色亚麻长袍，而同伴们则穿着西式服装。

当地知名女律师施良女士在拘留所待了八个月后，似乎增加了一些体重。她穿着一件由中式棉料制成的时髦西式连衣裙。

抵达后不久，他们向新闻界发表了一份联合声明，透露他们在前往南京之前，正等待行政院院长蒋介石将军的复电。昨天从苏州拘留所获释后，他们立即向委员长发去电报，请求接见。

评论当前局势时，救国会成员认为国家目前面临两大问题：国家团结和抗日。

他们认为，在中央政府的指导下，一场关乎中国种族独立的重大战争即将打响，最终胜利将属于中国一方。

（批：8月2日 DR）
（批：G.D.S.L C 3/4 ↓ 8月5日 8月8日）

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, AUGUST 2, 1937

As the seven leaders of the National
Salvation Movement, detained last
year for advocating armed resistance
against Japan, have regained their
freedom, local Chinese public bodies
have submitted petitions to the
Central Kuomintang and the Nanking
Garrison Commander asking them
likewise to release Messrs. Sun Shao-
tsung and Tsao Meng-chun, two
officials who were detained in
November last for participating in the
national salvation movement, and
who have since been held in Nan-
king.

鉴于去年因主张武装抗日而被拘留的救国运动七位领导人已重获自由，本地华人公共团体已向国民党中央和南京卫戍司令提交请愿书，要求同样释放孙晓宗（Sun Shao-tsung）和曹孟君（Tsao Meng-chun）两位官员，他们去年11月因参与救国运动而被拘留，此后一直被关押在南京。

Lih Pao publishes the following telegram from Soochow :- 31-7-37 (A.M.)

NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS TO BE RELEASED TO-DAY

It is learned that the Kiangsu High Court has granted the request made by Messrs. Chang Ih-ching (張一麐), Chang Ih-beng (張一鵬), Li Keng-yuen (李根源), Zien Shien-tsoo (錢錦琴) and other well-known people in Soochow for the release of Sung Chun-dz and six others who have been detained for about seven months in connection with the National Salvation Association. The seven persons will be released to-day (July 31).

According to reliable information received, Sung Chun-dz and the six other national salvation leaders will regain their freedom. At present the seven persons are fulfilling the procedure of furnishing securities. Their families will proceed to Soochow this morning to assist in the matter. On leaving the detention house to-day, the seven persons will call on the gentry of Soochow to express their appreciation for the assistance rendered them. Yesterday they sent a telegram to Generals Chiang Kai-shek and Feng Yu-hsiang expressing their willingness to proceed to Nanking to listen to instructions regarding policies for national salvation, but up to last night they had not received any reply.

Before returning to Shanghai, Sung Chun-dz and the six others will first make a trip to Nanking.

According to a statement made to a reporter of this paper by the families of the seven persons, the latter will come to Shanghai for a short stay after regaining their liberty. They will continue to undertake national salvation work under the leadership of the National Government.

S. I.
dR

《立报》刊登如下来自苏州的电讯：- 1937年7月31日（上午）

救国会领袖将于今日获释

据悉，江苏高等法院已批准张一麐先生、张一鹏先生、李根源先生、钱锦琴先生（音译）及其他苏州知名人士提出的请求，释放因全国救国会案被羁押约七个月的沈钧儒等七人。该七人将于今日（7月31日）获释。

据收到的可靠消息，沈钧儒及其他六位救国会领袖将重获自由。目前，该七人正在办理具保手续。他们的家属将于今晨前往苏州协助办理此事。该七人今日离开拘留所后，将拜访苏州士绅，以感谢他们所提供的帮助。昨日，他们向蒋介石将军和冯玉祥将军发出电报，表示愿意前往南京聆听关于救国政策的指示，但截至昨晚尚未收到任何回复。

在返回上海之前，沈钧儒等六人将先赴南京一行。

据该七人家属向本报记者发表的声明称，该七人在恢复自由后将来上海短暂停留。他们将在国民政府的领导下继续从事救国工作。

S. I.
dR

C. O. C. L.
e
g. R. 1937年8月2日

Date August 1, 19 37.

Subject Release of National Salvation Leaders.

Made by D. I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.S.

The seven national salvation leaders, who have been under
detention at Soochow since November 23, 1936, on a charge of
being reactionaries, were released on bail at 3 p.m., July 31,
1937. They will proceed to Nanking on August 1, and are
expected to stay there for one week during which time they
are to receive special instructions from the Government.
At the end of that period, they will come to Shanghai.
It is learned that the local national salvation elements
have decided to prepare an elaborate welcome for the seven
released persons on their arrival in Shanghai.

has recently delivered by mail the following four kinds of
pamphlets to some 6,000 shops, schools, factories and private

Yat-sen and Liao Chung-kai and 14 others to the Kiangsu
High Court" demanding that the latter release Sung Chun-dz
and the six other national salvation leaders or as an
alternative to detain the appellants in gaol together with

sake of national salvation. (A translation of this
pamphlet is attached to Special Branch Report dated
July 8, 1937).

and others to the Kiangsu High Court in connection with
the case. They are requested to place their finger
prints on the forms and sent them to the Kiangsu High

westward along Route de Zikawei in the direction of the local

At 10.40 a.m. the three representatives returned
from the Tangpu, and the processionists, under the escort of
some thirty Chinese police, proceeded to the corner of Tan Poo
Road and Zia Tu Road, Nantao, where they held a meeting on a
piece of vacant ground. The crowd, at that time, numbered
about 1,000. During the meeting, Mr. Bang Vung-ying informed
the attendance that as it was Sunday there were no responsible
officers at the local Tangpu, but that the Police authorities
had promised to convey their appeal for the release of the
seven national salvation leaders to the Tangpu authorities at
the first suitable opportunity. Mr. Chang Ting-fu (張廷福),
one of the three representatives, then delivered a speech in
appreciation of the loyalty and enthusiasm shown by the crowd
and urging them to work hard for the national salvation movement
in future. The third speaker was Miss Chen Pu-er, who informed
the attendance that at the conclusion of the meeting, they
should return to their homes separately and not in groups. In
the meantime, some uneasiness was noticeable among the crowd,
who intimated that if the seven leaders were not released, they
would all proceed to Soochow to request the Kiangsu High Court
to place them in detention as well. Mr. Bang Vung-ying
eventually mollified the crowd who then sang songs entitled
"Kuomintang Song", "March of the Volunteer Armies" and "Fight
Back to Our Old Homes", and shouted slogans of a national
salvation nature. In compliance with the instructions of the
Chinese Police, the meeting concluded and the crowd dispersed
peaceably at 11.40 a.m.

seven leaders and urging the overthrow of the Japanese
imperialism were distributed among the attendance.

In front of the crowd, two Chinese youths held
a Chinese National Flag and a Party Flag while another
upheld a portrait of Dr. Sun Yat-sen.

By 3.30 p.m. June 13, some 300 persons had assembled,
when the meeting entitled the Shanghai Citizens' Mass
Meeting in Support of Sung's Case was inaugurated. Chang Chien
(张健), who presided, after leading the attendance in paying respect
to the national emblem and Dr. Sun's portrait, delivered a
short speech urging the "patriot" to ask the Government
to release the seven leaders of the National Salvation
Association.

(2) That relief be afforded to students of the North East University.

(5) That no secret diplomacy be indulged in.

On the termination of the meeting, some 100 of the attendance marched in a body northward along Rue du Marche, but were prevented from proceeding further by the French Police at Route Conty where the processionists turned eastward. On arriving at Zao Chaw Road, Chinese controlled territory, they turned northward, but before re-entering the French Concession, were dispersed by the Chinese Police in conjunction with the French Police.

June 14, 1937.

NIPRO

VARIOUS CIRCLES NATIONAL SALVATION ASSOCIATION
HOLDS DEMONSTRATION IN FRENCH CONCESSION

On June 12 the Kiangsu High
Court held the second hearing of the case against the seven
leaders of the national salvation movement.
The Shanghai Various Circles
National Salvation Association issued a notification to
various public bodies in Shanghai to the effect that at
3 p.m. June 13 a demonstration would be held on a piece of
vacant ground on Route de Zikawei, French Concession, to
demand the release of the seven arrested leaders. About
5000 students and labourers assembled at the appointed
time and held a demonstration under a presiding board of
five professors.
Acting on information, the French
Police dispatched a number of policemen to the scene to deal
with the situation.
The chairman of the demonstration
, during the course of his speech, said that the seven leaders
were reported to have been sentenced to 5 years' imprisonment,
He further said that if such patriots were to be condemned
all Chinese people would be condemned because of their love
of patriotic movements. For this reason, the people
should strongly demand the release of the seven leaders.
This speech was followed by a loud cry from the 5000
demonstrators that the Government should release the seven
leaders immediately.
The following resolutions were
passed:-
1. That the trial of the seven leaders be cancelled and
the prisoners released immediately.
2. That patriotic movements be protected.
3. That the freedom of speech and organization be protected.
4. That democratic administration be practised.
5. That all political prisoners be released.
6. That Japanese goods be boycotted and smuggling be
suppressed by armed force.
7. That the Government be supported and an anti-Japanese
front be formed immediately.
8. That the East Hopei Autonomous Government be cancelled
and the lost territory be recovered.
9. That China's entire population be armed and stirred up.
10. That the Government issue an order to the people to
organize national salvation associations.
11. That the Government should finance the North-East
University.
12. That diplomatic affairs be open to the public.
13. That all pro-Japanese government officers be dismissed.
The demonstration was dispersed at 5 p.m. due to the
rain and the efforts of the French Police.
A large number of inflammatory anti-Japanese handbills
were distributed among the demonstrators.
The handbill contains the following
slogans:-
1. The Government should unite with the people to resist
enemies and save the country.
2. Celebrate in advance the release of the seven leaders
and the release of political prisoners.
3. Arrest of patriots must be discontinued and patriotic
movements must not be interfered with.
4. Freedom and equality of the people must be practised and
national independence must be completed.
5. Hurrah for the freedom, equality and independence of
China!

1937年6月14日。

NIPRO

各界救国会
在法租界举行示威

6月12日，江苏高等法院对救国运动七位领袖的案件进行了第二次审讯。
上海各界救国联合会向上海各公共团体发出通知，称将于6月13日下午3时在法租界徐家汇路的一块空地上举行示威，要求释放被捕的七位领袖。约5000名学生和工人在指定时间聚集，并在由五位教授组成的主席团主持下举行了示威。
法国警察根据情报，派遣多名警员前往现场处理局势。
示威主席在演讲过程中称，据报道七位领袖已被判处五年监禁。他进一步表示，如果这样的爱国者都要被判罪，那么所有热爱爱国运动的中国人民都将获罪。因此，民众应强烈要求释放这七位领袖。
这番讲话之后，5000名示威者高声呼喊，要求政府立即释放七位领袖。
通过了以下决议：
1. 撤销对七位领袖的审判，并立即释放囚犯。
2. 保护爱国运动。
3. 保护言论和结社自由。
4. 实行民主行政。
5. 释放所有政治犯。
6. 抵制日货，并以武力镇压走私。
7. 支持政府，立即组成抗日阵线。
8. 取消冀东自治政府，收复失地。
9. 武装并动员全中国人口。
10. 政府下令民众组织救国会。
11. 政府应为东北大学提供资金。
12. 外交事务公开化。
13. 罢免所有亲日政府官员。
由于下雨以及法国警察的努力，示威于下午5时被驱散。
大量煽动性的反日传单在示威者中分发。
传单包含以下标语：
1. 政府应与人民团结抗敌救国。
2. 提前庆祝七位领袖及政治犯的释放。
3. 必须停止逮捕爱国者，不得干涉爱国运动。
4. 必须实行人民的自由与平等，并完成民族独立。
5. 中华民族的自由、平等与独立万岁！

As a manifestation of their support of the seven
leaders of the National Salvation Movement who are now
detained at the Soochow High Court, members of local national
salvation organizations are planning to stage a demonstration
this afternoon, June 13. Participants have been instructed
to assemble at 2.30 p.m. either at the Public Recreation
Ground, Dah Chih Road, Nantao, or on a piece of vacant ground
in the vicinity of the junction of Zikawei Road and Rue du
Marche, in Nantao. At 2.45 p.m. certain leaders of the
movement will lead the attendance in a march from this
rendezvous to a venue, which is being kept secret. It is
quite possible that on the way to the secret venue, the
participants will march in processional order and stage a
demonstration. The secret venue will be in Nantao.
The following slogans will be shouted :-
1. "Demand the release of the seven leaders."
2. "Release the patriotic political offenders."
3. "Demand freedom of speech, publication and assembly."
4. "Mobilize troops to support the people in Jehol and
Charhar in recovering the territory lost to China."
5. "Support the Government to resist Japan."
6. "Down with the pro-Japanese cliques and traitors."
7. "Down with Japanese Imperialism."
8. "Long live the emancipation of the Chinese Race."

Translation

A petition of Shanghai residents proceeding to the
Kiangsu High Court at Soochow in connection with
the case of Mr. Sung Chun-dz and others.

Mr. Sung Chun-dz and others were arrested in Shanghai
for participating in the activities of the national
salvation association. The whole country was surprised
at the arrest. After their arrest, they were charged
with plotting against the internal security of the State.
Recently information was received to the effect that the
case would be heard again and that they would be sentenced.
As the case is an important one, we wish to make the
following points and to submit a legitimate appeal :-
1) During the third Plenary Session of the C.E.C.of the
Kuomintang, the Government passed several resolutions
calling for the release of patriotic political offenders,
granting the freedom of speech and the press to the people,
etc. The sentencing of Mr. Sung Chun-dz and others will
lead to the wrecking of the solidarity of the nation.
2) On the side of the judicial circles - As there is no
evidence against Mr. Sung Chun-dz and others, they should
be released. According to law, the public prosecution of
Mr. Sung Chun-dz and others can be withdrawn for lack of
evidence.
3) On the side of national salvation - If Mr. Sung Chun-dz
and others are sentenced, people will be afraid of
engaging in the national salvation movement.
We, therefore, request your court to withdraw the prosecution
of Mr. Sung Chun-dz, et al and release them.

Petitioner
pages.zh:
译文

上海市民因沈钧儒等案赴苏州江苏高等法院请愿书。

沈钧儒等人因参与救国会活动在上海被捕。举国对此逮捕感到震惊。被捕后，他们被指控危害国家内部安全。近日获悉，该案将重新审理并作出判决。鉴于此案重大，我们谨提出以下几点，并提交合法上诉：-
1) 在国民党第三届中央执行委员会全体会议上，政府通过了若干决议，呼吁释放爱国政治犯，给予人民言论和出版自由等。对沈钧儒等人的判刑将导致国家团结的破裂。
2) 从司法界方面来看——由于没有针对沈钧儒等人的证据，他们应予释放。根据法律，因缺乏证据，可以撤回对沈钧儒等人的公诉。
3) 从救国方面来看——如果沈钧儒等人被判刑，人们将害怕从事救国运动。
因此，我们请求贵院撤回对沈钧儒等人的起诉，并予以释放。

请愿人

pages.en:
Translation

A letter to the people throughout the country issued by
the Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation Association
requesting the release of Mr. Sung Chun-dz and others
in order to achieve national solidarity against external
aggression.

Since September 18, 1931, the Japanese imperialists
have occupied the North-eastern provinces. They are now
contemplating annexing North China. Their object is to
conquer the whole of China.

The people of China who do not wish to be countryless
slaves instituted the national salvation movement. Patriotic
citizens of Shanghai organized the so-called "Shanghai Various
Circles National Salvation Association" with the ultimate
object of uniting various parties in the country in saving
the nation from foreign aggression.

The government, instead of supporting us, arrested Mr.
Sung Chun-dz and six others in November of last year, and
charged them with plotting against the State. The latest
information is to the effect that they would be sentenced
to five years' imprisonment each.

During the present period of foreign aggression, united
resistance is imperative, but the charging of patriotic people
by the government is inexplicable to the people.

Every body knows Mr. Sung Chungdz and others are leaders
of the national salvation movement. If they are charged
and sentenced, a wrong unprecedented in the history of China
will be done.

National salvation associations are organised by people
who do not wish to be conquered. If Mr. Sung Chun-ds and
others are charged and sentenced, all the people engaged
in patriotic movements will become offenders.
pages.zh:
译文

上海各界救国联合会为促成团结御侮致全国同胞书，请求释放沈钧儒等人。

自1931年9月18日以来，日本帝国主义者占领了东北各省。他们现在正图谋吞并华北。其目的是征服整个中国。

不愿做亡国奴的中国人民发起了救国运动。上海的爱国公民组织了所谓的“上海各界救国联合会”，其最终目标是联合国内各党派，拯救国家免受外来侵略。

政府非但不支持我们，反而于去年十一月逮捕了沈钧儒等六人，并指控他们危害国家。最新消息称，他们将被判处每人五年监禁。

在当前外敌侵略时期，联合抵抗势在必行，但政府指控爱国人士令民众难以理解。

众所周知，沈钧儒等人是救国运动的领袖。如果他们被起诉和判刑，将造成中国历史上前所未有的冤案。

救国会是由不愿被征服的人们组织的。如果沈钧儒等人被起诉和判刑，所有从事爱国运动的人都将成为罪犯。

pages.en:
-2-

The sentencing of Mr. Sung Chun-dz and others will
betray the government's promise to work together with
the people for the salvation of the nation.
The sentencing of Mr. Sung Chun-dz and others will
discourage the people against engaging themselves in
the national salvation movement.
We believe the government will, at the request of
the people, carry out its promises to maintain peace
in the country and to offer resistance to foreign
aggression. We also believe the government will remove
all obstacles in the way of national unification.
The following are our slogans :-
1) "Withdraw the public prosecution and release of national
salvation movement leaders!"
2) "Protect patriotic movements!"
3) "Protect the freedom of speech and the press, freedom
of assembly and organization!"
4) "Enforce the principles of democracy!"
5) "Boycott the Japanese goods and prevent smuggling by force
of arms!"
6) "Support the government in declaring war upon!"
7) "Eliminate the bogus East Hopei Autonomous Regime and
recover all the lost territory!"
8) "Let all the people be armed!"
9) "Down with Japanese imperialism!"
10) "Down with Chinese traitors!"
11) "Release political offenders!"
12)"Long live the emancipation of the Chinese Race!"

对沈钧儒等人的判刑将打击民众参与救国运动的积极性。
我们相信，政府应民众之请，将履行其维持国内和平及抵抗外来侵略的承诺。我们也相信，政府将消除国家统一道路上的一切障碍。

Subject. Attempted Convening of a meeting to Discuss measures to effect
the release of prominent members of local National Salvation
Associations Arrested by the Authorities on November 24.

Made by D.S. Lockwood Forwarded by (Signature)

With reference to the telephone message from Mr. Maung
Ta Jua, Police Bureau, Shanghai Municipality, to the effect that
a Mr. Chu Fu-cheng (諸輔成), Principal of the Law College,
French Concession, had invited guests to dinner in the Chun
Zoeu Club, 674 Weihaiwei Road, and requested that no political
discussions should be held during the performance, D.S.Lockwood
accompanied by D.I. Pan Lien-pih interviewed the Secretary of
the Chun Zoeu Club and learned that Mr. Chu had reserved a private
room for a dinner party. Consequently the Secretary was warned
against permitting the holding of political discussions on the
premises contrary to condition 4 of the Club Licence.

At 7 p.m. information was received from the accountant
that Mr. Chu had cancelled the reservation for dinner.

At 7.45 p.m. Kiang Wen-yui (江問漁), Chief of the
Chung Hwa Vocational Education Society, accompanied by Wong
Shen-ts (黃任之), Secretary of the Shanghai Citizens'
Association, and an unknown Chinese, arrived at the Club, when
they were informed that the dinner had been cancelled. The
three Chinese then went to the Koong Tuh Ling, No.4 Lane 42,
Park Road, and engaged Room No.32, when dinner was served. The
three Chinese left the premises at 8.45 p.m. No political
discussions were held.

F. D. Lockwood
D. S.

After the release of the four accused,
Li Kung-poh( 李 公 樸 ), Sung Chun-dz( 沈 鈞 儒 ),
Wong Hau-dz( 王 造 時 ) and So Chien Li( 沙 千 里 )
by the Court on November 23 on the security of their
lawyers, the Chief of the Public Safety Bureau made
written application to the Court for the re-arrest
of the accused. The Court issued warrants and the
four accused were re-arrested by the Municipal Police
acting at the request of the Public Safety Bureau
on the night November 23/24 on a charge of committing
acts with intent to endanger the Republic, "Wei Hai
Min Kuo"( 危 害 民 國 ). This refers to Article 100
of the Chinese Criminal Code.

They were taken before the Second Branch of
the Kiangsu High Court on the morning of November 24
and the Court after hearing the evidence and arguments
of counsel held that it had no jurisdiction in the
case of three of the accused who lived and were
arrested in Chinese territory (Extra-Settlement Roads)
and as to the fourth accused So Chien Li, the evidence
was held to be sufficient to warrant handing over to
the Chinese Authorities.

All four accused were therefore taken over
by the Chinese Authorities.
pages.zh:
在法院于11月23日基于四名被告律师提供的担保将其释放后，公安局局长向法院提交书面申请，要求重新逮捕上述被告。法院签发了逮捕令，四名被告于11月23日/24日夜间，应公安局之请求，被工部局警务处以“危害民国”（Wei Hai Min Kuo）的罪名重新逮捕。此罪名指《中华民国刑法》第一百条。

他们于11月24日上午被提解至江苏高等法院第二分院。法院在听取证据及辩护律师的陈词后裁定，对于其中三名居住并在华界（越界筑路区域）被捕的被告，法院无管辖权；至于第四名被告沙千里，法院认为证据充分，足以将其移交给中国当局。

因此，四名被告均被移交给中国当局。

Enquiries show that the "certain printing company in
Shanghai....." refers to the Eastern Publishing Company, 749
Bubbling Well Road, which is under the management of Max
Granich, the editor of "The Voice of China." According to
information received the China News Agency does not exist in
New York, such nomenclature having been used by the sender of
the cablegram in question in order to obtain reduced cable
transmission rates. The sender of the cable - a Chinese named
Dao - is reliably reported to have been well acquainted with
Granich in New York prior to the latter's departure for Shanghai.
In connection with the publication in the local press of
the contents of the cable and the answer sent by Granich, it
has been learned that Granich made his way to the American
Consulate-General and complained of the manner in which his
private affairs, in the shape of the cables, had been broadcast
in local newspapers, and accused the Chinese authorities of
interfering with his rights as an American citizen. Granich,
however, received no sympathy and no advice from the Consular
representative.
In regard to the contents of the cable it has been learn-
ed that in certain quarters Granich has intimated that on
several occasions Sung Chun-shih, Li Kung-pao, Miss Sze Liang
and other prominent members of the National Salvation Association
group have discussed the policy of "The Voice of China" with
him and have assisted him considerably in its production. A
number of these members have been guests at his home from time
to time, whilst he himself has also visited their residences at
various times.

经查，“上海某印刷公司……”系指位于静安寺路749号的东方出版公司（Eastern Publishing Company），该公司由《中国呼声》（The Voice of China）编辑 Max Granich 管理。据收到的情报，纽约并不存在所谓的“中国新闻社”，该发报人使用此名称是为了获得较低的电报传输费率。据悉，该电报发报人——一名姓 Dao 的华人——在 Granich 动身前往上海之前，曾在纽约与其熟识。
关于当地报纸刊登电报内容及 Granich 回复一事，获悉 Granich 曾前往美国总领事馆，投诉其私人事务（以电报形式）被当地报纸公开传播的方式，并指责中国当局干涉其作为美国公民的权利。然而，Granich 并未从领事代表那里得到任何同情或建议。
关于电报内容，获悉在某些圈子里，Granich 暗示沈钧儒、李公朴、史良小姐及其他全国救国会团体的知名成员曾多次与他讨论《中国呼声》的方针，并在其出版过程中给予了极大协助。这些成员中的一些人不时成为他家中的客人，而他自己也多次拜访过他们的住所。

arrest of a number of leaders of the National Salvation
Association movement on the night of November 22/23, 1936,
cannot be doubted since the Bureau of Public Safety is in
possession of information to the effect that Chang Ngui Hsi
(章乃器) (arrested in the French Concession during the early
hours of November 23, 1936) and a number of others connected
with the same movement, have secretly accepted the task of
working on behalf of the Communist Party, and are, or, rather
were occupying themselves as agitators in fomenting workers'
and students' movements, propagating reactionary doctrines,
grouping extremist elements and advocating subversive activities
in the guise of anti-Japanese propaganda.

With the arrest of certain of its prominent members, the
National Salvation Association group can be said to have
received a serious setback in its workings, but there is reason
to believe, according to reports emanating from the Public
Safety Bureau, that with the influence and assistance of the
Communist Party it is endeavouring to resuscitate its activities,
first by demanding the release of the arrested men, in an attempt
to retain its hold on the sympathies of those many bodies of
workers and students, who have previously received its doctrines
and views with open arms.

The fact that certain of Granich's friends and acquaintances
of short-standing are termed by the Bureau of Public Safety as
agents of the Communist Party, coupled with what is known of his
connections with Earl Browder and other reactionaries in the
United States, clearly indicate that his interests as editor
of "The Voice of China" are definitely political and not financial.

1936年11月22日/23日夜间逮捕多名全国救国会运动领导人一事，无疑引起了共产党的极大关注，因为公安局掌握的情报显示，章乃器（1936年11月23日凌晨在法租界被捕）及其他与该运动有关联的人员，已秘密接受为共产党工作的任务，并且正在（或更确切地说，曾经）充当煽动者，鼓动工运和学运，宣传反动学说，聚集极端分子，并借抗日宣传之名倡导颠覆活动。

随着部分知名成员的被捕，可以说全国救国会团体的运作遭受了严重挫折，但根据公安局发出的报告，有理由相信，在共产党的影响和协助下，该团体正试图恢复其活动，首先是要求释放被捕人员，试图以此维持其对那些曾欣然接受其学说和观点的广大工人和学生群体的影响力。

公安局将 Granich 的一些新朋友和熟人称为共产党代理人，加之已知他与美国的 Earl Browder 及其他反动分子有联系，这清楚地表明，他作为《中国呼声》编辑的利益绝对是政治性的，而非经济性的。

（批：28/12）

pages.en:
Communist Party Concerned Over Arrests

The Sing Sung News Agency ( 新聲社 )
reports that, according to information received, the
Communist Party is much concerned over the arrest of Mr. Sung
Chun Shih and others, because it is an undeniable fact that
these men have had co-operative dealings with the working
members of the Party.
The "China News Agency" ( 中國新聞社 ) in
New York, U.S.A., has close relations with a certain printing
company in Shanghai. This printing company is managed by
a foreigner named "Ma-Ke-Lai-Li" ( 馬格南利 ) who is connected
with the Communist Party and undertakes the printing of
reactionary literature. Following the arrest of Mr. Sung
Chun Shih and others, one Mr. Dao ( 陶 ) of the "China News
Agency" of New York sent a telegram to Mr. "Ma-Ke-Lai-Li"
requesting information regarding the cause of their arrest
and inquiring after their health, and advising him to
request people to speak in their favour. The reply given
by Mr. "Ma-Ke-Lai-Li" contains only four words: "Friends are
in distress".
pages.zh:
共产党关注逮捕事件

新声社（Sing Sung News Agency）报道说，据收到的消息，共产党对沈钧儒先生等人被捕一事极为关注，因为不可否认的事实是，这些人曾与党的工作人员有过合作往来。
位于美国纽约的“中国新闻社”（China News Agency）与上海某印刷公司关系密切。该印刷公司由一名名为“马格南利”（Ma-Ke-Lai-Li，即 Max Granich）的外国人管理，此人与共产党有联系，并承印反动刊物。沈钧儒先生等人被捕后，纽约“中国新闻社”的一位姓陶（Dao）先生向“马格南利”先生发送电报，询问他们被捕的原因并问候其健康状况，同时建议他请求人们为他们说话声援。“马格南利”先生的回复仅包含四个字：“朋友受难”。

Date. December 1, 1936.

REPORT

Subject. Arrest of Yao Sz Yen (姚士彥).

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang.

Enquiries have been made at the P.S.B. and other sources.
On November 26 Detectives from P.S.B. in cooperation with French Police raided house No. 21 Route Jupleix with a warrant for the arrest of one Tang Chien Sung (湯堅松) on a charge of being a Communist. The man was not at home. On enquiries made from the landlord, it was learned that a man named Yao Sz Yen, residing at No. 6 Mei Hwa Lee, was responsible for the lease. Yao was then arrested at the address given. No incriminating documents were found and no evidence was produced by the P.S.B.
It appears that Yao was a Government spy on the "patriotic movement" in the pay of Mr. Chang Chung Ming (張仲明), a special delegate of the Central Tangpu, and he was required to give evidence against Tsang Nai Chee, one of the leaders recently arrested in connection with the national salvation movement, but as he had refused to do so, the P.S.B. took out a warrant for his arrest. The case is still pending in the French Special District Court. It is doubtful whether the P.S.B. will be able to produce evidence of Yao being a Communist and establish a prima facie case against him. It is alleged by the P.S.B. that Yao was implicated in a statement made by an arrested Communist but this cannot be confirmed.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 7 DEC. 1936）
Superintendent.

D. C. (Special Branch).

（左侧批注：FILE / DIS / 1/2）
（左侧批注：JBR / 1/2）

主题：逮捕姚士彦 (Yao Sz Yen)。

制作及转发人：谭绍良警司。

已向公安局及其他来源进行查询。11月26日，公安局侦探会同法国巡捕房，持逮捕令搜查了巨泼来斯路（Route Jupleix）21号，旨在逮捕一名涉嫌为共产党的汤坚松 (Tang Chien Sung)。此人不在家。经向房东查询，得知住在梅花里6号的一名叫姚士彦的人负责租赁事宜。姚随后在上述地址被捕。未发现任何罪证文件，公安局也未提出任何证据。
看来姚曾是中央党部特派员张仲明 (Chang Chung Ming) 雇佣的监视“爱国运动”的政府线人，他被要求提供证据指控最近因全国救国运动案件被捕的领导人之一章乃器 (Tsang Nai Chee)，但因他拒绝这样做，公安局遂签发逮捕令将其逮捕。该案仍在法国特区法院审理中。公安局能否提出姚是共产党的证据并建立针对他的初步案件，尚存疑问。公安局声称姚卷入了一名被捕共产党人的供词中，但这无法证实。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 1936年12月7日）
警司。

D. C. (特务科)。

November 27, 1936.
Morning Translation.

Arrest of Mr. Yao Sz Yen
Mr. Yao Sz Yen (姚士彥), age 24, residing at
No. 6, Mei Hwa Li (美華里), Route Dupleix, French Concession,
is a member of the staff of the Bankers' Co-operation
Credit Service, Ltd, 133 Yuen Ming Yuen Road,
On the morning of November 26, officers of
the Public Safety Bureau, with the assistance of the
French Police, arrested Mr. Yao at his residence.
Mr. Yao was arraigned before the Third Branch
of the Kiangsu High Court at 2 p.m. yesterday. Mr. Yuen
Chia Wang (袁家汪), the Municipal Advocate, stated that
the man had been arrested at the request of the Public
Safety Bureau and requested the Court to remand the case
for four days to permit of further investigations.
At this stage, the Judge cleared the Court
of spectators. The case was subsequently remanded to
November 30. The accused is being detained in custody.

pages.en:
Translation

Manifesto of the Illegally Arrested Sung Chun Dz and
Six Others Support Committee

Brethren throughout the country; we wish to tell you
one tragic incident as follows :-

When the Japanese imperialists are using gas and bombs
to invade our Suiyuan province and the nation is on the verge of
destruction, and the people are about to become slaves, the
Chinese Government, instead of fighting against the Japanese, took
into custody seven leaders of the national salvation associations
on the evening of November 23.

The government authorities declare that the people should
not meddle in politics and that if they do, they will be regarded
as reactionary elements or communists.

Brethren, is the attitude of the government right? Are
Sung Chun Dz, Wong Shao Dz, Soo Chi Li, and Sze Liang, who are
lawyers, Li Kung Poh, who is the principal of the Liang Zai
Supplementary School, Tsang Nai Chi, who is a famous banker, and
Chen Tao Feng, who is a noted writer, bandits or communists?

The attitude adopted by these people, which is the
attitude of the national salvation associations towards national
salvation is that since the fate of China is in the balance and
the country is about to be conquered by the Japanese imperialists,
the Chinese people, irrespective of officials or civilians, rich men
or poor, and party affiliations, who do not wish to become running
dogs of the Japanese, must unite and oppose Japan and the Chinese
traitors. Since the foundation of the national salvation
associations, their activities and those of the seven arrested
persons are open to the people of the country.

Brethren, is the attitude of the arrested persons and the
national salvation associations wrong? Must not the Chinese people
save their own country? Must the Chinese people be the running
dogs of the Japanese? Must the Chinese people slaughter
themselves?

If the attitude taken by the arrested persons is right,
why have the government authorities arrested them? Is it that the
people who wish to save their country are communists?

Brethren, China belongs to the people, every one who has
a right to save his nation. We want to save the country and we
resolutely demand that the government release the seven arrested
and assure us of the freedom of conducting the national salvation
movement.

Brethren, we wish to make known the arrest of the seven
leaders as far as possible in order that the people may render
them assistance and save the nation.

November 24.
pages.zh:
译文

沈钧儒等七人非法被捕后援会宣言

全国同胞们；我们要告诉你们一件悲惨的事，如下：

当日本帝国主义者使用毒气和炸弹入侵我国绥远省，国家处于灭亡边缘，人民即将沦为奴隶之时，中国政府不但不抗击日本，反而于11月23日晚拘捕了七位救国会领袖。

政府当局宣称，民众不应干涉政治，若干涉，将被视为反动分子或共产党人。

同胞们，政府的态度正确吗？律师沈钧儒（Sung Chun Dz）、王造时（Wong Shao Dz）、史良（Soo Chi Li）和沙千里（Sze Liang），良友补习学校校长李公朴（Li Kung Poh），著名银行家章乃器（Tsang Nai Chi），以及著名作家邹韬奋（Chen Tao Feng），是匪徒还是共产党人？

这些人所采取的态度，即救国会对救国的态度是：既然中国的命运危在旦夕，国家即将被日本帝国主义者征服，那么不愿成为日本走狗的中国人民，无论官民、贫富及党派归属，都必须团结起来反对日本和中国汉奸。自救国会成立以来，其活动及上述七位被捕人士的活动均对全国民众公开。

同胞们，被捕人士和救国会的态度错了吗？中国人民难道不应该拯救自己的国家吗？中国人民必须成为日本的走狗吗？中国人民必须自相残杀吗？

如果被捕人士的态度是正确的，政府当局为何逮捕他们？难道希望救国的人就是共产党吗？

同胞们，中国属于人民，每个人都有权拯救自己的国家。我们要救国，我们坚决要求政府释放七名被捕者，并保证我们开展救国运动的自由。

同胞们，我们希望尽可能广泛地公布这七位领袖被捕的消息，以便民众给予他们援助，拯救国家。

11月24日。

pages.en:
沈鈞儒等七人非法被捕後援會宣言

全國同胞們：
我們要告訴你一件痛心的事變：
當日本帝國主義正在用毒氣炸彈攻打我們的遠省的時候，國家快要亡了，我們大
家都快要做亡國奴的時候，我們的政府當局，不去和日本帝國主義打仗，反而，在廿三
日的半夜，把救國會的七位領袖捉去了。
政府當局說：國事不准他們管，他們救國，就是反動份子，是共產黨。
同胞們，這些話對嗎？做律師的沈鈞儒，王造時，沙千里，史良；和量才補習學校
校長李公樸，有名的銀行家章乃器，有名的著作家鄒韜奮，這些人，請問你，會做土匪
共產黨嗎？
他們平日所主張的，（也就是救國會所主張的）是：中國已經到了最危險的時候，
快要給日本帝國主義滅亡了。中國人民，不管是大官員和小百姓，不管是有錢的和窮光
蛋，不管那一黨那一派，只要不願意作東洋人的奴狗，都要聯合起來反抗東洋人和賣國
賊。自從救國會成立以來，救國會的言論行動和這七位的言論行動，很明白的擺在全國
人民的面前：完全是根據上面的主張的。
同胞們！他們的主張錯了嗎？中國人不應該救中國嗎？中國人應該做東洋人的奴狗
嗎？中國人應該自己人殺自己人嗎？
如果他們的主張是對的，那麼，政府當局捉他們去，是什麼理由呢？說救國就是共
產黨嗎？
同胞們！中國是大家的，誰都可以救國，救國是絕對自由的。我們為了要救國家，
我們堅決的要求政府馬上釋放這七位領袖！保證以後救國
運動的自由！
同胞們！我們要把這個事變，廣汎的傳播，大家起來援助我們的領袖，挽救
我們的國家！
十一月二十四日

REPORT
Date November 25, 1936.

Subject Attempted Convening of a Meeting to Discuss Measures to effect
the release of prominent members of local National Salvation
Associations Arrested by the Authorities on November 24

Made by D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by (签名)

Chu Wei-seng (褚慧僧 ) alias Chu Fu-chen
( 褚輔成 ), Chairman of the Chekiang Provincial
Association, 13 Lien Tsz Li, Avenue Road (Sinza District),
and his colleagues attempted to convene a meeting of
representatives of local public bodies including national
salvation associations at 6 p.m. November 24 in the Kung
Teh Ling Restaurant, Lane 41, No.4 Park Road, but the
meeting was not held owing to its prohibition by the
Municipal Police at the request of the Bureau of Public
Safety.

The ostensible object of the meeting was to
entertain to dinner Dr. Tsai Yuen-pei ( 蔡元培 ),
President of the Academia Sinica, 37B Brenan Road, and a
member of the Supervisory Committee of the Central Kuomintang
at Nanking, but the real object of the meeting was to
discuss ways and means to secure the release of the seven
prominent members of local national salvation associations
who were taken into custody on November 24 by the Chinese
Authorities.

Dr. Tsai Yuen-pei was not present in the restaurant
owing to other engagements. Chu Fu-chen, Koo Tseh-cheng
( 顧執中 ), a journalist of the Sin Wan Pao, and two
unknown Chinese appeared at the restaurant, but left
hurriedly owing to the presence of several members of the
Bureau of Public Safety in plain clothes, who kept unofficial
observation in the restaurant pending the arrival of the
Municipal Police.

The following fourteen persons were present at the
restaurant for the purpose of attending the meeting :-

SINZA Station,
REPORT
Date. 24th Nov., 1936.
Subject Report on meeting held at Yung Tuh Ling (永德林) Restaurant,
4/41 Park Road.
Made by D.I. Boddy. Forwarded by.

Sir,
At 5.10 p.m. 24/11/36, C.I. Bishop received information from
Major Bourne, I.C. i/c Special Branch that a meeting was being
held at 6 p.m. 24/11/36 at the Yung Tuh Ling Restaurant, Park
Road, and that police were to attend meeting.
C.I. Bishop, S.I. Duncan, C.D.S. 196, 272, D.I. Mau I Vung,
and the undersigned proceeded to the restaurant at 4 Lane 41
Park Road and ascertained that one named Wong (王) had
telephoned the restaurant asking for 2 large rooms stating he
desired to use them from 6 p.m. Tea boy No. 8 Soong Sung Yue
(宋松裕) of the restaurant took the message and could only state
person who telephoned gave his name as Wong (王).
The undersigned placed C.D.S. 196 and C.D.S. 272 on duty at
the restaurant they remaining with D.S.I. Lees, F.S. Pitts and
D.S.I. Shih and 3 members of the P.S.B. who were present.
Having ascertained Room 18 had been engaged they kept
observation from ground floor room.
18 persons in all entered the room, 4 leaving directly after
they entered, at about 6.30 p.m.
As it was suspected meeting was being held D.O. "A" Div.
who had been waiting at Sinza Station re the meeting was informed
and he gave instruction that as Special Branch did not wish
meeting to be held that party in the room be informed re political
meetings being held in restaurant and be dispersed.
The 14 persons in the room, 10 male and 4 females:-
1. Liu Veng Lai (劉文蘭),
2. Tsang Kung Hai (張公海),
3. Loh Dzu (陸祖),
4. Wan Yih Fung (萬逸奉),

事由：关于在派克路4/41号永德林（Yung Tuh Ling）餐厅举行的会议的报告。
制作：督察 Boddy。 转呈：。

先生，
1936年11月24日下午5时10分，毕晓普探长（C.I. Bishop）从特务科主任伯恩少校（Major Bourne）处获悉，将于1936年11月24日下午6时在派克路永德林餐厅举行会议，警方需出席该会议。
毕晓普探长、邓肯高级督察（S.I. Duncan）、刑事侦缉警员196号和272号、毛一雄督察（D.I. Mau I Vung）以及本人前往派克路41弄4号的餐厅，经查实，一名姓王（Wong）的人致电餐厅预订两个大房间，称希望从下午6点开始使用。餐厅8号茶役宋松裕（Soong Sung Yue）接听了电话，仅能说明打电话的人自称姓王（Wong）。
本人安排刑事侦缉警员196号和272号在餐厅执勤，他们与利斯副督察（D.S.I. Lees）、皮茨高级警司（F.S. Pitts）、施副督察（D.S.I. Shih）以及在场的3名公共安全局人员在一起。
在查明18号房间已被预订后，他们从底层房间进行监视。
共有18人进入房间，其中4人在进入后随即离开，时间约为下午6时30分。
由于怀疑正在举行会议，已通知一直在新闸警署等候处理该会议的“A”分区值班警官，他指示鉴于特务科不希望举行该会议，应告知房间内的人员不得在餐厅举行政治性集会，并将其驱散。
房间内的14人，10男4女：
1. 刘文兰（Liu Veng Lai），
2. 张公海（Tsang Kung Hai），
3. 陆祖（Loh Dzu），
4. 万逸奉（Wan Yih Fung），

During the early hours of the morning of November 23,
the Municipal Police, rendered assistance to the Shanghai
Bureau of Public Safety in affecting the arrest in the
Settlement of the following four prominent members of the
National Salvation Association on the authority of
instructions of the National Government :-

| Name and Address | Profession | Political Activities |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

Translation of French Police Report dated November 23, 1936

Arrest at the request of the Chinese Authorities of three
directors of the National Salvation Federation of Various Circles.

At 9 p.m. on November 22, Dr HUNG CHI (洪起)? Chief of the
2nd Branch of the Public Safety Bureau advised us by telephone
that the Mayor of Shanghai had received orders from Nanking to
arrest the directors of the clandestine anti-Japanese Association
known as "The Federation of the various circles for National
Salvation" (上海各界救国联合会). At the same time he requested our
assistance in effecting certain of these arrests in the French
Concession.

At about 11 p.m. he delivered to us official letter "Te" 298,
a translation of which is attached herewith.

By this letter and the list attached, the Chinese Authorities
requested us to effect the arrest with a view to subsequent
extradition of the persons named hereafter :

Mr TSANG NAI CHI (章乃器), Shi Wei Chun, Route Delastre,
formerly one of the directors of the Chekiang Industrial Bank,

circles group "United Front of Left Wing Revolutionaries
(左派人民革命联合阵线), organised with the object of confronting the

cortege which crossed the International Settlement in order to
visit the tomb of the unknown heroes (1510/1). Member of the
Administrative Council of the Chinese Physical Culture Association,
No.92 Rue Hue, organised with the object of favouring in China the

1936年11月23日法国巡捕房报告译文

应中国当局要求逮捕各界救国联合会三位董事。

11月22日晚9时，公安局第二分局局长洪起（HUNG CHI）博士电话通知我们，上海市长已收到南京方面的命令，逮捕名为“上海各界救国联合会”的秘密反日协会的董事。同时，他请求我们协助在法租界内执行部分逮捕行动。

约晚11时，他向我们递交了官方信函“特”字第298号，译文附后。

通过此信及所附名单，中国当局请求我们逮捕下列人员，以便随后进行引渡：

章乃器 (TSANG NAI CHI) 先生，住德拉司脱路施维春宅，前浙江实业银行董事之一，该银行位于汉口路150号。上海各界救国联合会发起人。左派人民革命联合阵线知识分子团体负责人，该组织旨在联合国民党各党派（除新国民党、国家主义派、共产党、生产党、社会民主党等外）对抗日本威胁（报告 2541/R）。参与了1936年5月30日的示威游行。是该次示威游行的主席团成员之一（1133/B）。主持了1936年1月28日在总商会举行的纪念1932年中日事变周年会议，并率领队伍穿过国际租界前往凭吊无名英雄墓（1510/1）。中华体育会理事会成员，该会位于霞飞路92号，旨在促进中国体育运动的发展，尤其是

pages.en:
(2)

practise of sports, and more especially, Chinese boxing (Report
593/1). Member of the Administrative Council of "The Bankers'
Cooperative Credit Service Ltd.", 133 Yuen King Yuen Road (Report
584/1). Member of the Neo-Kuomintang Party (Report 1159/S).

Miss SZE LIANG (史良), No.1 Lafayette Terrace, advocate,
Chief of the Women's Section of the "United Front of Left wing
Revolutionaries. Editor of the clandestine publication "Journal
of National Salvation (Report 114/3). Took part in the May 30, 1936
demonstration. Was one of the members of the Presidium of this
demonstration (vide Report 1133/S). President of the Feminine
Association of Shanghai for National Salvation (pro-communist
organisation) (Report No.1007/S), the correspondence office of
which was installed at No.55 Yuen King Yuen Road (Cf. Report 1589/1).
Presided over the meeting held on March 8, 1936, international
day of women at the Y.M.C.A., No.599 Szechuen Road. At the issue
of this meeting certain communist elements suggested that a
demonstration be held in the streets. This proposal was approved
and the demonstrators left Szechuen Road and went to Nantao via
Rue Tourane ( The Reserve Unit of the French Police had to intervene
and during the struggle which ensued two persons were injured -
Report 1589/1). Pleaded especially on behalf of communists who
were being prosecuted (Report 1485/1. Presided over the meeting
held on January 28, 1936 at the Chamber of Commerce in commemoration
of the 1932 Sino-Japanese incidents and headed the cortège which
traversed the International Settlement in order to visit the tomb
of the unknown heroes (Report 1510/1). Was a member of the Society
for the defense of the citizens against foreign invasion, organized
in the beginning of February 1933, the secret office of which was
located in the French Concession; first at No.48 Route Vallon and
later at No.6, Passage 68 of the same street (Cf. Report 83/R).

Mr CHOW TAO FENG alias CHOW HENKING (鄒韜奮 鄒恩潤 ),
No.4, Passage 601 Rue Lafayette. Graduate of St John's University,
pages.zh:
(2)

中国拳击（报告 593/1）。“银行家合作信用服务有限公司”理事会成员，地址为袁金园路133号（报告 584/1）。新国民党党员（报告 1159/S）。

史良 (SZE LIANG) 小姐，住拉斐特台1号，律师，“左派人民革命联合阵线”妇女部主任。秘密刊物《救国日报》编辑（报告 114/3）。参与了1936年5月30日的示威游行。是该次示威游行的主席团成员之一（见报告 1133/S）。上海妇女救国会（亲共组织）主席（报告号 1007/S），其通讯处设在袁金园路55号（参见报告 1589/1）。主持了1936年3月8日在国际妇女节于四川路59号青年会举行的会议。会议结束时，某些共产主义分子建议在街头举行示威。该提议获得批准，示威者离开四川路，经都乐路前往南市（法国巡捕房后备队不得不介入，随后的冲突中有两人受伤 - 报告 1589/1）。特别为受起诉的共产党员辩护（报告 1485/1）。主持了1936年1月28日在总商会举行的纪念1932年中日事变会议，并率领队伍穿过国际租界前往凭吊无名英雄墓（报告 1510/1）。曾是1933年2月初成立的“公民御侮自救会”成员，该会秘密办事处位于法租界；最初在华伦路48号，后迁至同街68弄6号（参见报告 83/R）。

邹韬奋 (CHOW TAO FENG)，又名邹恩润 (CHOW HENKING) (鄒韜奮 鄒恩潤 )，住拉斐特路601弄4号。圣约翰大学毕业生，

pages.en:
(3)
ex-Director of the Sen-Huo book-store (Life) (生活書店), ex-editor
of the old revues Sen-Huo (Life) (生活週刊), Ta Chung Seng Huo
(Popular Life) (大衆生活), Eternal Life (永生週刊) and founder
of the journal Sen Huo Jhih Pao (生活日報), published in Hongkong
which has stopped publication. Editor and publisher of the weekly
edition SEN HUO, the office of which is at Office 319 in the
"Shanghai Times" building, 160 Avenue Edward VII. Was one of the
founder members of the Chinese Society of the Rights of Man
League, an association dissolved in 1933 by order of the Chinese
authorities. Now a member of the Nationalist Party (Kuo Chia Chu
I Pai) (國民黨左派), directed by General FENG YU HSIANG and
General LI LIEH CHUN, which is at the head of the anti-Japanese
movement. In 1935 CHOW founded the revue "Life". Following the
Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1932, this revue having taken on a
purely anti-Chiang Kai Shek character, the Generalissimo
ordered the local authorities to ban sale of it. When Mr CHOW
heard of this order he found it preferable to go on a voyage to
Europe and entrusted the management of his revue to HSU PAH CHING
(徐伯昕). As the revue continued to publish numerous articles
against the National Government, a search was carried out at the
office of the publication at the request of the Chinese authorities
on December 11, 1933. Following this raid the director decided to
suspend publication of "Life". After a long sojourn in Europe,
chiefly in the U.S.S.R., Mr CHOW returned to Shanghai in the
Spring of 1935 and founded with the support of General LI LIEH
CHUN his revue "Popular Life" (大衆生活), a revue which, beyond
doubt, is the propaganda organ of the anti-Japanese faction of
the Kuomintang Party (Cf Report 1512/1).

The required arrests were carried out between 2 and 3 a.m.
at the homes of the accused.

At the home of CHOW TAO FENG (韜奮) some thirty brochures
and circulars without much interest were found. Some of the
foreign
brochures in foreign languages are the work of known communists.

At the home of TSANG HAI CHI (章乃器) were seized 4,000
pamphlets in favour of the strikers of Japanese mills and
pages.zh:

前生活书店主任，前《生活周刊》、《大众生活》、《永生周刊》等旧刊编辑，《生活日报》创始人，该报在香港出版，现已停刊。《生活》周刊编辑及出版人，办事处位于爱德华七世路160号“上海泰晤士报”大楼319室。曾是人权保障同盟中国分会的创始成员之一，该协会于1933年奉中国当局命令解散。现为国民党左派（Kuo Chia Chu I Pai）(國民黨左派) 成员，该派系由冯玉祥将军和李烈钧将军领导，处于反日运动的前沿。1935年，邹创办了《生活》杂志。继1932年中日敌对行动之后，该杂志呈现出纯粹的反蒋介石性质，委员长下令地方当局禁止销售。邹先生得知此令后，认为最好前往欧洲旅行，并将杂志管理事务委托给徐伯昕 (HSU PAH CHING)。由于该杂志继续刊登大量反对国民政府的文章，应中国当局要求，于1933年12月11日对该出版机构办公室进行了搜查。此次突袭后，主编决定暂停《生活》的出版。在欧洲长期逗留，主要是在苏联，邹先生于1935年春返回上海，并在李烈钧将军的支持下创办了《大众生活》杂志，该杂志无疑是国民党反日派的宣传机关（参见报告 1512/1）。

所需的逮捕行动于凌晨2时至3时在被告住所执行。

在邹韬奋 (韜奮) 家中，发现了约三十本小册子和传单，价值不大。部分外文小册子系已知共产党员的作品。

在章乃器 (章乃器) 家中，查获了4000份支持日商纱厂罢工工人的宣传册，以及

44 books of tickets with counterfoils, each containing 50 tickets,
for subscriptions on behalf of the strikers, 6 copies of Bulletin

At Mis SZE LIANG's place some regulations appertaining to

On being interrogated by the Political Branch the three
prisoners denied the accusation of communist activities, but admitted

In the International Settlement, at the same time and under
the same circumstances, the following persons belonging to the
same organisation were arrested :
Mr LI KUNG PO (李公樸)/ Director of the Liang Zai School
(量才補習学校) in Nanking Road, Continental Emporium, Nanking; director
of the SHUN PAO Library; editor of the revue "The life of Students";
member of the administrative committee of the Shanghai section
for Sino-Soviet cultural cooperation, the office of which is at
the University of Communications, Avenue Haig. Member of the left
wing of the United Revolutionaries. Has participated in various
anti-Japanese and anti-government demonstrations.
Mr SHA CHUAN LI (沙千里), a lawyer with offices at 429 Kiukiang
Road. Editor of the bi-monthly revue Seng Fu Tse Se (生活知識)
(Shengroxhsh), No.3 Passage 512 Chengtu Rd; not very well known.
Mr WANG CHAO JU (王造時), advocate, one of the promoters
of the Association of various circles of Shanghai for National
Salvation. Member of the Party Neo-Kuomintang. Member of the
educational association of the Shanghai district (organisation
with social democratic tendencies); member of the Chinese Social
Democratic Party. Professor at the Kwang Hua University in Great
Western Road. Very active member of the League for the defense of
Civic Rights - President TSAI YUAN PEI (蔡元培). Took part in the
manifestation of May 30, 1936 and that of January 28, 1936.

由援助罢工工人委员会发起的捐款收据，44本带存根的票簿，每本含50张为罢工工人捐款的票据，6份《学界救国联合会》第1号情报简报。
在史良小姐处，查获了一些关于“援军抗敌委员会”的规章以及一些无价值的文件。
经政治处审讯，三名囚犯否认从事共产主义活动的指控，但承认从事反日活动。

李公樸 (LI KUNG PO) 先生 / 南京路大陆商场量才补习学校主任；申报图书馆主任；《学生生活》杂志编辑；中苏文化合作协会上海分会行政委员会委员，办事处位于海格路交通大学。左派联合革命者成员。曾参与各种反日和反政府示威游行。
沙千里 (SHA CHUAN LI) 先生，律师，事务所在九江路429号。双月刊《生活知识》(Seng Fu Tse Se) (Shengroxhsh) 编辑，成都路512弄3号；知名度不高。
王造時 (WANG CHAO JU) 先生，律师，上海各界救国联合会发起人之一。新国民党党员。上海区教育协会会员（具有社会民主倾向的组织）；中国社会民主党党员。大西路光华大学教授。民权保障同盟活跃成员 - 主席蔡元培 (TSAI YUAN PEI)。参加了1936年5月30日和1936年1月28日的示威游行。

pages.en:
Official letter from the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau, Character
"Te", No.298, dated 19/11/36
--------------------------

The Police Force of the French
Concession of Shanghai.

I have the honour to inform you confidenti-
ally that according to information received by us, one TCHANG NGAI
HSI ( 张 乃 器 ) and two others, who have secretly accepted to work
on behalf of the Communist Party, are occupied in fomenting within
the territory of the Municipality (Chinese) of Shanghai all kinds
of workers and students movements in order to hinder the public
peace, and with the object of creating disorders the consequences
of which are likely to be serious and of committing acts of
violence etc...

We send you herewith a list of the names
of these individuals, TCHANG NGAI HSI and consorts, known as
professional agitators occupied in grouping extremist elements,
in propagating communist doctrines, and in fomenting insurrect-
ionary conspiracies. At present they are pursuing their subversive
activities and unless they are immediately placed in a position
where they can do no harm, no one knows what may be the consequences
of their agitation.

In consequence, the bearer will hand over to
you the present letter and attached list, and I beg that you
to
will accord us the necessary assistance to enable the arrests to
be proceeded with and the subsequent extradition of the accused
effected.

(signed) TSAI CHING CHUN
Head of the Public Safety Bureau
pages.zh:
上海市公安局公函，特字第298号，日期1936年11月19日
--------------------------

致上海法租界巡捕房。

本人谨此密告，据我方获得之情报，张乃器（TCHANG NGAI HSI）及另外两人已秘密接受为共产党工作，正在上海华界境内煽动各类工人与学生运动，以扰乱公共安宁，其目的在于制造后果可能极为严重的骚乱，并实施暴力行为等……

现随函附上张乃器及其同伙的名单，这些人被称为职业煽动者，从事集结极端分子、宣传共产主义学说以及煽动叛乱阴谋的活动。目前他们仍在进行颠覆活动，若不立即将其置于无法造成危害的境地，无人能知其煽动之后果如何。

因此，持信人将向贵方递交本函及所附名单，恳请贵方给予必要协助，以便进行逮捕并随后引渡被告。

（签名）蔡劲军
公安局局长

of National Salvation (Report 114/3). Took part in the May 30, 1936
demonstration. Was one of the members of the Presidium of this
demonstration (vide Report 1133/S). President of the Feminine
Association of Shanghai for National Salvation (pro-communist
organisation) (Report No.1007/S), the correspondence office of
which was installed at No.55 Yuen Ming Yuen Road (Cf. Report 1589/1).
Presided over the meeting held on March 8, 1936, international
day of women at the Y.M.C.A., No.599 Szechuen Road. At the issue
of this meeting certain communist elements suggested that a
demonstration be held in the streets. This proposal was approved
and the demonstrators left Szechuen Road and went to Nantao via
Rue Tourane ( The Reserve Unit of the French Police had to intervene
and during the struggle which ensued two persons were injured -
Report 1589/1). Plead ed especially on behalf of communists who
were being prosecuted (Report 1485/1. Presided over the meeting
held on January 28, 1936 at the Chamber of Commerce in commemoration
of the 1932 Sino-Japanese incidents and headed the cortege which
traversed the International Settlement in order to visit the tomb
of the unknown heroes (Report 1510/1). Was a member of the Society
for the defense of the citizens against foreign invasion, organized
in the beginning of February 1933, the secret office of which was
located in the French Concession; first at No.48 Route Vallon and
later at No.6, Passage 68 of the same street (Cf. Report 85/A).

No.4, Passage 601 Rue Lafayette. Graduate of St John's University,

史良（SZE LIANG）小姐，住拉斐特公寓1号，律师，左派人民革命联合阵线妇女部负责人。秘密刊物《救国日报》编辑（报告114/3）。参加了1936年5月30日的示威游行。是该次示威主席团成员之一（见报告1133/S）。上海妇女救国会（亲共组织）主席（报告编号1007/S），其通讯处设于圆明园路55号（参见报告1589/1）。主持了1936年3月8日国际妇女节在四川路599号青年会举行的会议。会议结束时，某些共产党分子建议在街头举行示威。该提议获准，示威者离开四川路，经都郎路（Rue Tourane）前往南市（法国警察后备队不得不介入，随后的冲突中有两人受伤——报告1589/1）。特别为受起诉的共产党人辩护（报告1485/1）。主持了1936年1月28日在商会举行的纪念1932年中日事变会议，并率领队伍穿过公共租界前往凭吊无名英雄墓（报告1510/1）。曾是1933年2月初成立的“公民御侮会”成员，该会秘密办事处位于法租界，先是在华伦路（Route Vallon）48号，后在该路68弄6号（参见报告85/A）。

邹韬奋（CHOW TAO FENG），又名邹恩润（CHOW HSIENSHENG），住拉斐特路601弄4号。圣约翰大学毕业生，

pages.en:

of the old revues Sen-Huo (Life) (生活週刊), Ta Chun Seng Huo
(Popular Life) 大眾生活, Eternal Life 永生週刊 and founder
of the journal Sen Huo Jhih Pao (生活日報), published in Hongkong
which has stopped publication. Editor and publisher of the weekly
edition SEN HUO, the office of which is at Office 319 in the
"Shanghai Times building, 160 Avenue Edward VII. Was one of the
founder members of the Chinese Society of the Rights of Man
League, an association dissolved in 1933 by order of the Chinese
authorities. Now a member of the Nationalist Party (Kuo Chia Chu
I Pai) (國家主義派), directed by General FENG YU HSIANG and
General LI LIEH CHUN, which is at the head of the anti-Japanese
movement. In 1935 CHOW founded the revue "Life". Following the
Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1932, this revue having taken on a
purely anti-Chiang Kai Shek character, the Generalissimo
ordered the local authorities to ban sale of it. When Mr CHOW
heard of this order he found it preferable to go on a voyage to
Europe and entrusted the management of his revue to HSU PO CHING
(徐伯昕). As the revue continued to publish numerous articles
against the National Government, a search was carried out at the
office of the publication at the request of the Chinese authorities
on December 11, 1933. Following this raid the director decided to
suspend publication of "Life". After a long sojourn in Europe,
chiefly in the U.S.S.R., Mr CHOW returned to Shanghai in the
Spring of 1935 and founded with the support of General LI LIEH
CHUN his revue "Popular Life" 大眾生活, a revue which, beyond
doubt, is the propaganda organ of the anti-Japanese faction of
the Kuomintang Party (Cf Report 1512/1).

Official letter from the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau, Character
"Te", No.298, dated 19/11/36
--------------------------

The Police Force of the French
Concession of Shanghai.

I have the honour to inform you confidenti-
ally that according to information received by us, one TCHANG NGAI
HSI (张乃玺) and two others, who have secretly accepted to work
on behalf of the Communist Party, are occupied in fomenting within
the territory of the Municipality (Chinese) of Shanghai all kinds
of workers and students movements in order to hinder the public
peace, and with the object of creating disorders the consequences
of which are likely to be serious and of committing acts of
violence etc...

We send you herewith a list of the names
of these individuals, TCHANG NGAI HSI and consorts, known as
professional agitators occupied in grouping extremist elements,
in propagating communist doctrines, and in fomenting insurrect-
ionary conspiracies. At present they are pursuing their subversive
activities and unless they are immediately placed in a position
where they can do no harm, no one knows what may be the consequences
of their agitation.

In consequence, the bearer will hand over to
you the present letter and attached list, and I beg that you
will accord us the necessary assistance to enable the arrests to
be proceeded with and the subsequent extradition of the accused
effected.

(signed) TSAI CHING CHUN
Head of the Public Safety Bureau

上海市公安局公函，特字第298号，日期1936年11月19日
--------------------------

致上海法租界巡捕房。

本人谨此密告，据我方获得之情报，张乃玺（TCHANG NGAI HSI）及另外两人已秘密接受为共产党工作，正在上海华界境内煽动各类工人与学生运动，以扰乱公共安宁，其目的在于制造后果可能极为严重的骚乱，并实施暴力行为等……

现随函附上张乃玺及其同伙的名单，这些人被称为职业煽动者，从事集结极端分子、宣传共产主义学说以及煽动叛乱阴谋的活动。目前他们仍在进行颠覆活动，若不立即将其置于无法造成危害的境地，无人能知其煽动之后果如何。

因此，持信人将向贵方递交本函及所附名单，恳请贵方给予必要协助，以便进行逮捕并随后引渡被告。

（签名）蔡劲军
公安局局长

Memo No. 24/36.

The attached list contains the names of certain leaders

Branch.

If the Public Safety Bureau should ask for assistance
in arresting them to-night, or on a future occasion, assistance

before a Special Court when the case will be heard in camera.

be informed of any arrests made.

3.

ASSISTANCE TO CHINESE AUTHORITIES.

The two accused Sung Chun Zu (沈鈞儒) and
Wong Zau Zu (王造時) appeared before the Kiangsu
High Court at 2 p.m. 24/11/36.

As the Court opened Li Kung Pao (李公樸)
the third person mentioned in Warrant No. 699 surrendered
in Court.

After the hearing of the case the following
decision was given:-

" The three accused named Li Kung Pao, Sung Chun
Zu and Wong Zau Zu were not apprehended within the
boundary of the Shanghai International Settlement so the
question of extradition does not arise. S.P.S. Bureau
to negotiate with the Municipal Council of the
International Settlement regarding their extradition."

The three accused were returned to Bubbling Well
Station at 4.45 p.m. 24/11/36 when the facts of the case
were communicated to Mr. R.W. Yorke, D.O. "B" Division
who after consulting with Major Bourne, D.C.(Special
Branch) instructed that they be handed over to
representatives of the P.S.Bureau. A receipt for these
persons was obtained and is now on file.

The question of photographing these persons prior
to handing over was waived on instructions of Major
Bourne D.C.(S.B.)

Copy to D.C.(Special Branch).

（印：TRIAL BRANCH 25 NOV. 1936 SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）

開庭時，第699號逮捕令中提到的第三人李公樸 (李公樸)
在法庭自首。

聽證後作出如下裁決：-

「三名被告李公樸、沈鈞儒和王造時並非在上海國際租界範圍內被捕，因此不涉及引渡問題。公共安全局應就其引渡事宜與國際租界工部局協商。」

三名被告於1936年11月24日下午4點45分被送回靜安寺捕房，當時案件事實已通報給「B」區分區督察長 R.W. Yorke 先生，他在與政治部副督察長 Bourne 少校協商後，指示將他們移交給公共安全局的代表。已獲得這些人的收據，現存檔。

根據政治部副督察長 Bourne 少校的指示，免除了在移交前對這些人拍照的程序。

抄送政治部副督察長。

The three accused namely Li Kung Po ( 李公樸 ),

appeared before the Kiangsu High Court on the A.M.

decision was rendered:-

"Remanded until 2p.m. 25/11/36 for further hearing.
All accused to be released on personal bonds of
their respective lawyers and to appear before the
Court whenever required.

1st. accused:- to Lawyers Tsang Yi Van, Ngau
Sung and Zung Tse Kao.

2nd. accused:- to Lawyers Tsang Yoh Tseng and
Zung Tse Kao.

3rd. accused:- to Lawyer Lee Vung Chih and
Yu Tsoong Ru.

Nyih of S.S.D. Court at the request of the Shanghai
Public Safety Bureau, was received by the Senior
Detective, B'Well Station for the arrest of the above
named three persons.

At 12.15a.m. 24/11/36 a party of detectives under
D.I. Toon and D.S. Kelly accompanied by members of
the P.S.B. proceeded to House 84, Lane 1376, Yu Yuan
Road, the home of Li Kung Po, but found him absent,

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
The following is the statement of. Li Kung Po ( 李公樸 ), age 35,
native of Changchow taken by me D.S. Kelly
at B'Well Stn on the 23/11/36 and interpreted by ------.

My name is Li Kung Po ( 李公樸 ), age 35, married,
native of Changchow, residing House 24, Lane 1376 Yu Yuen Road.
I arrived in Shanghai 5 years ago from Nanking to obtain
a situation with the "Shun Pao" Chinese Press on Hankow Road
as an editor and to organise a library and the Shun Pao
evening classes, where I have been employed since my arrival
at a salary of $300.00 per month.
I am not a member of any political party and have no
communist feelings. My last political connections were in
the year 1927 when I proceeded to the United States of
America where I studied politics and for two years until 1929
when I returned to Nanking and obtained a situation with the
Official Moral Endeavour Association until I left for Shanghai
as stated. My salary from the Association was $200.00 per
month.
I have numerous friends in Shanghai whom I have met during
my sojourn here.
This is my true statement.

Signed and crossmarked by:
Li Kung Po.

以下是李公樸 ( 李公樸 )，35歲，常州人的供詞，由我探員 Kelly 於1936年11月23日在靜安寺捕房錄取，由 ------ 翻譯。

我叫李公樸 ( 李公樸 )，35歲，已婚，常州人，居住愚園路1376弄24號。
我5年前從南京來到上海，在漢口路《申報》館擔任編輯，並組織圖書館和《申報》夜校，自抵達以來一直受僱於此，月薪300.00元。
我不是任何政黨成員，也沒有共產主義傾向。我最近的政治聯繫是在1927年，當時我前往美國學習政治，為期兩年，直到1929年返回南京，在官方道德促進會任職，月薪200.00元，之後如前所述前往上海。
我在上海期間結識了許多朋友。
這是我的真實供詞。

簽名並劃十字標記：
李公樸。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Sung Chun Zu ( ), age 63,
native of Kashing taken by me D.S. Kelly
at B'Well Stn. on the 23rd Nov, 1936 and interpreted by Clerk Y'eng.

My name is Sung Chun Zu, age 63, native of Kashing,
residing 51, Lane 1292 Yu Yuen Road, where I have resided
the last 2 years.

I came to Shanghai 9 years ago from Hangchow (1927) and
I have followed my employment as a lawyer since my arrival,
and I am a member of the Chinese Lawyer's Association, Rue
Lafayette.

Previous to come to Shanghai I was a member of the
Chekiang Provincial Government between 1926 and 1927, having
arrived in Hangchow from Peking in the year 1926.

Previous to the year 1926 I was a member of the National
Parliament in Peking since the forming of the Kuomintang
Government in 1911.

My reasons for coming to Shanghai was I had to seek
employment when the Provincial Government of Chekiang
reorganized in 1927.

I am at present a member of the Kuomintang Political
Party but take no active part.

I have numerous friends and relatives in Shanghai, many
of whom are members of the Kuomintang Party.

This is my true statement.

Signed and crossmarked by:
Sung Chun Zu.

以下是沈鈞儒 ( )，63歲，嘉興人的供詞，由我探員 Kelly 於1936年11月23日在靜安寺捕房錄取，由職員 Y'eng 翻譯。

我叫沈鈞儒，63歲，嘉興人，居住愚園路1292弄51號，我已在那裡居住了最後2年。

我9年前（1927年）從杭州來到上海，自抵達以來一直從事律師職業，我是福州路中國律師協會的會員。

在來上海之前，我曾於1926年至1927年間在浙江省政府任職，並於1926年從北京抵達杭州。

1926年之前，自1911年國民黨政府成立以來，我一直在北京擔任國會議員。

我來上海的原因是，1927年浙江省政府改組時，我需要尋找工作。

我目前是國民黨黨員，但不參與積極活動。

我在上海有許多朋友和親戚，其中許多人是國民黨黨員。

這是我的真實供詞。

簽名並劃十字標記：
沈鈞儒。

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of. WONG ZAU ZU
Tsao Shih tong (王造時), age 34,
native of Kiangse taken by me D.S. Kelly
at B'well Stn. on the 23/11/36 and interpreted by ----.

My name is Tsao Shih Wong, age 34, native of Kiangse,
married, residing 7B Tifeng Road.

I have resided in Shanghai since my arrival here in
1930 from England where I studied at the School of Economics
in London for 1 year. Prior to which I studied Political science
at the University of Wisconsin, U.S.A. 1925-1929 and obtained
a degree of P.H.D. From 1930 till 1933 I was Dean of School
of Liberal Arts and professor of Political Science at the Kwang
Hua University, Gt. Western Road, Shanghai.

Since 1933 till the present date I have practised law
at the local Courts (1st and 2nd. Special District Courts),
my offices being situated at No. 10 Mai Li Yuen, Gt. Western
Road, until the present month since which I have moved to 7B
Tifeng Road. I am also doing writing and editing work and
have edited many books.

I do not belong to any Political Party and have no
connection with the communist Party at all.

I have numerous friends in Shanghai, many of whom are
members of the Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang
and National Government.

This is my true statement.

Signed and crossmarked by:
WONG ZAU ZU
~~Tsao Shih Wong~~

以下为王造时（WONG ZAU ZU）之供词，
王造时（Tsao Shih tong），34岁，
江西籍，由本人 D.S. Kelly 于 1936年11月23日在百老汇路捕房（B'well Stn.）录取，并由 ---- 翻译。

本人姓名王造时（Tsao Shih Wong），34岁，江西籍，
已婚，住提篮桥路（Tifeng Road）7B号。

本人自1930年从英国抵达上海后便在此居住，此前曾在伦敦经济学院学习一年。在此之前，本人于1925年至1929年在美国威斯康星大学攻读政治学，并获得哲学博士学位。1930年至1933年，本人任上海大西路光华大学文学院院长及政治学教授。

自1933年至今，本人在本地法院（第一及第二特区地方法院）从事律师职业，事务所位于大西路麦里邨10号，直至本月搬至提篮桥路7B号。本人亦从事写作及编辑工作，曾编辑多部书籍。

本人不属于任何政党，与共产党毫无关联。

本人在上海有许多朋友，其中许多人是国民党中央执行委员会及国民政府成员。

此为本人真实供词。

签署并画押：
王造时（WONG ZAU ZU）
~~王造时（Tsao Shih Wong）~~

But now those accused were arrested unlawfully and so the disposal of them should be released in open court.
Mr. Ano Mei:-With reference to all the pleadings of the accused's lawyers, the actions of this court are absolutely unlawful. Therefore your honour does not execute the law but breaks the law.

郑道高先生：-现在这三名被告在阁下的保护下处于本法庭内。由于上海市警察局代表无权在本法庭逮捕他们，且警方也无权在无逮捕令的情况下逮捕他们，我请求阁下在听证后对他们进行处置。
姚先生：-我想了解，警方依据什么理由将被告带走？
伦恩先生：-在这种情况下，被告应被带回警察局，即恢复到出庭前的原始状态。
姚先生：-如果是由警方逮捕，应持有本院签发的逮捕令；如果是由上海市警察局逮捕，该局代表应身着制服。但现在这些被告是被非法逮捕的，因此对他们的处置应是在公开法庭上释放。
阿诺梅先生：-参照被告律师的所有辩词，本院的行为完全违法。因此，阁下不是在执法，而是在违法。
李范森先生：-根据起诉书，上海市警察局处于原告地位，因此这三名被告本应由警方逮捕，而不应由作为本案原告的上海市警察局逮捕。

So Chien Li (沙千里)
Shanghai.                                D.S. Haskell.
Sinza St'n              23-11-36.                Clerk Tsao Hsu Fan.

My name is So Chien Li, aged 34. I am a Lawyer by profession
and at present residing at House No. 14, Lane 524 of Avenue
Road. I have lived at this address for the past 6 or 7 years,
My business office being situated over the Stock Exchange
Building, No. 429 Kinkiang Road. I am a native of Shanghai,
having been born in this city. Up to the age of about 17
I attended a small Primary School on Honan Road (Building since
Demolished), during which time I lived with my mother. After
leaving this primary school, I remained at home for a period
of one year, and from the age of 18 onwards I studied Chinese
Law, at the Shanghai Law College on Kiangwan Road, attending
this Law course for 4 years, after which I again remained at
home for 1 year. At the age of 25 years, I decided to launch
out on a career of my own as a Lawyer, receiving financial
help from my mother So Koo Sz (沙顧氏). My first business
office was situated at No. 280 Peking Road. At which time I
lived at No. 9 Zung Chi Lee Alleyway of Shanhaikwan Road,
where I remained for 4 or 5 years, after which I removed to my
present address. I married my present (first) wife about 12
years ago, and am now the father of four children.

During February this year (1936) I became a member of the
National Salvation Association (全國救國會), and am now
an Executive Member of this organisation. I have attended
several meetings, findings of these meetings having on divers
occasions been forwarded to the Nanking Government, by the
association Committee, of which I am a member. I have nothing
further to say.

The aforegoing is my true statement.

Signed: So Chien Li
pages.zh:
沙千里（So Chien Li）
上海。                                副督察长 Haskell。
新闸巡捕房              1936年11月23日。                书记员曹旭藩（Tsao Hsu Fan）。

我叫沙千里，现年34岁。我的职业是律师，目前居住在爱文义路524弄14号。我在该地址已居住约6或7年，我的营业事务所位于江西路429号交易所大楼楼上。我是上海本地人，出生于此城市。直到约17岁，我就读于河南路上的一所小型小学（该建筑已被拆除），在此期间我与母亲同住。离开这所小学后，我在家待了一年，从18岁起，我在江湾路的上海法政学院学习中国法律，修读该法律课程4年，之后又在家待了1年。25岁时，我决定自立门户从事律师职业，得到母亲沙顾氏（So Koo Sz）的经济帮助。我的第一个营业事务所位于北京路280号。当时我住在山海关路众智里9号，在那里住了4或5年，之后搬至现在的地址。我大约在12年前娶了现在的（第一任）妻子，现在是四个孩子的父亲。

在今年（1936年）2月期间，我成为全国救国会会员，现为该组织的执行委员。我参加过几次会议，这些会议的决议曾由我所属的协会委员会多次转发给南京政府。我别无其他陈述。

以上是我的真实供词。

签名：沙千里

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
FEB 9 - 1939

“Seven Gentlemen” Going Free

Chungking Court
Withdraws Case

Activities Of Pre-War
Period No Longer
Subversive

The famous “Seven Gentlemen Case,” in which seven leaders of the National Salvation Association were charged with subversive activities endangering the Chinese Republic, has been brought to a conclusion in Chungking.

Declaring that the views and actions of the seven scholars, lawyers and professors were in no way contrary to the present national policy, the Chungking High Court, assigned by the Highest Court to take over the case from the Soochow Branch Kiangsu High Court, withdrew the prosecution against them. The decision was given in Chungking in the absence of the accused who are now actively engaged in political training and war service duties. Several of them are members of the People’s Political Council.

The seven leaders of the All-China National Salvation Association, an organisation with a large following among students and workers, are: Shen Chung-ju, lawyer; Li Kung-po, writer; Seh Chien-li, lawyer; Tsang Nai-chi, economist; Taou Tao-fen, writer; Wang Chao-shih, professor; and Miss Shih Liang, woman lawyer.

In the spring of 1937, they were rounded up in Shanghai and sent to Soochow to stand trial on charges of subversive activities. Demonstrations followed their arrest and, led by Madame Sun Yat-sen, widow of the late founder of the Kuomintang, many stormed the Soochow court. The legal battle lasted many months but came to an abrupt end in July when they were released following the outbreak of hostilities in North China. The ruling by the Chungking Court was merely a formality upholding their views and actions.

（批：G.8.2.54 FILE S/ 22 9/2）

1939 年 2 月 9 日

“七君子”获释

重庆法院
撤销案件

战前时期的活动
不再具有颠覆性

著名的“七君子案”已告终结，该案中七位全国救国会领导人被指控从事危害中华民国的颠覆活动。

重庆高等法院宣布，这七位学者、律师和教授的观点和行动绝不违背当前的国策，该院奉最高法院之命从江苏高等法院苏州分院接管此案后，撤销了对他们的起诉。判决是在重庆作出的，被告未出庭，他们目前正积极参与政治训练和战时服务工作。其中几人是国民参政会成员。

全国救国会是一个在学生和工人中拥有大量追随者的组织，其七位领导人是：律师沈钧儒；作家李公朴；律师史良（译注：原文为 Seh Chien-li，通常指史良，但此处拼音似有误，结合上下文及常见名单，Seh Chien-li 应指史良或沙千里，但后文列出 Miss Shih Liang 即史良，故 Seh Chien-li 极可能为沙千里 Sha Qianli 的误拼或另一人，此处依音译暂作“谢千里”或保留疑义，但根据历史事实，“七君子”为沈钧儒、章乃器、邹韬奋、李公朴、王造时、沙千里、史良。原文 Seh Chien-li 对应沙千里 Sha Qianli 的可能性较大，但拼音差异大。鉴于要求不确定保留原文，此处译为“谢千里(音译)”或根据历史常识校正？要求说“能确定的用当时通行的中文”，七君子名单是确定的。Seh Chien-li 极可能是 OCR 错误或拼写错误指代 Sha Qianli (沙千里)。但为了严谨，若无法完全确定对应关系，保留音译。然而，后文有 Miss Shih Liang (史良)。通常七君子包括沙千里。此处 Seh Chien-li 很可能是沙千里。但拼音相差甚远。让我们看其他名字：Shen Chung-ju (沈钧儒), Li Kung-po (李公朴), Tsang Nai-chi (章乃器), Taou Tao-fen (邹韬奋), Wang Chao-shih (王造时), Miss Shih Liang (史良)。剩下的一个是沙千里。Seh Chien-li 与 Sha Qianli 不符。可能是 She Qianli? 或者是 OCR 错误。鉴于这是历史档案翻译，且要求不脑补，我将保留音译并注明，或者如果非常确定是七君子之一，使用标准名。考虑到“Seh”可能是“Sha”的误读，“Chien-li”可能是“Qian-li”的误读。但在严格遵循“不确定保留原文”的原则下，我将译为“谢千里(音译)”，并在心中存疑。不过，为了读者理解，通常“七君子”是固定组合。让我再检查一下。啊，原文是 "Seh Chien-li"。在旧式拼音中，沙有时拼作 Sha，有时 Sa。Seh 很奇怪。也许是“史”？不，史良在后面。也许是“章”？章乃器是 Tsang Nai-chi。也许是“李”？李公朴是 Li Kung-po。也许是“王”？王造时是 Wang Chao-shih。也许是“沈”？沈钧儒是 Shen Chung-ju。也许是“邹”？邹韬奋是 Taou Tao-fen。剩下的就是沙千里。我将译为“沙千里(原文拼写为 Seh Chien-li)”，但这违反了“不确定保留原文”的规则吗？规则说“能确定的用当时通行的中文”。七君子是谁是确定的。但这个名字拼写是否指代沙千里是不确定的（因为拼写差异太大）。为了安全起见，我将使用音译“谢千里(音译)”，因为这更符合字面翻译要求，避免过度解读 OCR 错误。等等，再看一眼，有没有可能是“史良”被列了两次？不，Miss Shih Liang 是女性律师。Seh Chien-li 是律师。沙千里也是律师/经济学家？沙千里通常被描述为社会活动家。好吧，我将严格按照文本翻译。）
*修正思考*：根据历史事实，七君子为：沈钧儒、章乃器、邹韬奋、李公朴、王造时、沙千里、史良。原文列表：Shen Chung-ju, Li Kung-po, Seh Chien-li, Tsang Nai-chi, Taou Tao-fen, Wang Chao-shih, Miss Shih Liang.
Shen = 沈
Li = 李
Tsang = 章
Taou = 邹
Wang = 王
Shih Liang = 史良
剩下 Seh Chien-li 必然对应 沙千里 (Sha Qianli)。尽管拼音奇怪，但在历史语境下是确定的。我将译为“沙千里”，因为这是“能确定的”。

全国救国会七位领导人是：律师沈钧儒；作家李公朴；律师沙千里；经济学家章乃器；作家邹韬奋；教授王造时；以及女律师史良小姐。

1937 年春，他们在上海被捕，并被送往苏州，以颠覆活动罪名受审。逮捕引发了示威活动，在国民党已故创始人遗孀孙夫人的带领下，许多人冲击了苏州法院。法律斗争持续了数月，但在 7 月随着华北战事的爆发而突然结束，他们随后获释。重庆法院的裁决 merely 是一种形式，旨在支持他们的观点和行动。

（批注：G.8.2.54 档案 S/ 22 9/2）

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, July 6, 1937

Mme. Sun Active
Convicting Self
Widow And Colleagues
Collecting Evidence
To Get Into Jail

Madame Sun Yat-sen, widow of the late founder of the Kuomintang and "father" of the Chinese republic, and her colleagues are today collecting evidence against themselves in order that they may be detained and prosecuted with the seven All-China National Salvation Association leaders now facing charges of undermining the security of the state in the Kiangsu High Court in Soochow.

The party of 12, including Mrs. Chang Nai-chi, wife of one of the seven prisoners in Soochow, returned to Shanghai last night by the afternoon express after having staged a 10-hour "sit-down" strike in the Soochow court during which they demanded detention and prosecution with the seven accused inasmuch as they are co-workers in the National Salvation Association.

It was finally agreed that the 12 should furnish the procurate of the Kiangsu High Court with evidence substantiating their claim that they are similar in belief and behavior with the seven All-China National Salvation Association leaders.

The party arrived at the court shortly after 9 o'clock yesterday morning. They engaged in a heated verbal clash with the president and chief procurator of the court and were left alone in the reception room at 12.30. It was not until 5 p.m. that a procurator appeared and resumed negotiations with the petitioners. During the interval, however, the court supplied the petitioners with electric fans, tea and towels.

The discussion between the petitioners and the procurator lasted for more than two hours during which the latter is said to have admitted that the National Salvation Association itself is not an illegal organization and promised the petitioners to detain them and prosecute them in the event they produce sufficient evidence against themselves.

22860
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937 年 7 月 6 日，星期二

孙夫人积极
自我定罪
遗孀与同事
收集证据
以求入狱

孙中山夫人，国民党已故创始人及中华民国“国父”的遗孀，和她的同事们今天正在收集针对自己的证据，以便他们能够被拘留并与目前在苏州江苏高等法院面临危害国家安全指控的七位全国救国会领导人一同被起诉。

这支由 12 人组成的队伍，其中包括在苏州的七名囚犯之一章乃器的妻子章夫人，于昨天下午乘快车返回上海。此前，他们在苏州法院进行了长达 10 小时的“静坐”罢工，期间他们要求与七名被告一同被拘留和起诉，理由是他们是全国救国会的同事。

最终达成协议，这 12 人应向江苏高等法院检察官提供证据，证实他们的主张，即他们在信仰和行为上与七位全国救国会领导人相似。

该团体于昨天上午 9 点过后不久到达法院。他们与法院院长和首席检察官发生了激烈的口头冲突，并于 12:30 被独自留在接待室。直到下午 5 点，一名检察官才出现并与请愿者恢复谈判。然而，在此期间，法院向请愿者提供了电风扇、茶水和毛巾。

请愿者与检察官之间的讨论持续了两个多小时，据说后者承认全国救国会本身并非非法组织，并承诺如果请愿者提供足够的针对自己的证据，将拘留并起诉他们。
