The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, July 5, 1937

Mme. Sun Stages
Sit-Down Strike
In Soochow Court

Widow Of Party Chief
And Others Seek
Arrest, Trial

TRIBUNAL REJECTS
SYMPATHY PLEA

Over 200 Said Asking
To Share Charges
With 7 Leaders

(Special To The Post)
SOOCHOW, July 5.—Madame Sun Yat-sen, widow of the founder of the Kuomintang and "father" of the Chinese Republic, has declared a "sit-down" strike in the Kiangsu High Court here.
With eleven others, who described themselves as co-workers of the seven All-China National Salvation Association leaders now facing charges of undermining the security of the state in the tribunal, Madame Sun, who is the former Miss Soong Ching-ling, a sister of of Madame Chiang Kai-shek and Madame H. H. Kung, arrived here by the "Capital Express" from Shanghai this morning.

See President
They immediately proceeded to the court where they demanded to see the president and the chief procurator of the court to present a petition urging that they be also detained with the seven National Salvation Association leaders because they are similar both in "belief and behavior." They should share the consequences with the seven for what they have done together, they declared.
A delegation of three, headed by Madame Sun, was finally allowed to meet the president of the court. During the interview the president claimed that he has no rights to order their detention and that a procurators' conference must be called to deal with the request. The chief procurator finally came to meet Madame Sun, Mr. Hu Yutsz and Mr. Chu Ching-lai, writers.

Better Go Home
A heated verbal clash took place at this moment. The procurator declared he has no right to detain them and that in his investigations, he has so far found nothing against the petitioners warranting their detention and prosecution. The weather is hot in Soochow and the petitioners had better return to Shanghai immediately, the chief procurator said.
The argument continued until 12 noon when the chief procurator left the reception room. As the court is observing a summer schedule, no responsible officials were to show up this afternoon.

Have Tiffin
Undaunted by the refusal to detain them and to prosecute them together with the seven accused on charges of undermining the security of the state, Madame Sun and her colleagues decided to remain inside the reception room. Bowls of noodles were ordered and sent to the reception room as their "tiffin." At an early hour this afternoon, they were showing no signs of leaving.
Some 50 youths were waiting outside the court compound with a similar request that they be arrested and prosecuted together with the "seven gentlemen," as the seven accused are known. It is said that more were arriving for the same purpose.

No Date Set
The 12 petitioners who arrived this morning, other than Madame Sun, Mr. Hu and Mr. Chu, included Mrs. Chang Nai-chi, wife of the economist who is held as one of the seven leaders of the National Salvation Association.
No date for the resumption of the trial of the seven now world-famous "salvationists," however, has been set. It is widely rumored that they are due for release on bail and that they will go abroad. Their case, it is understood, will be widely discussed during the Kuling conference of Chinese intellectuals when they meet under the chairmanship of General Chiang Kai-shek and Mr. Wang Ching-wei, beginning July 15.

（批：26k 5/7）

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937 年 7 月 5 日，星期一

孙夫人在
苏州法院
发起静坐罢工

党魁遗孀
及其他人士寻求
逮捕、审判

法庭驳回
同情请求

据称超过 200 人要求
与七位领导人
共同承担指控

（本报特约稿）
苏州，7 月 5 日电。— 国民党创始人及中华共和国“国父”的遗孀孙夫人，宣布在此间的江苏高等法院进行“静坐”罢工。

宋庆龄女士（即孙夫人），蒋介石夫人和孔祥熙夫人的姐姐，与另外十一人于今天上午乘“京沪特快”从上海抵达此处。这十一人自称是目前在法庭上面临危害国家安全指控的七位全国救国会领导人的同事。

谒见院长
他们立即前往法院，要求谒见法院院长和首席检察官，提交请愿书，敦促将他们与七位救国会领导人一同拘留，因为他们在“信仰和行为”上相似。他们宣称，他们应与七人共同承担因共同行为而产生的后果。
由孙夫人率领的三人代表团最终获准会见法院院长。在会谈中，院长声称他无权命令拘留他们，必须召开检察官会议来处理这一请求。首席检察官最终前来会见孙夫人、作家胡愈之和朱镜哉（Chu Ching-lai，音译）先生。

最好回家
此时发生了激烈的口头冲突。检察官声明他无权拘留他们，并且在他的调查中，迄今为止未发现任何针对请愿者足以 warrant 拘留和起诉的证据。苏州天气炎热，首席检察官说请愿者最好立即返回上海。
争论持续到中午 12 点，首席检察官离开了接待室。由于法院执行夏季作息时间，今天下午不会有负责官员出现。

用午餐
孙夫人和她的同事们并未因拒绝将他们与七名被告一同以危害国家安全罪拘留和起诉而退缩，决定留在接待室内。他们点了碗面送到接待室作为“午餐”。今天下午早些时候，他们没有表现出离开的迹象。
大约 50 名青年在法院大院外等候，提出类似的请求，要求与被称为“七君子”的七名被告一同被捕和起诉。据说更多的人正出于同样的目的赶来。

未定日期
今天上午到达的 12 名请愿者，除孙夫人、胡先生和朱先生外，还包括经济学家章乃器的妻子章夫人，章乃器是被拘押的救国会七位领导人之一。
然而，目前尚未确定重新审理这七位如今世界闻名的“救国会成员”案件的日期。广泛流传的说法是，他们预计将被保释并出国。据悉，他们的案件将在 7 月 15 日开始的中国知识分子庐山会议上，在蒋介石将军和汪精卫先生的主持下进行广泛讨论。

（批注：26k 5/7）

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, June 26, 1937

Patriots Demand
Arrest For Aid
To Salvationists

Liberal Leaders Urge
Own Trial; Petition
Sent To Soochow

“IS PATRIOTISM
CRIME IN CHINA?”

Verbal Clashes Mark
Session; Hearing
Postponed

Declaring that they are also directors, members and friends of the All-China National Salvation Association and that they had worked together for the same cause with the seven accused now facing the serious charge of undermining the security of the state, Madame Sun Yat-sen, widow of the late founder of the Kuomintang and father” of the Chinese republic, Madame Liao Chung-kai, widow of the late Kuomintang leader assassinated in Canton in 1925, and 11 professors, authors and movie stars yesterday filed a petition with the Kiangsu High Court in Soochow asking that they also be placed under arrest and share the punishment, if any is forthcoming, with the seven defendants.

Those who signed the petition, which formed another dramatic development in the so-called “Case of the Seven Gentlemen,” are: Madame Sun (the former Miss Soong Ching-ling), Madame Liao, Professors Chu Ching-lai, Peng Wen-yin, Chang Tsung-hsi, Wang Puh-yen, Chang Chung-shih and Pan Ta-kwei, Writers Yu-chih, Wong Tung-shan, Chiang Tien-yih and Chen Tu-chiu, and Movie Actress Chen Po-chen, the “stormy-petrel of Chinese freedom” who last year was “requested” to leave Peiping due to Japanese resentment over her activities in organizing an anti-Japanese movement in the former capital.

Translation
A free translation of the full text of the petition follows:
“In connection with the case agains Shen Chung-ju et al on charges of endangering the republic, the petitioners, whose opinions and behavior are similar to theirs, pledge themselves to the court for trial in the same case.
“It needs little explanation that it is not a crime to be patriotic. The activities of Shen Chung-ju et al in working for the cause of national salvation are not illegal. Now they have been detained for more than half-a-year. If they were found guilty, the entire nation would be agog. The petitioners are either members of the National Salvation Association or directors of the National Salvation Association or, despite their non-membership, have worked together in the past with Shen et al for the cause of national salvation.

Ask Same Treatment
“If to be patriotic is a crime, then the petitioners should be given the same treatment as Shen et al. The petitioners could not allow Shen et al to take the punishment but are willing to share the responsibility resulting from the joint activities for the cause of national salvation. We urge the court to put us under detention for trial. In the event that to be patriotic is not a crime, we shall regain our freedom with Shen et al. If to be patriotic is a crime, we shall share the punishment with Shen et al. We are willing to risk our bodies to test if to be patriotic is a crime or not.”

Verbal clashes between Procurator Ong Chan-hien who drew up the indictment and the defendants and their defense lawyers and the persistent requests by the defense that evidence and witnesses in their favor be taken into consideration featured the lengthy seven-hour session in the Kiangsu High Court yesterday. The clashes developed to such a climax that the procurator threatened to take disciplinary action against the defense counsels and the defendants only to find his statement receiving a further deluge of scathing denunciations.

Coup Discussed
A major section of the hearing was devoted to the questioning of the accused in connection with their alleged instigation of the Sian Coup. The charges caused a deluge of protest from the defendants who urged the court to summon General Chang Hsueh-liang to the court for questioning whether he had staged the coup at their instigation or at his own will. They also suggested that the court also question Mr. Ma Hsiang-po, the 98-year-old member of the State Council, General Sung Che-yuan, chairman of the Hopei-Chahar Political Council, General Han Fu-chu, chairman of the Shantung provincial Government, and General Fu Tso-yi, chairman of the Suiyuan provincial government, concerning the identic telegrams despatched by the National Salvation Association asking them to send troops to Suiyuan to aid the defense against the “Manchukuan” and Mongolian insurgents.

The court rejected all of the requests but agreed to take steps to obtain the files from the Military Affairs Commission in connection with General Chang Hsueh-liang’s trial for the coup for which he was sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment, a sentence subsequently lifted.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年6月26日，星期六

爱国人士要求
因援助救国会成员
而被捕

自由派领袖敦促
对自己进行审判；请愿书
已送至苏州

“在中国，爱国主义
是犯罪吗？”

言语冲突标志
庭审过程；听证会
延期

孙中山夫人（已故国民党创始人及“中华民国之父”的遗孀）、廖仲恺夫人（1925年在广州遇刺身亡的已故国民党领导人的遗孀）以及11位教授、作家和电影明星昨日向位于苏州的江苏高等法院提交了一份请愿书。她们声明自己也是全国各界救国联合会的理事、成员和朋友，并与目前面临危害国家安全重罪指控的七名被告为同一事业共同奋斗过，请求法院也将她们逮捕，并与七名被告一同承担可能到来的惩罚。

签署这份请愿书的人士包括：孙夫人（即前宋庆龄小姐）、廖夫人、朱经农教授、彭文应教授、章宗羲教授、王造时教授、张仲实教授和潘大桂教授，作家郁达夫、王统照、江天翼和陈独秀，以及电影女演员陈波儿。陈波儿被称为“中国自由的暴风雨信天翁”，去年因在日本首都组织抗日运动引发日方不满而“被要求”离开北平。这份请愿书构成了所谓“七君子事件”中的又一戏剧性发展。

译文
以下是请愿书全文的自由翻译：
“鉴于沈钧儒等人因危害民国罪被起诉一案，请愿人因其观点和行为与诸被告相似，特向法院具结，要求在同一案件中接受审判。
‘爱国主义不是犯罪’，这无需多言。沈钧儒等人为救国事业所从事的活动并不违法。如今他们已被拘留半年有余。若判其有罪，举国必将哗然。请愿人或是救国联合会成员，或是救国联合会理事，或虽非成员但过去曾与沈钧儒等人为救国事业共同合作。

要求同等对待
“如果爱国主义是犯罪，那么请愿人应受到与沈钧儒等人同等的对待。请愿人不能容忍沈钧儒等人独自受罚，而愿分担因共同为救国事业活动所产生的责任。我们恳请法院将我们拘留受审。倘若爱国主义不是犯罪，我们将与沈钧儒等人重获自由。倘若爱国主义是犯罪，我们将与沈钧儒等人共担刑罚。我们愿以身体试法，以检验爱国主义是否构成犯罪。”

昨日在江苏高等法院长达七小时的庭审中，起草起诉书的检察官翁赞贤与被告及其辩护律师之间发生了言语冲突，辩方坚持要求法庭考虑对其有利的证据和证人。冲突激化至顶点，检察官威胁要对辩护律师和被告采取纪律行动，结果其言论反而招致更猛烈的严厉谴责。

讨论政变
听证会的主要部分集中于讯问被告，指控他们煽动西安事变。这一指控引发了被告的强烈抗议，他们敦促法庭传唤张学良将军到庭，质询他发动政变是受他们唆使还是出于自愿。他们还建议法庭就救国联合会发出的要求他们派兵赴绥远协助防御“满洲国”及蒙古叛军的同名电报一事，讯问国务会议成员、98岁高龄的马相伯先生，冀察政务委员会委员长宋哲元将军，山东省政府主席韩复榘将军，以及绥远省政府主席傅作义将军。

法庭驳回了所有请求，但同意采取措施，从军事委员会获取有关张学良将军因政变受审的文件档案，张将军曾被判处十年监禁，该判决随后被撤销。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, June 15, 1937

Seven-Gentlemen
Release Sought
By Many Leaders

Financiers, Publishers
Here Urge Freedom
Of Salvationists

SCHEME STUDIED
FOR COMPROMISE

Prisoners Might Leave
China; Nipponese
Attack Trial

The movement for the release, unconditionally or otherwise, of the seven All-China National Salvation Association leaders now detained in Soochow on charges of undermining the security of the state is rapidly growing.

More than 10 leading Chinese figures in Shanghai financial circles have jointly telegraphed to Chairman Lin Sen of the National Government, Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek, Mr. Wang Ching-wei and President Onli Cheng of the Judicial Yuan asking for leniency for Mr. Chang Nai-chi, one of the "Seven Gentlemen," and his release.

Mr. Chang, banker and economist, the financial leaders pleaded, worked in the financial world for more than 10 years and his services for works on economic reconstruction should be valuable. The names appearing on the telegram included those of Messrs. S. I. Hsu, Li Ming, Ling Hong-mou, Tzeng Yang-shih and Yu Kuo-ching.

The Publishers' Association in Shanghai is also rallying to the aid of its distinguished member, Mr. Tsou Tao-fan, writer and editor who once was publisher of the now defunct "Life Weekly." In a telegram worded in the same manner, the Association urged the high authorities to release the seven.

Conditional Release Talked

Two influential Chinese community leaders, at the same time, are quietly asserting their efforts for the same end via a different route. They are Messrs. Tu Yueh-sen, president of the Shanghai Civic Association, and Mr. Y. M. Chien, manager of the Joint Savings Bank. They visited Soochow during the week-end and are understood to have discussed with the seven accused a proposal to arrange for their release under conditions acceptable both to the Nanking authorities and the defendants.

Details of the reported proposal, however, could not be ascertained this morning. It is rumored, however, that a telegram has already been sent to Nanking by the two community leaders and new developments may take place within the next few days. It is generally believed that the "Seven Gentlemen" would be required to suspend their activities and, perhaps, go abroad in the event they are dismissed from the charges.

Ruling Delayed

Meanwhile, the Kiangsu High Court in Soochow has telegraphed to the Ministry of Justice for instructions in connection with the petitions filed by the seven now world-famous defendants for new judges to preside over their trial. The Ministry of Justice is understood to have replied that the court is entitled to the right to give a ruling on the petition and that in the event the accused are not satisfied with the decision, they may file an appeal with the Supreme Court.

No date has yet been set for the resumption of the trial. The question arising out of the petition for new judges on grounds that the three judges who presided over the first session are allegedly prejudiced and biased must be first settled before the trial may proceed.

Trial A "Farce"

The trial of seven leaders of the All-China National Salvation Association in Soochow was described this morning by The Shanghai Mainichi as a "farce."

The accused men, the daily said, had a six-month respite to prepare their defense. Their replies at last Friday's session showed extreme caution.

Significance Said Lost

Moreover, the Mainichi declared the trial was shorn of all its significance by the reported compromise accord between the Kuomintang and the Chinese Communist Party.

Finding support in this accord, the journal asserted, the defendants "actually put the Soochow judges on the defensive."

"It is interesting, however," the Mainichi concluded, "to see what verdict will be passed by the government without impairing its own dignity."
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年6月15日，星期二

众多领袖寻求
释放七君子

金融家、出版商
在此呼吁释放
救国会成员

研究妥协
方案

囚犯可能离开
中国；日本人
抨击审判

目前，要求无条件或以其他条件释放被控危害国家安全、现拘押于苏州的七位全国各界救国联合会领导人的运动正在迅速扩大。

上海金融界的十多位中国知名人士联名致电国民政府主席林森、蒋介石委员长、汪精卫先生以及司法院院长居正，请求对“七君子”之一的章乃器先生从宽处理并予以释放。

金融界领袖在电文中恳称，章先生作为银行家和经济学家，在金融界工作已超过十年，他在经济重建工作方面的服务具有重要价值。电报署名者包括徐新六、李明、凌鸿勋、曾仰丰和虞洽卿等先生。

上海出版业协会也在 rallying 支持其杰出会员、作家兼编辑邹韬奋先生，他曾是现已停刊的《生活周刊》的出版人。在该协会措辞类似的电报中，也敦促高层当局释放七人。

谈论有条件释放

与此同时，两位有影响力的华人社区领袖正通过不同途径 quietly 为实现同一目标而努力。他们是上海市民协会会长杜月笙先生和四行储蓄经理钱永铭先生。他们于周末访问了苏州，据悉已与七名被告讨论了一项提案，旨在安排他们在南京当局和被告双方均可接受的条件下获释。

然而，今晨尚无法查明该据报道提案的细节。不过有传言称，这两位社区领袖已向南京发出电报，未来几天内可能会出现新的进展。普遍相信，“七君子”将被要求停止活动，并且如果在指控被撤销的情况下，可能会出国。

裁决推迟

与此同时，位于苏州的江苏高等法院已就七位如今举世闻名的被告提出的更换主审法官的请愿书，向司法部请示指示。据悉，司法部回复称，法院有权对该请愿书作出裁决，如果被告对决定不满意，可向最高法院提起上诉。

尚未确定恢复审判的日期。由于声称主持首次庭审的三位法官存在偏见和偏袒，因此基于此理由要求更换法官的请愿书所引发的问题必须首先得到解决，审判方可继续进行。

审判是一场“闹剧”

《上海每日新闻》今晨形容在苏州进行的七位全国各界救国联合会领导人审判为一场“闹剧”。

该日报称，被告有六个月的喘息时间来准备辩护。在上周五的庭审中，他们的回答显示出极度的谨慎。

称意义已失

此外，《每日新闻》宣称，由于据报道国民党与中国共产党达成了妥协协议，此次审判已失去其所有意义。

该报刊断言，被告在这一协议的支持下，“实际上让苏州的法官处于守势”。

“然而，”《每日新闻》总结道，“看看政府在不损害自身尊严的情况下会作出何种判决，是很有趣的。”

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, April 26, 1937

Salvation Trial
Begins April 28
In High Tribune

Ten To Face Charges
Of Endangering
State Safety

TWO OUT ON BAIL
WITH 8 IN JAIL

Educational, Culture
Circles Watching
Proceedings

The trial of the 10 alleged leaders of the National Salvation Association, including the seven prominent intellectuals arrested in Shanghai November 23, will begin at the Kiangsu High Court in Soochow on Wednesday, April 28, it was announced today. The hearing, which will be continued on April 29, will be presided over by Chief Judge Fang Wen and Judges Chu Chien-hsen and Hai Wen.

The 10 accused are charged with offenses against the security of the state under Article Six of the Emergency Law governing Punishment for Offenses Endangering the Republic. When convicted, a maximum term of 15 years may be given. The minimum sentence, according to the article, is five years' imprisonment.

Two On Bail

Of the 10 accused, two are on bail and eight detained in the cells of the Kiangsu High Court. The seven arrested in Shanghai and among those detained are: Messrs. Shen Chung-ju, Sa Chien-li, Wong Tsao-shih, Li Kung-po, Tsing Nai-chi, Tsou Tao-fen and Miss Shih Liang. They are lawyers, professors, economists and writers. The other accused detained in the cells is Mr. Tso Tsing, formerly a secretary of the Chekiang Railway. He was arrested early this year in Nanking, where he is alleged to have attempted to organise an all-Kiangsu National Salvation Association.

The two accused released on bail and summoned to attend the trial on April 28 are Hu Liau-nsing and Ren Chung-kao, self-confessed members of the National Salvation Association. They were among the few delegates who signed a petition asking for the release of the seven prisoners. Few days ago they went to the court to present the petition, they were compelled to appear at witness stand and had to face the chief prosecutor. The three other delegates, however, did not attend. We hear that we still find them difficult to locate for their arrest has been ordered.

Seeks Professor

The court is also seeking the custody of Professor Tao Yin-chu, prominent Chinese rural education expert, whom the procurator charges as one of the leaders of the allegedly subversive organization. Professor Tao was known to have been lecturing in the United States.

The trial is being watched by Chinese educational and cultural circles and others sympathetic with their clamor for resistance against Japanese aggression. Only recently a group of American educators and editors, including Dr. John Dewey and Dr. Paul Monroe, cabled to Nanking expressing their concern over the arrest and detention of the seven National Salvation Association leaders.

General Li Lieh-chung, veteran Kuomintang member and a close associate of General Feng Yu-hsiang, yesterday visited the cells to call on the seven prisoners, according to Soochow reports. General Li has been staying in Soochow recently.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年4月26日，星期一

救国会审判
将于4月28日
在高院开始

十人将面临
危害国家
安全指控

两人保释
八人在押

教育、文化
界关注
诉讼进程

今日宣布，包括11月23日在上海被捕的七位著名知识分子在内的十名涉嫌全国各界救国联合会领导人的审判，将于4月28日星期三在苏州江苏高等法院开庭。听证会将于4月29日继续，由首席法官方文及法官朱建勋和海文主持。

十名被告被控违反《危害民国紧急治罪法》第六条规定的危害国家安全罪。一旦定罪，最高可判处15年徒刑。根据该条款，最低刑期为五年监禁。

两人保释

在十名被告中，两人保释在外，八人拘押在江苏高等法院的牢房中。在上海被捕并被拘押的七人是：沈钧儒、沙千里、王造时、李公朴、章乃器、邹韬奋和史良女士。他们是律师、教授、经济学家和作家。另一名被拘押在牢房中的被告是左恭先生，他曾任浙赣铁路秘书。今年年初他在南京被捕，据称他试图在那里组织全江苏救国联合会。

两名保释并被传唤参加4月28日庭审的被告是胡寥星和任崇高，他们是自认的救国联合会成员。他们是签署请愿书要求释放七名囚犯的少数代表中的几位。前几天他们去法院递交请愿书时，被迫出庭作证并面对首席检察官。然而，其他三名代表并未出席。我们听说仍然难以找到他们，因为已下令逮捕他们。

寻找教授

法院还在寻求拘捕陶行知教授，他是中国著名的乡村教育专家，检察官指控他是该涉嫌颠覆组织的领导人之一。据悉陶行知当时正在美国讲学。

中国教育界和文化界以及其他同情他们呼吁抵抗日本侵略的人士正在关注此次审判。就在最近，包括约翰·杜威博士和保罗·门罗博士在内的一群美国教育家和编辑致电南京，表达对七位救国联合会领导人在被捕和拘留一事的关切。

据苏州报道，国民党元老、冯玉祥将军的亲密盟友李烈钧将军昨日前往牢房探望了七名囚犯。李将军最近一直住在苏州。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, April 5, 1937

Salvationists
Facing Formal
Court Charges

Offenses To Security
Of State Alleged
By Government

TRIAL SCHEDULED
FOR THIS WEEK

Four More Well-Known
Intellectuals Named
As Conspirators

Formal charges of alleged offenses against the security of the state have been preferred against the seven leaders of the All-China National Salvation Association arrested in Shanghai on November 23, 1936, and three others who were taken into custody later. The trial of the 10 persons, including a woman lawyer, is scheduled to begin at the Kiangsu High Court in Soochow sometime this week.

The indictment against the "National Salvation" leaders, filed by the procurators with the High Court at the last minute before the expiration of the time-limit of the legally allowed detention of four months, also charged four others with similar offenses. As they are not yet within the jurisdiction of the High Court warrants were issued for their arrest. One of the "wanted" man is Mr. Tao Yin-chi, prominent educator and expert in rural education, who is known to be in America and last reported to be lecturing at Columbia University.

Jail Term Provided
The 10 accused now in custody of the Kiangsu High Court are charged with having organized groups with the aim of endangering the republic and having propagated doctrines incompatible with the Three Principles of the People. The article provides, in case of conviction, a jail term of from five to 15 years.

All of the 10 accused, it is understood, have denied the charges when they were handed duplicate copies of the indictment. They are consulting with their counsels to file their petitions.

Prisoners Well-Known
The names of the 10 accused of whom the first seven were arrested in the International Settlement and French Concession on November 23, follow:

1. Shen Chung-ju, lawyer, member of the standing committee of the Chinese Bar Association and dean of a law college in Shanghai.
2. Tsang Nai-chi, American-educated economist and formerly manager of a leading Chinese bank in Shanghai, being relieved of the post for his alleged political activities.
3. Li Kung-pe, American-educated educator and formerly president of the Sze Liang-tsai (newspaper publisher) Memorial School.
4. Tsou Tao-fen, writer and formerly editor of the Life Weekly, the periodical with the largest circulation in China.
5. Wang Tsou-shih, American-educated lawyer and formerly a professor with a local university.
6. Sa Chien-li, lawyer.
7. Miss Sze Liang, lawyer and the only woman in the group.
8. Lo Ching, formerly secretary at the Chengtai Railway Administration, arrested in Kiangyin last year and now detained in Soochow.
9 and 10. Ku Liu-hsing and Ren Chung-kao, alleged members of the Association retained since February 3 when attending a session in response to summons issued them by the High Court.

Warrants Issued
The four others for whose arrest warrants have been issued are:
1. Mr. Tao Yin-chi, educator now in America.
2, 3 and 4. Chang Chung-mien, Chen Tac-hung and Chen Chih, members of the National Salvation Association.

Names Signed
The last named three and Ku and Ren, who are now in custody and charged with the eight others, it is understood, were among the 21 National Salvation Association members who visited Soochow in January to appeal to the Kiangsu High Court for a speedy trial and release of their leaders. In submitting the petition, the court authorities asked them to nominate delegates and sign their names on the document. The five signed. Early in February, summons were sent to Shanghai asking the five to appear in court. Ku and Ren attended the session accordingly and were promptly detained. The three others failed to attend and warrants for their arrest have been issued.

Repeated petitions had been sent to Nanking and the court authorities in Soochow asking for their acquittal and immediate release. A few weeks ago, leading American educators, professors and editors jointly sent a telegram to Nanking expressing their concern over the seven National Salvation leaders. It is believed that the court has ordered the arrest of Mr. Tao Yin-chu as result of this telegram, believing that he was the man who prompted the Americans to send the telegram. Several of the signatories of the despatch to Nanking, it is recalled, were professors at Columbia University Teachers' College.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年4月5日，星期一

救国会成员
面临正式
法庭指控

政府指控
危害国家安全罪

审判定于
本周进行

另有四名知名
知识分子被指
为共谋者

针对1936年11月23日在上海被捕的七名全国各界救国联合会领导人，以及随后被拘留的另外三人，当局已正式提出涉嫌危害国家安全的指控。包括一名女律师在内的这十人的案件，定于本周内在苏州江苏高等法院开庭审理。

检察官在四个月法定拘留期限届满前的最后一刻，向高等法院提交了对“救国会”领导人的起诉书，该起诉书还指控另外四人犯有类似罪行。由于这些人尚不在高等法院的管辖范围内，已签发逮捕令予以缉拿。其中一名被通缉者是陶行知先生，他是著名的教育家和乡村教育专家，据悉身在美国，最近的消息称他在哥伦比亚大学演讲。

规定了监禁刑期
目前被江苏高等法院羁押的十名被告，被指控组织旨在危害民国的团体，并宣传与三民主义不相容的学说。根据该条款，一旦定罪，将判处五至十五年监禁。

据悉，这十名被告在收到起诉书副本时均否认了指控。他们正在与辩护律师商议，准备提交诉状。

囚犯均为知名人士
以下是十名被告的名单，其中前七人于11月23日在公共租界和法租界被捕：

1. 沈钧儒，律师，中华律师协会常务委员，上海某法学院院长。
2. 章乃器，受过美国教育的经济学家，曾任上海一家主要华商银行经理，因涉嫌政治活动而被免职。
3. 李公朴，受过美国教育的教育家，曾任史量才（报纸出版商）纪念学校校长。
4. 邹韬奋，作家，曾任《生活周刊》编辑，该刊物是中国发行量最大的期刊。
5. 王造时，受过美国教育的律师，曾任本地一所大学的教授。
6. 沙千里，律师。
7. 史良小姐，律师，也是该群体中唯一的女性。
8. 罗青，曾任正太铁路管理局秘书，去年在江阴被捕，现拘押于苏州。
9和10. 顾留馨和任崇高，据称为救国会成员，自2月3日应高等法院传票出席庭审以来一直被拘留。

已签发逮捕令
另外四名已被签发逮捕令的人是：
1. 陶行知先生，目前在美国的教育家。
2、3和4. 张仲勉、陈则洪和陈志，全国各界救国联合会成员。

签署姓名
据悉，最后提到的三人以及顾留馨和任崇高（现被拘留并与其余八人一同受指控），是今年一月前往苏州向江苏高等法院呼吁尽快审判并释放其领导人的21名救国会成员中的几位。在提交请愿书时，法院当局要求他们提名代表并在文件上签名。这五人签了名。二月初，传票寄往上海，要求这五人出庭。顾留馨和任崇高依约出席了庭审，随即被拘留。另外三人未出庭，已对其签发逮捕令。

人们曾多次向南京和苏州的法院当局发送请愿书，要求宣告无罪并立即释放。几周前，美国知名的教育家、教授和编辑联合向南京发出电报，表达对七位救国会领导人的关切。据信，法院下令逮捕陶行知先生正是这封电报的结果，因为法院认为他是促使美国人发送电报的人。回想起来，发给南京的电报签署者中有几位是哥伦比亚大学师范学院的教授。

Writ Detains
"Salvationists"
60 More Days

Kiangsu Highest Court
Says Examinations
Not Completed

SEVEN REMAINING
IN MODEL PRISON

Possible Amnesty Seen
For All Political
Prisoners

A writ authorizing the detention of the seven alleged All-China National Salvation Association leaders for two more months to allow further investigations was handed down by the procurate of the Kiangsu High Court in Soochow yesterday noon. The seven leaders, including a woman, were arrested in Shanghai two months ago.

In announcing the extension of the detention period, the procurate stated that the cases involving the seven defendants are so complicated that the preliminary examinations could not be completed within two months. Pending the indictment and formal trial, they are being held at the Kiangsu Model Prison and given treatment that is said to be better than that received by ordinary prisoners.

The seven prisoners are Shen Chung-ju, Sa Chien-li, Wong Chao-shih, lawyers; Li Kung-po educator; Chang Nai-chi, economist; Tsou Tao-fen, magazine editor; and Miss See Liang, woman lawyer. Miss See disappeared for several weeks after she was allowed bail by the Second Special District Court in the French Concession. She finally surrendered herself to the Kiangsu High Court in Soochow.

The round-up of the seven alleged leaders of the so-called "popular front" caused much excitement. During the Sian Coup, their immediate release was one of the demands sent to Nanking in exchange for the return of General Chiang Kai-shek. Their detention, however, may be cut short in the event the Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang, in its plenary session opening 11 days from today, approves the resolution for a general amnesty to all political prisoners.

拘票延长
“救国会成员”

江苏高等法院
称审讯
尚未完成

其余七人
关押于模范监狱

所有政治犯
可能获得大赦

昨天中午，苏州江苏高等法院检察处下达了一份拘票，授权将七名涉嫌为全国各界救国联合会领导人的嫌疑人再拘留两个月，以便进行进一步调查。这七名领导人（包括一名女性）于两个月前在上海被捕。

在宣布延长拘留期时，检察处表示，涉及七名被告的案件非常复杂，初步审讯无法在两个月内完成。在起诉和正式审判之前，他们被关押在江苏模范监狱，据说受到的待遇比普通囚犯要好。

这七名囚犯是：律师沈钧儒、沙千里、王造时；教育家李公朴；经济学家章乃器；杂志编辑邹韬奋；以及女律师史良小姐。史良小姐在法租界第二特区法院准予保释后失踪数周。她最终向苏州江苏高等法院自首。

对这七名所谓“人民阵线”嫌疑领导人的抓捕引起了极大轰动。在西安事变期间，他们的立即获释曾是向南京提出的换取蒋介石将军返回的条件之一。然而，如果国民党中央执行委员会在11天后开幕的全会上批准对所有政治犯实行大赦的决议，他们的拘留期可能会缩短。

（批：2/4 ok ）

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, DECEMBER 31, 1936

Miss Sze Liang Gives Self Up
At Soochow, Ends Long Hunt

The nation-wide police hunt for Miss Sze Liang, fugitive woman lawyer who jumped her bail following her arrest here last month together with six other leaders of the All-China National Salvation Association, ended yesterday when she surrendered to the Kiangsu High Court at Soochow.

Miss Sze appeared at the Court shortly after 12 o'clock and informed the procurator of the tribunal that she is the wanted person. She was questioned at a special Court session which lasted over two hours. The woman lawyer was ordered to be placed under detention together with the six other salvation association leaders.

Arrested in an early morning raid on her home in the French Concession on November 23, Miss Sze was released by the 2nd Kiangsu High Court on the bond of two of her lawyers. She failed to appear the next day when the Court reopened for hearing. Since that time, police of various cities had been ordered to arrest her. In several letters written to her lawyers Miss Sze pleaded that she had been ill and unable to attend court sessions.

It is understood that Miss Sze will be brought up for hearing together with the other leaders of her organization on charges of subversive activities.

《字林西报》，1936年12月31日，星期四

史良小姐在苏州自首
结束长期搜捕

全国警方对女律师史良小姐的搜捕于昨日结束，当时她向苏州江苏高等法院自首。史良小姐是一名逃犯，上月与其他六名全国各界救国联合会领导人一起在此被捕后弃保潜逃。

史良小姐在12点后不久出现在法院，并向法庭检察官表明自己就是被通缉者。她在一次持续两个多小时的特别庭审中接受了讯问。这名女律师被命令与其他六名救国会领导人一起被拘留。

史良小姐于11月23日清晨在法租界的家中被捕，随后由两名律师担保，经江苏高等法院第二分院释放。次日法院重新开庭审理时，她未能出庭。自那时起，各地警察奉命逮捕她。在写给律师的几封信中，史良小姐辩称自己生病，无法出庭。

据悉，史良小姐将以颠覆活动的罪名，与其他组织领导人一起接受审讯。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, December 10, 1936

The Arrested Salvation Leaders
COMMENTING upon the recent arrest of
six well known Chinese intellectuals,
writers and organizers of the All China Na-
tional Salvation Association, the China Critic
finds this action "unfortunate" in that "it
might give rise to misunderstanding among
the ignorant section of the public that they
were arrested for their writing and for being
leaders of the National Salvation Associa-
tion."
The Critic seems to have us, among
others, impaled upon its prong, for we confess
ourselves under the impression that the six
were arrested as leaders of the National
Salvation Association and if that makes us
out as ignorant, we'll have to face the charge
But we fear the Critic's logic is not
thoroughly air-tight when it suggests that
the arrest of these leaders cannot be due to
their connection with the association because
the Government has not suppressed the as-
sociation as "illegal" though it is unregistered.
The Critic says that the arrest was "due
to some recent acts of theirs, though the
statement failed to make explicit charges
against them." It seems well enough es-
tablished that the acts were as leaders of the
association, and that they consisted of par-
ticipation in the recent strike troubles in
Japanese cotton mills; which caused the Gov-
ernment to put them away because, as leaders
of the association, they were stirring up
something which might cause the Japanese
pot to boil.
We are glad to see that the Critic con-
cludes with expression of a hope that the
arrested "will be charged and tried publicly
as soon as possible, so that any possible mis-
givings on the part of the public may be soon
dispelled." Mayor Wu's office recently as-
sured us that due processes of law would be
followed, and had been followed. Even if
technicalities permit it, there should be no
delay in settling this case with its obvious
purely political connotations.
Ta Kung Pao has made an interesting
plea for leniency, suggesting that national
salvation now comes before all else.

（印：SHANGHAI BRANCH 11 DEC 1936）
（批：262 19/2）
（批：Jds）
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年12月10日，星期四

被捕的救国会领导人
《中国评论周报》在评论最近逮捕六名著名的中国知识分子、作家和全国各界救国联合会组织者一事时，认为这一行动“不幸”，因为“这可能会在公众中无知的那部分人当中引起误解，以为他们是因为写作和担任救国会领导人而被捕的。”
《评论周报》似乎把我们其他人也置于其矛头之下，因为我们承认，我们原本的印象是这六人是因为作为救国会领导人而被捕的，如果这使我们显得无知，那我们只能接受这一指责。
但我们担心，《评论周报》的逻辑并非无懈可击，因为它暗示这些领导人的被捕不能归因于他们与该协会的关系，理由是政府并未将该协会取缔为“非法”，尽管它未注册。
《评论周报》称，逮捕是“由于他们最近的一些行为，尽管声明中未明确列出对他们的指控。”似乎已有充分证据表明，这些行为是以协会领导人的身份进行的，具体包括参与近期日资棉纺厂的罢工风波；政府之所以将他们拘押，是因为作为协会领导人，他们在煽动可能导致日本方面局势激化的事态。
我们很高兴看到，《评论周报》最后表达了一种希望，即被捕者“将尽快被起诉并公开审判，以便早日消除公众任何可能的疑虑。”吴市长办公室最近向我们保证，将会且已经遵循法律正当程序。即使技术细节允许，也不应拖延处理这个具有明显纯粹政治含义的案件。
《大公报》提出了一个有趣的宽大处理请求，建议救国现在高于一切。

（印：上海分处 1936年12月11日）
（批：262 19/2）
（批：Jds）

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, December 2, 1936

Six Prisoners
Remain In Jail

“Salvationist” Leaders
Receive “Special
Treatment”

The Bureau of Public Safety
still is waiting for instructions
from Nanking as to the disposal
of the six leaders of the National
Salvation Association rounded up
10 days ago with Miss Szé Liang,
a woman lawyer who jumped bail
and disappeared, on charges of
alleged offenses against peace and
order.
The six are Shen Chung-ju, Sze
Chien Li, Wong Tsao-shih, law-
yers, Dr. Tsang Nai-chi, former
banker, Li Kung-po, writer and
educator, and Tsao Tao-feng,
editor.
They are being given “special
treatment” in the Bureau, being
provided with two rooms near the
commissioner’s office and allowed
all freedom to move about within
the rooms and receive visitors.
The six persons are not noticeably
worried and spend their time
playing chess, chatting and read-
ing. Up to now, no formal charges
had been preferred against them
although they were understood to
have been questioned in camera
separatively by a Bureau officer
Monday night.
Miss Szé Liang is still missing.
Her two attorneys, T. Z. Chang
and Tang Hou, who furnished
personal bail for her, yesterday
were summoned before the pro-
curate of the Third Branch
Kiangsu High Court for question-
ing. They were ordered held on
bail pending action.
In an editorial appearing in
the Ta Kung Pao, influential Chi-
nese daily, this morning, the
action by the authorities in de-
taining the six persons without
trial was scathingly denounced as
illegal inasmuch as the Chinese
law provides that prisoners should
be sent to courts for hearing 24
hours after their arrest. The
paper suggests that the six per-
sons should be handed over to
courts immediately for trial.
ing. They should be released or
sentenced, if they are guilty,
without delay.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年12月2日，星期三

六名囚犯
仍被关押在狱中

“救国会”领袖
受到“特殊
待遇”

公共安全局仍在等待南京方面关于处置十天前被捕的全国救国会六名领袖的指示。当时一同被捕的还有女律师施良（Szé Liang）女士，她已具保后潜逃失踪，被捕罪名是涉嫌危害和平与秩序。
这六人是：律师沈钧儒（Shen Chung-ju）、史良（Sze Chien Li）、王造时（Wong Tsao-shih），前银行家章乃器（Tsang Nai-chi）博士，作家兼教育家李公朴（Li Kung-po），以及编辑曹孟君（Tsao Tao-feng）。
他们在局内受到“特殊待遇”，被安排在靠近局长办公室的两间房间内，并允许在房间内自由走动及会见访客。
这六人并未表现出明显的焦虑，他们下棋、聊天、阅读以打发时间。截至目前，尚未对他们提出正式指控，尽管据悉周一晚间，一名警局官员已分别对他们进行了秘密讯问。
施良女士仍然下落不明。她的两位律师张知方（T. Z. Chang）和唐豪（Tang Hou）曾为她提供个人担保，昨日被传唤至江苏高等法院第三分院检察官处接受讯问。他们被责令具保候审，以待进一步处理。
在今早出版的中国有影响力的日报《大公报》的一篇社论中，当局未经审判即拘留六人的行为遭到严厉谴责，被视为非法，因为中国法律规定，犯人应在被捕后24小时内送交法庭听审。该报建议应立即将这六人移交法庭受审。
他们应被释放，或者如果有罪，则应立即判刑。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, December 14, 1936

Dementi
To the Editor:
Allow me to inform you that the report which appeared in your esteemed paper of Dec. 8, to the effect that "General Feng Yu-hsiang is harboring Miss Sze Lianz, woman lawyer who jumped bail after being arrested on charge of being a leader of the National Salvation Association," is absolutely groundless. It is a lie, pure and simple.
That the lie was fabricated with a malicious intent can hardly be questioned, since the Japanese paper from which you quoted declared Feng as a "notorious anti-Japanese leader."
Inasmuch as the report in question was a reproduction from the Japanese "Shanghai Nippo" you are of course duty-bound to produce the paper and send it on to us if you please.
Let me say, however, that it is perhaps more correct to say that General Feng is anti-Japanese imperialism and aggression rather than that he is anti-Japanese, for there is a world of difference between the two attitudes. If anti-Japanese imperialism and aggression are considered by the Japanese to be anti-Japanese, then there is no use of debating it here.
Kindly make due correction of the report in your next issue of the Shanghai Evening Post, send me a copy of the Japanese "Shanghai Nippo" in question and have this letter of mine published at the same time.
With greetings and thanking you in advance,
Yours for international good-will,
T. M. LOO.
Secretary of the General
General Feng's Headquarters
Nanking.
Dec. 11, 1936.

We gladly publish the above letter. However, having received the translation in question from a news agency and not being possessed of the copy of the "Nippo" for which demand is made, we have no intention of acting as a free clipping bureau for the General's Headquarters.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年12月14日，星期一

否认声明
致编辑：
请允许我告知贵报，贵刊12月8日刊登的一则报道，称“冯玉祥将军窝藏了施连珍（Sze Lianz）女士，该女律师因涉嫌为全国救国会领袖被捕后具保潜逃”，此说法毫无根据。这纯粹是谎言。
鉴于引用该报道的日本报纸称冯为“著名的反日领袖”，不难质疑该谎言是出于恶意捏造的。
既然相关报道是转载自日本《上海日日新闻》，贵报当然有责任出示该报纸，如蒙允准，请将其寄送给我们。
不过，我要说的是，或许更准确的说法是，冯将军反对的是日本帝国主义和侵略，而不是反对日本，因为这两种态度之间有着天壤之别。如果日本人将反对日本帝国主义和侵略视为反日，那么在此辩论便毫无意义。
恳请在下一期《上海晚邮报》中对该报道进行适当更正，将相关的日本《上海日日新闻》副本寄给我，并同时刊登我这封信。
致以问候并预先致谢，
致力于国际亲善的，
T. M. LOO.
冯将军总部秘书
南京。
1936年12月11日。

我们乐意刊登上述信件。然而，由于我们是从一家通讯社收到该译稿，且并不拥有被要求提供的《日日新闻》副本，我们无意充当冯将军总部的免费剪报服务机构。

pages.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 5, 1936

6 Of Salvation
Group Sent
To Soochow

Accused To Be Tried
In Kiangsu Higher
Court

The six leaders of the All-China National Salvation Association, who were arrested here two weeks ago for alleged subversive activities against the National Government, have been transferred to Soochow where they will be brought up for trial at the Kiangsu High Court, a report appearing in the China Evening News last night stated.

Ordered to be handed over to the Bureau of Public Safety authorities by the High Courts in the International Settlement and the French Concession, the group had been detained at the Bureau's headquarters on Bonlai Road. Arrangements were made early this week for transferring the group to Soochow.

Officials of the Bureau while admitting that the group would be sent to Soochow, refrained from revealing the date of their departure. It was reported last night that the men left for Soochow yesterday afternoon by automobiles.

Miss Sze Missing

Included in the group are Mr. Li Kung-po, Principal of the Liang Tsai Memorial School; Mr. Tsou Tao-feng, editor of the Life Weekly; Mr. Shen Chuen-ju, lawyer; Mr. Wang Chao-shih, former dean of the Kwang-Hua University; Mr. Chang Nai-chi, banker and economist; and Mr. Sa Chien-li, lawyer.

Meantime, Miss Sze Liang, the only girl and the seventh member of the group, was still missing yesterday. Arrested in her home two weeks ago during a raid when the other members were also taken into custody in their respective residences, Miss Sze, who is a lawyer by profession, was released on the bond of her attorney.

She failed to appear the next morning when a special session was arranged for the hearing of the arrested Salvation Association leaders at the 3rd Kiangsu High Court. Except for a letter received by her lawyers stating that she had no intention of returning to Shanghai to face trial, the fugitive girl has not been heard of since the day she walked out of the courtroom.

Miss Sze's lawyers were arraigned by the High Court last week for their failure to produce their charge. A court order directed them to furnish bail for their own liberty and produce Miss Sze in Court within 10 days.

In their desperate hope that Miss Sze might return, the attorneys inserted front page advertisements in local Chinese dailies, pleading that she live up to her promises. Miss Sze's sister also joined in the plea in another advertisement in which she said that their mother has been seriously ill ever since the woman lawyer disappeared from Shanghai.

（印：7 DEC 1936）

pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年12月5日，星期六

救国会
六成员
被送往
苏州

被告将在
江苏高等
法院受审

据昨晚《中国晚报》刊登的一则报道，两周前在此地因涉嫌从事反对国民政府的颠覆活动而被捕的全中国救国会六名领袖，已被转移至苏州，他们将在江苏高等法院受审。

根据公共租界和法租界高等法院的命令，该团伙被移交给公共安全局当局，此前他们一直被拘押在邦莱路（Bonlai Road）的警局总部。本周早些时候已安排好将该团伙转移至苏州的事宜。

警局官员虽然承认该团伙将被送往苏州，但拒绝透露出发日期。昨晚有报道称，这些人已于昨天下午乘汽车前往苏州。

施良失踪

该团伙成员包括：良友纪念学校校长李公朴先生；《生活周刊》编辑邹韬奋（Tsou Tao-feng）先生；律师沈钧儒（Shen Chuen-ju）先生；前光华大学教务长王造时（Wang Chao-shih）先生；银行家兼经济学家章乃器（Chang Nai-chi）先生；以及律师沙千里（Sa Chien-li）先生。

与此同时，作为该团伙中唯一的女性及第七名成员，施良女士昨天仍然下落不明。两周前在一次突袭行动中，她在自家住所被捕，当时其他成员也在各自住所被拘留。身为职业律师的施女士由其律师担保获释。

当江苏高等法院第三分院安排特别庭审审理被捕的救国会领袖时，她次日早晨未出庭。除了她的律师收到一封信，称她无意返回上海受审外，自从这名逃亡女子走出法庭那天起，就再也没有她的消息。

上周，高等法院因施女士的律师未能交出当事人而对他们提起诉讼。法院命令他们为自己的自由提供保释金，并在10天内将施女士带上法庭。

 attorneys 怀着施女士可能回来的绝望希望，在当地中文日报的头版刊登广告，恳求她履行承诺。施女士的姐姐也在另一则广告中加入呼吁，她说自从这位女律师从上海失踪以来，她们的母亲一直病重。

（印：1936年12月7日）

288/5/2

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, December 3, 1936

Salvation Leaders
To Face Soochow
Court On Charges

The six leaders of the All-China National Salvation Association, arrested 11 days ago on charges of alleged offenses against peace and order, will shortly be sent to Soochow under heavy police escort for trial in the Kiangsu High Court.

Under the Chinese law of criminal procedure, persons held on suspicion of offenses against peace and order are under the jurisdiction of the high court.

Whether or not Yao Shih-yen, a former employee of the Chinese Bankers' Credit Information Service arrested on suspicion of being connected with the six leaders and handed over to the Bureau by the Third Branch Kiangsu Court in French Concession yesterday, will be sent to Soochow could not be ascertained.

Miss Sze Liang, woman lawyer who jumped bail following her release, still is missing. Miss Sze is also alleged to be a leader of the National Salvation Association.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年12月3日，星期四

救国会领袖
将因指控
在苏州法庭
受审

11天前因涉嫌危害和平与秩序罪被捕的全中国救国会六名领袖，不久将在警方严密护送下被送往苏州，在江苏高等法院受审。

根据中国刑事诉讼法，因涉嫌危害和平与秩序罪而被拘留的人员属于高等法院管辖。

姚士彦（Yao Shih-yen），前中国银行家征信所雇员，因涉嫌与六名领袖有关联而被捕，并于昨天由法租界的江苏高等法院第三分院移交给警局，他是否会被送往苏州尚无法确定。

具保获释后潜逃的女律师施良女士仍然下落不明。施女士也被指控为全国救国会领袖之一。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, December 3, 1936

Detention Without Hearing
"LIBERAL", contributing to The Readers'
Forum today, comments among other
things upon the detention of six members of
the National Salvation Association.
While conscious of our obligation, as a
foreign journal in China, not to indulge in
undue tendering of advice or critical activity
toward the nation which is our host, we feel
it proper to note that yesterday's Ta Kung
Pao remarked upon the same event in a
frame of mind comparable to that of
"Liberal".
In fact that outspoken journal was dis-
tinctly opposed to the attitude of the authori-
ties in detaining the six without complying
with Chinese legal requirements to a hearing
within 24 hours of arrest. It declared itself
strongly on behalf of the civil rights of the
individual, and if any official view to the
contrary has manifested itself, the fact has
not come to our attention.
More pleasant, however, is the fact that
good treatment is apparently being accorded
the six. They are said to be incarcerated in
two comfortable rooms vastly better than
prison cells, near the office of headquarters
of the Bureau of Public Safety; special con-
sideration is reported to be accorded them,
and they are given such privileges as the
chance to smoke and play games. In other
words the authorities seem to be merely
keeping them "out of circulation" while in-
dulging in none of the horrors which have
been features of some past acts against
Leftists.
Clearly the authorities felt themselves
entitled to resort to extraordinary measures
to deal with an extraordinary situation. The
Salvationists sought to capitalize strike
troubles in local Japanese cotton mills in
connection with the Suiyuan warfare, and the
authorities feared international complications.
While the reported good treatment is
praiseworthy as far as it goes, the whole
affair is clearly extra-legal. Therefore it is
damaging to China's reputation for living by
her own laws.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年12月3日，星期四

未经听审的拘留
今日在“读者论坛”栏目投稿的“自由主义者”（LIBERAL），除其他内容外，评论了对六名全国救国会成员的拘留一事。
虽然我们意识到，作为在中国的外国期刊，我们有义务不对东道国过度提供建议或进行批评活动，但我们认为有必要指出，昨天的《大公报》也以与“自由主义者”相似的心态评论了同一事件。
事实上，那家直言不讳的报纸明确反对当局在未遵守中国法律关于被捕后24小时内进行听审的要求的情况下拘留六人的态度。它强烈主张维护个人公民权利，如果有任何相反的官方观点表现出来，我们并未注意到。
然而，更令人欣慰的事实是，这六人显然受到了良好的待遇。据说他们被关押在靠近公共安全局总部办公室的两间舒适房间里，条件远优于监狱牢房；据报道他们受到了特殊照顾，并被赋予吸烟和玩游戏等特权。换句话说，当局似乎只是让他们“停止活动”，而没有实施过去针对左翼人士的一些行动中所具有的那些恐怖手段。
显然，当局认为自己有权采取非常措施来应对非常局势。救国会成员试图利用绥远战事期间当地日本棉纺厂的罢工问题牟利，当局担心引发国际纠纷。
虽然据报道的良好待遇值得称赞，但整个事件显然是法外的。因此，这损害了中国依法治理的声誉。

pages.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 1 1936

Eighth Arrest Made
In Alleged Plotting
Against Government

Preparations are being made
by the Bureau of Public Safety
to send the six leaders of the
National Salvation Association
who were recently arrested for
alleged plotting against the
Government, to Nanking, it was
learned last night. The men
will be escorted to the Capital
for trial as soon as instructions
have been received which are ex-
pected to arrive in the next two
days. In the meantime the men
are being accorded special treat-
ment by the Chinese authorities.
Miss Sze Liang, a woman
lawyer and another leader of the
association, has fled from
Shanghai to an unknown destina-
tion after having been released
on bail. She is now being sought
by police throughout the country.
An eighth arrest in connection
with the case has been made by
the police. The prisoner, Yao
See-ngan, was brought up before
the Second Special District Court
for questioning yesterday.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年12月1日，星期二

涉嫌策划
反对政府案
第八人被捕

据悉，公共安全局正准备将最近因涉嫌策划反对政府而被捕的全国救国会六名领袖送往南京。一旦收到预计在未来两天内到达的指示，这些人将被护送至首都受审。在此期间，这些人正受到中国当局的特殊待遇。
女律师兼该协会另一领袖施良女士，在具保获释后已从上海逃往未知目的地。目前全国警方正在搜寻她。
警方已就此案实施了第八次逮捕。囚犯姚锡安（Yao See-ngan）昨天被提审至第二特区法院接受讯问。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, November 28, 1936

Woman Lawyer
Still Hides Out

Patriotic Organization
Leader Is Scheduled
To Face Court

With her case scheduled for
this afternoon at the Third
Branch Kiangsu High Court for
further hearing of the Bureau of
Public Safety application for her
extradition, Miss Sze Liang, one of
the seven "wanted" All-China
National Salvation Association
leaders, still failed to return to
her Route Lafayette home by this
noon and is accused by officers
of having jumped bail.
Six other leaders of the National
Salvation Association, termed by
government quarters as anti-
Nanking, are now all in custody
of the Chinese authorities after a
week of legal entanglements which
followed their arrest on Sunday
night. Four of them, arrested
in the International Settlement
and areas adjoining the extra-
Settlement roads, are in custody
of the Public Safety Bureau with
"special treatment." Of the three
arrested in the French Concession,
two were handed over by the pro-
curate of the Third Branch
Kiangsu High Court to the pro-
curate of the Shanghai District
Court yesterday afternoon for in-
vestigation into charges of offenses
against social order. The third
one, Miss Sze, is missing.
The extradition of the two, Dr.
Tsang Nai-chi and Mr. Tsao Tao-
feng, yesterday followed a brief
session. A communication was
sent to the Prefecture court by
the Nantao district court for their
custody. The prisoners were ar-
raigned before the court at 4 p.m.
and ordered handed over to the
Nantao procurate, not the Bureau.
The four leaders detained at the
Bureau are Messrs. Li Kung-po,
Shen Chung-ju, Sa Chien-li and
Wong Chao-shih.
It is generally believed that a
warrant for Miss Sze's arrest will
be issued by the Third Branch
Kiangsu High Court in the event
she fails to show up this after-
noon. When she left Shanghai
on Tuesday after furnishing bail
for her freedom, she announced
that she was heading for Soochow
to appear in the court there for
her client. No trace, however,
could be found of her in that city.
She was later said to be heading
for Changchow and Nanking and
nothing had been heard of her
since then.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1936年11月28日，星期六

女律师
仍然藏匿

爱国组织
领导人预定
出庭受审

鉴于江苏省高等法院第三分院定于今天下午进一步审理公共安全局申请引渡她的案件，作为七名被通缉的“全国各界救国联合会”领导人之一的史良女士，截至今日中午仍未返回其辣斐德路（Route Lafayette）寓所，并被警官指控弃保潜逃。
另外六名被政府方面称为反南京的救国会领导人，在上周日晚被捕后经历了一周的法律纠葛，目前均已被中国当局羁押。其中四人是在公共租界及越界筑路区域被捕的，现由公共安全局羁押并受到“特殊对待”。在法租界被捕的三人中，有两人于昨日下午由江苏省高等法院第三分院检察官移交给上海地方法院检察官，以调查其扰乱社会秩序之罪名。第三人即史良女士，目前下落不明。
昨天，经过简短庭审后，曾养甫博士和曹笃丰先生二人被引渡。南汇地方法院向该分院发出函件，要求羁押二人。囚犯于下午4时被提审至法庭，并被命令移交给南汇检察官，而非公共安全局。
被拘留在公共安全局的四位领导人是李公朴、沈钧儒、沙千里和王造时先生。
人们普遍认为，如果史良女士今天下午未出庭，江苏省高等法院第三分院将签发对她的逮捕令。她在周二提供保释金获释离开上海时，曾宣布她将前往苏州为其客户出庭。然而，在该市并未发现她的踪迹。后来据说她正前往常州和南京，此后便杳无音信。

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, NOVEMBER 29, 1936

WOMAN LAWYER IS
STILL HIDING

Leader Of Salvation
Group Is Sought;
Warrant Issued

Although Miss Sze Liang, one of
the seven alleged leaders of the All-
China National Salvation Associa-
tion, was still not found when her
case was called for hearing at the
Third Branch Kiangsu High Court
yesterday afternoon, a warrant has
been issued for her arrest and her
lawyers were urged to make all
efforts to locate her.

Six other alleged leaders are all
in the custody of Chinese authori-
ties after their arrest on last Sun-
day night in the Settlement and
French Concession. Miss Sze, a
lawyer, was also taken into custody
with the others but was released on
bail. She has been reported vari-
ously to be in Soochow, Changchow
and Nanking.
pages.zh:
《上海星期时报》，1936年11月29日

女律师
仍在躲藏

搜寻救国会
领导人；
已签发逮捕令

尽管昨天下午在江苏省高等法院第三分院传唤审理案件时，仍未找到 alleged 全国各界救国联合会七名领导人之一的史良女士，但已签发对她的逮捕令，并敦促她的律师尽一切努力寻找她的下落。

其他六名 alleged 领导人在上周日晚于租界和法租界被捕后，目前均处于中国当局的羁押之下。史良女士是一名律师，当时也与其他几人一同被拘留，但随后获准保释。据报道，她可能在苏州、常州或南京。

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, NOVEMBER 28, 1936

ANOTHER ARREST IN
SHANGHAI
Yet another man has been arrest-
ed in connection with the local
movement against alleged Commun-
ists and "reactionary" elements, thus
increasing the number of such ar-
rests to eight. He is Mr. Yeo Shih-
yen, an investigator of the Bankers
Co-operative Credit Service, Hong-
kong Road, who is now being de-
tained by the Third Branch Kiangsu
High Court.
Judge Yang Pong, presiding judge
of the Third Branch of the Kiangsu
High Court, has gone to Nanking to
interview his superiors regarding
the case.
Yeo was brought before the court
on Thursday afternoon at a short
hearing which was held in camera,
but it was then announced that his
case would be formally heard on
Monday. Yeo was arrested in his
house in Route Dupleix by the
French police at the request of the
Bureau of Public Safety. His house
was searched but it is not known
whether or not the officers seized
any documents.
pages.zh:
《上海时报》，1936年11月28日，星期六

上海又有一人
被捕

又有一个人因涉及当地针对 alleged 共产党人和“反动”分子的行动而被捕，从而使此类逮捕人数增至八人。此人是叶士彦（音译）先生，他是香港路银行家合作信贷服务的调查员，目前正被江苏省高等法院第三分院拘留。
江苏省高等法院第三分院主审法官杨鹏（音译）已前往南京，就此事与其上级进行面谈。
叶某于周四下午在一次不公开举行的简短听证会上被带上法庭，但当时宣布他的案件将于周一正式审理。叶某是在应公共安全局的要求，由法国警察在其霞飞路（Route Dupleix）寓所内被捕的。他的住所遭到了搜查，但目前尚不清楚警官是否查获了任何文件。

pages.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 27, 1936. No. S. B. D. 2086
Late

Editor, THE CHINA PRESS.
Sir,—I hope you will grant a foreign reader the space to express his views on the reported re-arrest, and your editorial comment thereon, of the National Salvation Association leaders. For a person who has closely followed the events of the last 12 months, it seems unbelievable—if not to say outrageous—that prominent personalities of social standing like the seven arrested should be persecuted for publicly advocating a united patriotic front against foreign aggression. And it appears simply farcical when you state, in this connection that "confronted by external aggression China must of necessity preserve every ounce of her energy in a unified struggle for national existence." If the united front as advocated and achieved by the National Salvation Association is accused of "subversive activities," who shall carry on a united struggle? Is a coalition with Japan the desired "united front" then?
Every right-minded person, familiar with Chinese personalities, knows that the arrested lawyers, bankers, etc. have done nothing but defended the unity and national independence of China, and have found enthusiastic supporters in all the ranks of the Chinese people.
In the light of your statement (in the editorial "Admitted") that the "Chinese are . . . not prepared to yield to military pressure without fighting to the last," the reader must come to the conclusion that you are inconsistent or—worse—biassed.
In the second paragraph of "Subversive" you express your confidence "that justice will be meted out in accordance with law" while in the last paragraph of the same editorial you come to the conclusion that "by agitation . . . they have merely forfeited their right even to a hearing of their views."
Comparing these two statements, one becomes naturally afraid as to the fate of the seven arrested, if the most elementary right of every accused—to be heard—should be violated.
The open support of the strikers in Japanese mills by the National Salvation Association does not prove any instigation. The workers who slave endless hours for a miserable $12 a month need no agitators to tell them which way the wind blows. It was only logical that the strikers should be supported in view of the ten per cent wage-increase granted by Chinese mill-owners.
For a foreigner who believes in the Bill of Rights; who knows furthermore that revolutionary leaders in the fight for national independence like George Washington have found great admiration in China; and who sees the necessity of a really united front among the Chinese people, irrespective of political views, in order to waive off foreign aggression:—the arrests and your comments thereon seem inconsistent with your own views on national unity, nay, even most unpatriotic.
A BRITISH READER.
Shanghai, Nov. 25, 1936.

S. 1-
R
27/11
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年11月27日，星期五。编号 S. B. D. 2086
迟发

致《字林西报》编辑：
先生，——我希望您能给予一位外国读者版面，让他表达对 reported 重新逮捕全国各界救国联合会领导人一事以及贵报对此发表的社论评论的看法。对于一个密切关注过去12个月事态发展的人来说，像这七位被捕者这样具有社会地位的知名人士，竟因公开倡导建立抗日爱国统一战线而遭受迫害，这似乎令人难以置信——甚至可以说是 outrage。而当您在此背景下声称“面对外来侵略，中国必须保存每一分力量，进行统一的民族生存斗争”时，这显得简直荒谬可笑。如果救国会倡导并实现的统一战线被指控为“颠覆活动”，那么谁来开展统一斗争呢？难道与日本结盟才是所期望的“统一战线”吗？
每一个熟悉中国人物且心智健全的人都知道，被捕的律师、银行家等人除了捍卫中国的统一和民族独立外，别无他图，并在中国各阶层人民中找到了热情的支持者。
鉴于您的声明（在题为“承认”的社论中）称“中国人……不准备在不战斗到最后一刻的情况下屈服于军事压力”，读者必然会得出结论：您要么是自相矛盾，要么更糟——存有偏见。
在题为“颠覆性”的文章第二段中，您表示相信“正义将依法得到伸张”，而在同一篇社论的最后一段中，您却得出结论认为“通过煽动……他们仅仅丧失了甚至让其观点被听取的权利”。
比较这两种说法，人们自然会担心，如果连每个被告最基本的权利——被听取意见的权利——都受到侵犯，这七名被捕者的命运将会如何。
全国各界救国联合会对日本纱厂罢工工人的公开支持，并不能证明有任何煽动行为。那些每月仅靠微薄的12美元工资而无尽劳作的工人，不需要煽动者来告诉他们风向如何。鉴于中国纱厂老板给予了百分之十的加薪，支持罢工者在逻辑上是理所当然的。
对于一个信奉《权利法案》的外国人来说；一个知道像乔治·华盛顿这样为民族独立而战的革命领袖在中国受到极大钦佩的人；一个看到无论政治观点如何，中国人民内部真正统一战线的必要性以抵御外来侵略的人而言：——这些逮捕行动以及贵报对此的评论，似乎与贵报关于国家统一的观点不一致，甚至可以说是最不爱国的。
一位英国读者。
上海，1936年11月25日。

S. 1-
R
27/11

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, November 26, 1936

Woman Lawyer
Still "Wanted"

Alleged Salvationist
Leader Disappears,
Others In Jail

Miss Sze Liang, woman lawyer
and one of the "wanted" leaders
of the All-China National Salva-
tion Association who was allowed
bail by the Third Branch Kiangsu
High Court, still is away from
Shanghai while four of her alleged
colleagues are detained in the
Bureau of Public Safety Headquar-
ters and two others are in custody
of the procurate of the higher tri-
bunal of French Concession.

The whereabouts of the woman
lawyer are unknown at her home.
When approached by The Shang-
hai Evening Post and Mercury,
it was declared that she would
return on Saturday to face the
court. When she left Shanghai in
a hurry on Tuesday, it was added,
she said she was going to Soo-
chow to appear for a client and
may go to Chanchow and Nanking
as well.

The latest alleged National
Salvation Association leader to be
handed over to the Chinese au-
thorities is Attorney Sa Chien-
li, who was arrested and re-ar-
rested at his Avenue Road home.
When brought up before the
Second Branch Kiangsu High
Court yesterday afternoon, the
application by the Bureau for his
custody was granted. A ruling
from the same court was respon-
sible for the extradition of
Messrs. Li Kung-po, Wong Chao-
shih and Shen Chung-ju Tues-
day afternoon.

Messrs. Tsao Tao-feng and Dr
Tseng Nai-chi, magazine editor
and former banker, who were ar-
rested with Miss Sze on Monday
morning in French Concession
were brought before the Third
French Kiangsu High Court yes-
terday and sent to the procurate
of the same court for investiga-
tion. No ruling was handed down
on the application for their
custody filed by the Public Safety
Bureau.

Meanwhile, students of 12 Chi-
nese universities in Peiping yes-
terday began their two-day strike
to protest against the arrest of
the seven National Salvation As-
sociation leaders. A delegation of
seven left for Nanking yesterday
morning to petition for their
early release.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1936年11月26日，星期四

女律师
仍被“通缉”

 alleged 救国会
领导人失踪，
其他人入狱

史良女士是一位女律师，也是江苏省高等法院第三分院准予保释的“被通缉”的全国各界救国联合会领导人之一，她目前仍不在上海，而她 alleged 的四位同事被拘留在公共安全局总部，另外两人则由法租界高等法院检察官羁押。

这位女律师在其寓所的住址不明。当《上海晚邮报与信使报》记者询问时，有人宣称她将于周六返回出庭。补充说，当她周二匆忙离开上海时，她说她要去苏州为客户出庭，也可能去常州和南京。

最近一名被移交给中国当局的 alleged 救国会领导人是律师沙千里，他在其爱文义路（Avenue Road）寓所被捕并再次被捕。昨天下午，当他被带至江苏省高等法院第二分院时，公共安全局申请羁押他的请求获得批准。同一法院的一项裁决导致了李公朴、王造时和沈钧儒先生在周二下午被引渡。

曹笃丰先生和曾乃炽（音译）博士（杂志编辑和前银行家），他们与史良女士于周一上午在法租界一同被捕，昨天被带至江苏省高等法院第三分院（注：原文此处可能有误，通常指涉法租界相关司法机构或江苏高院三分院在法租界的程序），并被送往同一法院的检察官处进行调查。对于公共安全局提出的羁押申请，尚未作出裁决。

与此同时，北平12所中国大学的学生昨天开始为期两天的罢课，以抗议逮捕七名救国会领导人。一个由七人组成的代表团昨天上午启程前往南京，请愿要求尽早释放他们。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, November 26, 1936

Mme. Sun Issues
Arrests Protest

“Hand Of Japanese” Is
Declared Evident
In Detentions

Mme. Sun Yat-sen (Soong Ching-ling) today issued a vigorous protest against the arrest of members of the Executive Committee of the All-China Federation of National Salvation Associations, at the same time dealing with rumors in the Japanese press that she herself has been arrested by French authorities. Her statement follows in full:
* * *
As one of the members of the Executive Committee of the All-China Federation of National Salvation Associations and in view of the arrest of seven of the leaders of this organization, I wish to enter my protest against these unwarranted arrests and the groundless charges made against them.

Japanese Influence
It is obvious to any thinking person that these arrests and these charges are the result of Japanese influence. That the hand of the Japanese can be seen in these arrests is evidenced by the report of the Shanghai Mainichi, issued on November 25th (yesterday) in which it is stated that I was arrested early this morning by the French authorities, charged with Communist activities, in connection with the Third International. Perhaps the Mainichi and the Nippo, which published similar rumors, have advance information, in which case my contention is well taken!
The well-known object of the National Salvation Association is to bring the Government and the people together into one united front of resistance to Japanese aggression. Contrary to the provocative assertions of the Japanese, the National Salvation Association is neither pro-Communist nor anti-Government. These charges are deliberately fabricated by the Japanese as a means of inciting the Chinese Government against the National Salvation Association, thus driving a wedge between the Chinese Government and the people for their own advantage.

Not Anti-Government
Despite these arrests and malicious charges, the National Salvation Association reaffirms its position: It is not anti-Government; it is not pro-Communist; it is for a united front to all people, regardless of their political beliefs or party affiliations, and for a national war of liberation.
May I point out the fact that such tactics on the part of the Japanese, contrary to their intention, will only serve instead to further arouse the wrath and patriotic indignation of the people against them.

Too Ridiculous
As to the personal charges made against me, it is too ridiculous that it should be necessary to refute the slanders of the Japanese press, which is notorious for its libelous and dirty disseminations.
Seven leaders of the National Salvation Association have been arrested, but there are still 400 million Chinese people, whose patriotic wrath and righteous indignation cannot be suppressed. Let the Japanese militarists beware! They may cause the arrest of seven leaders, but they must still reckon with the Chinese people.

Soong Ching-Ling
Member of Executive Committee
All China Federation of National Salvation Unions.
29 Rue Moliere.

S. I.
DBR
Chen 27/11

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年11月26日，星期四

宋庆龄女士发表
逮捕抗议书

宣称日本人在
拘捕行动中插手明显

孙逸仙夫人（宋庆龄）今日对全国各界救国联合会执行委员会成员被捕一事发出强烈抗议，同时驳斥了日本报纸上关于她本人已被法国当局逮捕的谣言。她的声明全文如下：
* * *
作为全国各界救国联合会执行委员会委员之一，鉴于该组织七位领导人被捕，我谨对这些毫无理由的逮捕以及针对他们的无端指控提出抗议。

日本的影响
任何有思考能力的人都清楚，这些逮捕和指控是日本影响的结果。日本方面插手这些逮捕行动的迹象，可见于11月25日（昨日）发布的《上海每日新闻》的报道，其中称我于今晨被法国当局逮捕，罪名是与第三国际有关的共产主义活动。或许刊登类似谣言的《每日新闻》和《日本日报》掌握了提前消息，若是如此，则我的论点便得到了证实！
众所周知，救国会的宗旨是促使政府与人民结成抵抗日本侵略的统一战线。与日本方面的挑衅性断言相反，救国会既不亲共，也不反政府。这些指控是日本方面故意捏造的，旨在煽动中国政府反对救国会，从而在中国政府与人民之间制造裂痕，以谋取其自身利益。

并非反政府
尽管发生这些逮捕和恶意指控，救国会重申其立场：它不反政府；它不亲共；它主张不分政治信仰或党派归属，团结所有人民组成统一战线，并进行民族解放战争。
我要指出，日本方面的这种策略，与其意图相反，只会进一步激起人民对他们的愤怒和爱国义愤。

荒谬至极
至于针对我个人的指控，实在荒谬至极，竟有必要去反驳日本报纸的诽谤，该报以散布诽谤和肮脏言论而臭名昭著。
救国会的七位领导人已被捕，但仍有四亿中国人民，他们的爱国愤怒和正义义愤是无法压制的。让日本军国主义者小心吧！他们可能导致七位领导人被捕，但他们仍必须面对中国人民。

宋庆龄
全国各界救国联合会执行委员会委员
莫利爱路29号。

S. I.
DBR
陈 11月27日

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 26, 1936

Charges Against Salvation
Group Suspects Defined

Instigation Of General Strike In Shanghai Is
Alleged By City Government To Have Been
Planned By Seven Arrested Leaders

Reasons for the arrest on Monday morning of seven well-known Shanghai residents and ways of dealing with them were explained in an official statement issued by the Greater Shanghai Municipality yesterday evening.

The seven arrested persons are: Li Kung-po, principal of the Liang Tsai Memorial School, Wang Tsaoshih, professor of Economics at Kwang Hwa University, Miss Shih Liang, attorney, Sha Chien-li, lawyer, Chang Nai-chi, formerly Assistant Manager of the Chekiang Industrial Bank, Shen Chun-ju, dean of the Shanghai Law College, and Tsuo Tao-fen, formerly editor of the "Life Weekly."

A free translation of the statement follows:

"Since the illegal organization of the National Salvation Association under their auspices, Li Kung-po and the others have maliciously manufactured rumours, under the guise of national salvation, their motive being no other than to weaken the people's confidence in the Central Government.

Recently, they have associated themselves with Communists, advocating the formation of the so-called people's united front, instigating class conflict, advocating the substitution of a National Defence Government for the Central Government.

Lenient Attitude

During the past year the authorities have adopted a most lenient attitude toward them, incessantly advising them to give up such activities. All the advice, however, had fallen on deaf ears, and worse, their opinions have recently taken shape in concrete activities.

Substantial evidence has been obtained that they recently have been secretly fanning a general labour strike in Shanghai, in order to attain their objective of creating disturbance and overthrowing the government.

At the present juncture, when the Suiyuan situation is tense, it is imperative that order and peace should be solidly maintained in the rear. To nip destructive forces in the bud, the authorities could not help but adopt the measures as called for in a period of emergency.

Unprecedented Crisis

When the nation is passing through such an unprecedented crisis, it is time that the entire nation, high and low, co-operated. Under such circumstances, it is necessary that subversive activities of a few radicals be curbed.

As to ways of dealing with them, it is natural that they will be tried in accordance with the proper procedure of law.

It has also been discovered that Communistic elements are still included in the National Salvation. To purge the organ of all undesirable influences, representatives have been sent together with members of the City Tangpu, to make a detailed investigation.

Shouldering the responsibility of maintaining peace and order here, the authorities of the Greater Shanghai Municipality not only could not stand aloof and see several hundred thousand labourers being led astray, but also would not tolerate the plunging of a city of three million people into a state of anarchy.—Central News.

（批：S.I / JKR）

《字林西报》，1936年11月26日，星期四

明确了对救国会
嫌疑人的指控

市政府称七名被捕领导人
策划在上海煽动总罢工

大上海市政府昨晚发布的一份官方声明中，解释了周一早晨逮捕七名上海知名人士的原因以及处理他们的方式。

七名被捕者为：良友纪念学校校长李公朴、光华大学经济学教授王造时、律师史良女士、律师沙千里、前浙江兴业银行副经理章乃器、上海法学院院长沈钧儒，以及前《生活周刊》编辑邹韬奋。

以下为该声明的自由译文：

“自从他们在幕后非法组织救国会以来，李公朴等人借救国之名恶意制造谣言，其动机无非是削弱人民对中央政府的信心。

最近，他们与共产党人勾结，鼓吹建立所谓的人民统一战线，煽动阶级冲突，主张以国防政府取代中央政府。

宽大态度

在过去一年里，当局对他们采取了最为宽大的态度，不断劝告他们放弃此类活动。然而，所有劝告均被置若罔闻，更糟糕的是，他们的观点最近已转化为具体行动。

已获得确凿证据，表明他们最近在秘密煽动上海总罢工，以实现其制造动乱和推翻政府的目标。

在绥远局势紧张的当前关头，必须稳固维持后方的秩序与和平。为了将破坏势力消灭在萌芽状态，当局不得不采取紧急时期所需的措施。

空前危机

当国家正经历如此空前的危机时，正是举国上下、无论高低贵贱通力合作之时。在这种情况下，必须遏制少数激进分子的颠覆活动。

至于处理他们的方式，自然将依照适当的法律程序进行审判。

还发现救国会内部仍包含共产主义分子。为了清除该机构中的所有不良影响因素，已派遣代表会同市党部成员进行详细调查。

大上海市政府当局肩负着在此维持和平与秩序的责任，不仅不能袖手旁观，坐视数十万工人被引入歧途，也不能容忍使一座拥有三百万人口的城市陷入无政府状态。——中央通讯社。

（批：S.I / JKR）

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 26, 1936
17772

Sa Extradited
But Cases Of 2
Others Pending

Tsao And Tsang Detained
In Frenchtown Until
Further Probing

One more of the seven prominent Chinese arrested in the Settlement and Concession here Monday on charges of subversive activity was handed over to the Chinese authorities yesterday, after a brief hearing on the 2nd Kiangsu High Court. Two others, Messrs. Tsao Tao-feng and Dr. Tsang Nai-chi were brought before the 3rd Kiangsu High Court for extradition hearings in the Concession but were ordered into the custody of the procurator for detention pending further investigations after a star chamber session.

There was no commotion, no excitement when Mr. Sa Chien-li, age 34, well-known local attorney, was brought before the 2nd Kiangsu High Court yesterday afternoon, to listen to extradition proceedings brought against him by the Bureau of Public Safety. Unlike the case on the day previous when Messrs. Li Kung-po, Wang Tsao-shih, and Shen Chien-ju were handed over by the police to the Chinese authorities, the matter was dispensed with quietly and quickly.

Sa entered the prisoners' dock shortly before 2.30 p.m. Half an hour later, he had been ordered handed over to the Bureau of Public Safety, and was on his way, under guard, out of the court compound.

The trouble which arose in court Tuesday afternoon when Messrs. Li, Wang and Shen faced extradition proceedings arose out of the fact that the trio had been arrested on extra-Settlement roads. Mr. Sa, however, was arrested at his home on Avenue Road and no such question entered into the proceedings.

Asks Proof Be Presented

The session opened with the request of a representative of the Bureau of Public Safety for the custody of the man on the grounds that the authorities were in possession of information to the effect that he was connected with a pro-communistic organization. Mr. Sa denied this, and insisted that proof be presented.

While the police handed Messrs. Li, Wang and Shen over to the Bureau of Public Safety after the court had announced that the question of extradition did not arise since the men had been arrested in Chinese territory, the court and not the police order Sa handed over.

The session held in the 3rd Kiangsu High Court yesterday afternoon in connection with extradition proceedings brought by the Bureau of Public Safety for the custody of Messrs. Tsao Tao-feng, former Editor of Life Weekly, Dr. Tsang Nai-chi, former Assistant Manager of the Chekiang Industrial Bank, and Miss Sze Liang, attorney.

Both Messrs. Tsao and Tsang were arrested Monday morning, and brought before the Frenchtown tribunal on the same day together with Miss Sze Liang. Like the four arrested in the Settlement, they were stated to have been nabbed on suspicion of having been the leaders of the All-China National Salvation Association, and that they had engaged in activities subversive to the Government.

Miss Sze Missing

They were released on personal bonds signed by their attorneys but the two men were re-arrested Tuesday evening and taken before the court in a midnight session which lasted until early yesterday morning. Miss Sze, however, could not be located.

The two men were brought back before the court yesterday afternoon. The court wanted to know why Miss Sze had not put in an appearance whereupon her legal representative stated that after her release on Monday, she had gone directly to Soochow where she had an important case pending in the 1st Kiangsu High Court. She remained in Soochow Tuesday and then went to see her grandmother at Changchow. Her attorney stated that so far as he know, she was still in Changchow.

After the matter of Miss Sze's whereabouts had been disposed of, the court cleared the room of all spectators and newspapermen.

Reasons for the arrest Monday morning of the seven Shanghai residents and ways of dealing with them were explained in an official statement issued by the Greater Shanghai Municipality yesterday evening.

A free translation of the statement follows:

"Since the illegal organization of the National Salvation Association under their auspices, Li Kung-po and the others have maliciously manufactured rumors under the guise of national salvation, their motive being no other than to weaken the people's confidence in the Central Government.

Formed People's Front

"Recently, they have associated themselves with Communists, advocating the formation of the so-called people's united front, instigating class conflict, advocating the substitution of a National Defense Government for the Central Government.

"During the past year the authorities have adopted a most lenient attitude toward them, incessantly advising them to give up such activities. All the advice, however, had fallen on deaf ears, and worse, their opinions have recently taken shape in concrete activities.

"Substantial evidence has been obtained that they have recently been secretly fanning a general labor strike in Shanghai, in order to attain their objective of creating disturbance and overthrowing the government.

"At the present juncture when the Suiyuan situation is tense, it is imperative that order and peace should be solidly maintained in the rear. To nip destructive forces in the bud, the authorities could not help but adopt the measures as called for in a period of emergency.

Need Co-operation

"When the nation is passing through such an unprecedented crisis, it is time that the entire nation, high and low, co-operate. Under such circumstances, it is necessary that subversive activities of a few radicals be curbed.

"As to ways of dealing of them, it is natural that they will be tried in accordance with the proper procedure of law.

"It has also been discovered that Communistic elements are still included in the National Salvation. To purge the organ of all undesirable influences, representatives have been sent, together with members of the City Tangpu, to make a detailed investigation.

"All in all, shouldering the responsibility of maintaining peace and order here, the authorities of the Greater Shanghai Municipality not only could not stand aloof and see several hundred thousand laborers being led astray, but also could not tolerate the plunging of a city of three million people into a state of anarchy."

（批：S.I / MR）

《字林西报》，1936年11月26日，星期四
17772

萨被引渡
但另两人案件
尚待处理

曹与章被拘押于法租界
以待进一步调查

周一在本市公共租界和法租界因涉嫌颠覆活动而被捕的七位知名华人中，又有一人于昨日在江苏高等法院第二分院进行简短聆讯后，被移交给中国当局。另外两人，曹陶风先生和章乃琦博士，虽在法租界被提至江苏高等法院第三分院进行引渡聆讯，但在一次秘密审讯后，被命令交由检察官羁押，以待进一步调查。

昨日下午，当34岁的本地知名律师萨建利先生被带至江苏高等法院第二分院听取公共安全局对其提起的引渡程序时，现场没有骚动，也没有激动情绪。与前一日李公朴、王造时和沈钧儒三位先生由警方移交给中国当局时的情况不同，此事处理得安静而迅速。

萨先生在下午2点30分前不久进入被告席。半小时后，他已被命令移交给公共安全局，并在警卫看守下离开法院大院。

周二下午，李、王、沈三人在面对引渡程序时，法庭上出现的麻烦源于这三人是在租界以外的道路上被捕的。然而，萨先生是在其爱文义路（Avenue Road）的家中被捕的，因此程序中并未涉及此类问题。

要求出示证据

聆讯开始时，公共安全局代表以当局掌握其与亲共组织有关联的信息为由，请求羁押该男子。萨先生对此予以否认，并坚持要求出示证据。

当法院宣布由于这些人是在中国领土上被捕，故不涉及引渡问题后，警方将李、王、沈三人移交给公共安全局；而对于萨先生，则是法院而非警方命令将其移交。

昨日下午在江苏高等法院第三分院举行的聆讯，涉及公共安全局为羁押《生活周刊》前主编曹陶风先生、浙江实业银行前副经理章乃琦博士以及律师史良女士而提起的引渡程序。

曹、章二人均于周一上午被捕，并于同日与史良女士一起被带至法租界会审公廨。据称，与在公共租界被捕的四人一样，他们因涉嫌担任全中国救国会领导人并从事危害政府的颠覆活动而被捕。

史良失踪

他们由律师签署具保书后获释，但这两名男子于周二晚上再次被捕，并被带至法庭参加一直持续到昨日凌晨的午夜庭审。然而，史良女士却下落不明。

昨日下午，这两名男子再次被带至法庭。法庭询问史良女士为何未出庭，其法律代表陈述称，她周一获释后直接前往苏州，因其在江苏高等法院第一分院有一重要案件待审。她周二留在苏州，随后前往常州探望祖母。其律师表示，据他所知，她目前仍在常州。

在处理完史良女士下落的问题后，法庭清退了所有旁听者和新闻记者。

大上海市政府昨晚发布的一份官方声明解释了周一上午逮捕七名上海居民的原因及处理方式。

以下是该声明的自由译文：

“自李公朴等人假借救国名义非法组织救国会以来，他们恶意制造谣言，其动机无非是削弱民众对中央政府的信心。

组成人民阵线

“最近，他们与共产党人勾结，鼓吹组成所谓的‘人民统一战线’，煽动阶级冲突，主张以国防政府取代中央政府。

“在过去一年中，当局对他们采取了最为宽容的态度，不断劝告他们放弃此类活动。然而，所有劝告都未被听取，更糟糕的是，他们的观点最近已转化为具体的行动。

“已获得确凿证据表明，他们最近在上海秘密煽动总罢工，以达到制造动荡和推翻政府的目的。

“在当前绥远局势紧张之际，必须稳固维持后方的秩序与和平。为了将破坏势力消灭在萌芽状态，当局不得不采取紧急时期所需的措施。

需要合作

“当国家正经历如此前所未有的危机时，正是举国上下、不分高低贵贱通力合作之时。在这种情况下，必须遏制少数激进分子的颠覆活动。

“至于处理方式，自然将依照适当的法律程序对他们进行审判。

“此外还发现，救国会内部仍包含共产主义分子。为了清除该机构中的所有不良影响因素，已派遣代表会同市党部成员进行详细调查。

“总之，肩负着维护本地和平与秩序的责任，大上海市政府当局不仅不能袖手旁观，坐视数十万劳工被引入歧途，也不能容忍将一座拥有三百万人口的城市陷入无政府状态。”

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, November 25, 1936

Students Rise
Against Arrest

Release Of Salvation
Leaders Demanded;
Police On Watch

Demanding the immediate release of the seven alleged leaders of the All-China National Salvation Association rounded up by International Settlement and French Concession police at the request of the Public Safety Bureau on charges of endangering the republic, university students in Peiping were scheduled to go on a two-day strike today. A delegation of the student body was also scheduled to leave the former capital for Nanking to petition the National Government for the immediate liberation of the seven persons while a manifesto was to be issued presenting their case. The steps were taken following a mass meeting of the student delegates from various universities and colleges in Peiping which was held on Monday night, some 15 hours after the arrest of the seven alleged leaders in Shanghai.

Chinese authorities in Shanghai are closely watching local students in order to prevent possible reaction. While the National Salvation Association is known to have close contact with the student bodies, the precautionary measures taken by the authorities following the city-wide student troubles last semester are expected to show effect in frustrating all plans to stage demonstrations sympathetic with the arrested persons.

The Bureau of Public Safety, believed to be acting on orders from Nanking, is determined to gain custody of all seven persons. While Messrs. Shen Chung-ju, 63-year-old lawyer, Li Kung-po, president of the Liang Tsai Memorial School, and Wang Chao-shih, lawyer and professor, have already been put into detention cells of the Bureau, legal proceedings were being resumed this afternoon for the custody of the four others.

学生起而反对逮捕

要求释放救国会领袖；警方严密监视

北平的大学生计划于今日举行为期两天的罢课，要求立即释放被公共租界和法租界警方应公共安全局请求、以危害民国罪逮捕的全中国救国会七名所谓领袖。学生代表团也计划离开故都前往南京，向国民政府请愿要求立即释放这七人，同时将发表宣言陈述他们的理由。这些举措是在周一晚间举行的北平各大学学生代表大规模集会之后采取的，此时距离七名所谓领袖在上海被捕约15小时。

上海的中国当局正密切监视当地学生，以防止可能出现的反应。虽然已知救国会与学生团体有密切联系，但鉴于上学期全市范围的学生骚乱，当局采取的预防措施预计将在挫败所有策划声援被捕者的示威计划方面发挥作用。

据信受命于南京的公共安全局决心获得对所有七人的羁押权。虽然63岁的律师沈钧儒先生、量才纪念学校校长李公朴先生、律师兼教授王造时先生已被关入公共安全局的拘留所，但今天下午已恢复对另外四人的羁押法律程序。

公共租界将三人
移交给中方

聆讯期间法庭气氛紧张；教育家否认共产党指控

因涉嫌从事危害政府的颠覆活动而被通缉的量才纪念学校校长李公朴先生、63岁的上海法学院院长兼上海律师公会常务委员沈钧儒先生，以及34岁的光华大学经济学教授王造时先生，于昨日下午在江苏高等法院第二分院经历了该院历史上最戏剧性的场面之一后被移交给中国当局。

另外两名男子，《生活周刊》编辑邹韬奋先生和银行家章乃琦先生，周一在法租界同样因涉嫌颠覆活动被捕，在昨晚和昨日下午于江苏高等法院第三分院举行的聆讯中，被命令在无保情况下羁押，以待下一次聆讯。

虽然这两名男子的审判原定于11月28日才进行，但昨日举行了特别庭审。邹先生于4点钟与其律师一同出庭，而章先生则在午夜前不久的一次特别聆讯中被提审。

史良女士，律师，周一因涉嫌颠覆活动被捕的七人小组中唯一的女性，昨日在被传唤时未出现在法租界高等法院。她的律师解释说，她正在苏州，作为律师在该市法院出庭。此处法院命令她于今日下午4点前到庭。

中央社报道称，周一被捕的七人被指控犯有运营与共产党合作的非法组织、煽动劳工、学生和总罢工以及其他颠覆活动的罪行，其最终目的是推翻政府。

出现在公共租界法庭上的这三名男子并非由法院本身移交，而是由警方移交。这一行动紧随被告对其被捕进行的激烈抗争之后，他们坚称逮捕是非法的。他们从法庭被带到老闸捕房，随后被正式移交给中国当局羁押。虽然中午过后不久已发出命令清空法庭内的旁听者和新闻记者，但大量这三名囚犯的追随者仍聚集在法庭内。新闻记者也走了进来，但预计随时会被命令离开。然而，该命令从未发出。

警察众多

大量警察在场以防止暴力行为，并曾在一次场合中被要求维持秩序。这正是在这些人被警方接管之后。旁观者中爆发出反对的喊声，但未发生暴力事件。喊声逐渐平息，三名囚犯被带离房间。

李、沈、王三人是周一上午应中国当局请求，由公共租界和法租界警方逮捕的七人（六男一女）中的三位。这三人连同34岁的知名律师萨建利先生，由上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）带走，并 accordingly 被带至高等法院。他们被命令由其律师具保释放。此事发生在上午，但到了夜间，已向公共租界当局提出请求，以他们可能试图离境为由，将这四人重新逮捕。

他们的重新逮捕令由第一特区

（印章：特别处 / 1936年11月25日 / 上海公共租界工部局警务处）
