Court after the police had found themselves unable to contact the District Court in Nantao to obtain dispatch warrants, which was the proper procedure for arrests to be made on extra-Settlement roads. All four men were residents of extra-Settlement roads.

Voluntarily Surrenders

Messrs. Sheng and Wang were nabbed at 1 o'clock yesterday while at home in bed. Sa was picked up later but apparently was not so badly wanted as the others because he did not appear in court yesterday. Mr. Li, however, managed to evade re-arrest by not staying at home. He was out when the police called, nor did he appear until about 2.45 p.m. yesterday when he made a dramatic entrance into the courtroom and voluntarily gave himself up.

When the four men were released on personal bond Monday afternoon, the next hearing of the case was remanded until Wednesday afternoon. Their re-arrest, however, made it necessary that they be brought before the tribunal yesterday. The session was opened before a full court. A representative of the Bureau of Public Safety presented request for the handing over of the three prisoners on the grounds that their names had been linked with certain communistic activities in China, although admittedly members of the National Salvation Association, which professes to be non-communistic in character.

The representative continued that certain communists had been arrested by the Chinese authorities and that these people had implicated Messrs. Li, Wang and Shen as important members of the radical group. This was denied by the three prisoners.

Mr. Li was the first of the three to speak on his own behalf. He spent little time dwelling on the charges but declared that he had been illegally re-arrested; that the First Special District Court had no right to re-arrest him after he had once been arrested and released on bond. Mr. Shen, a man of short stature but still active despite his 68 years of age, was the second speaker and he also claimed illegal arrest. Mr. Wang followed with a similar claim.

Former Minister Present

The large group of attorneys for the prisoners headed by Mr. Chang Yao-tang, former Minister of Justice for the defunct Peking Government, spent considerable time on the subject of illegal arrest, and further insisted that a prima facie case be established against their clients before extradition could even be considered. They declared that the court could not accept the statement made by the re-

Public Safety as a prima facie case. Further, they demanded that proof to the representative's statements be submitted.

At 3.30 p.m., the court called a recess of five minutes, after which it announced that "since the three resided in Chinese territory off extra-Settlement roads, the question of extradition does not arise."

This announcement had the effect of an exploding bombshell on almost everyone in the courtroom. If such was the case, then the prisoners would automatically become the prisoners of the Bureau of Public Safety. Nothing was said by the court, however, in respect to handing the men over.

The matter did not end here, however. Both the prisoners and their attorneys continued to fight for their freedom and this time, they charged that they had been illegally re-arrested because the warrants had been issued by the First Special District Court and not the Special District Court in Nantao.

Up To Nantao Court

Under the old Mixed Court Rendition Agreement, it was provided that prisoners taken by the Settlement police must be handed over to a modern law court. Since the Nantao court comes under this classification, prisoners are handed over only to that court and not to the Bureau of Public Safety which is a police body. In the case of arrests on extra-Settlement roads, such arrests have been made in the past on despatch warrants issued by the Nantao tribunal and not the First Special District Court.

The court, however, did not take an active part in the discussions that followed on this point. It had already rendered its decision to the effect that no question of extradition had arisen since the arrested men resided in Chinese controlled territory. Despite this ruling, however, the matter of handing the men over had not been settled.

Police officials at the court communicated the turn the proceedings had taken to police headquarters on Foochow Road and asked for instructions. Instructions came back from headquarters, apparently, to hand the men over. This was subsequently announced in court and the police took custody of the trio, bringing an end to the proceedings.

After considerable discussion of this point, the High Court admitted that the warrants should have been issued by the Nantao tribunal and accordingly withdrew the warrants of re-arrest. This action left Messrs. Li, Shen and Wang free men, enjoying the same status they had when they were released under personal bond on Monday.

This situation, however, was short-lived. Settlement police officers in the court-room apparently acting on instructions from their superiors, immediately took custody of the three men, and it was announced that they were to be handed over. The action raised a shout of disapproval from spectators but constables had restored order in a few minutes.

（续第1栏第3页。）

法院方面，警方发现无法联系到南市地方法院以获取逮捕令（dispatch warrants），而按照在租界外道路执行逮捕的正当程序，本应如此办理。这四名男子均为租界外道路的居民。

主动投案

盛先生和王先生于昨日凌晨1点在家中床上被捕。萨先生随后也被抓获，但他似乎不像其他人那样被迫切需要归案，因为他昨日并未出庭。然而，李先生通过不在家逗留成功避免了再次被捕。警察上门时他不在家，直到昨日下午约2点45分，他才戏剧性地出现在法庭并主动投案。

当这四名男子于周一下午具保释放后，案件的下次听证会延期至周三下午。然而，他们的再次被捕使得有必要于昨日将他们带上法庭。庭审在全员出席的法庭上开庭。公安局代表提出移交这三名囚犯的请求，理由是他们的名字与中国的某些共产主义活动有关联，尽管他们承认是全国救国会的成员，而该会声称其性质是非共产主义的。

该代表继续称，中国当局已逮捕了一些共产党人，这些人指认李、王和沈三位先生为激进团体的重要成员。这三名囚犯对此予以否认。

李先生是三人中第一个为自己辩护的人。他没有花太多时间纠缠于指控，而是宣称自己遭到非法再次逮捕；第一特区地方法院在他曾被捕并具保释放后，无权再次逮捕他。第二位发言的是沈先生，他身材矮小，但尽管已68岁高龄，依然精力充沛，他也声称逮捕非法。王先生随后提出了类似的主张。

前部长在场

由已故北京政府前司法总长章耀堂（Chang Yao-tang，音译）先生率领的庞大律师团，在非法逮捕这一问题上花费了大量时间，并进一步坚持认为，甚至在考虑引渡之前，必须针对其当事人建立表面证据确凿的案件（prima facie case）。他们宣称，法庭不能接受公安局重新提出的陈述作为表面证据确凿的案件。此外，他们要求提交证明代表所述内容的证据。

下午3点30分，法庭休庭五分钟，随后宣布：“鉴于这三人居住在租界外道路的中国领土上，因此不存在引渡问题。”

这一宣布对法庭内的几乎所有人来说犹如一颗爆炸的炸弹。如果情况确实如此，那么这些囚犯将自动成为公安局的囚犯。然而，法庭并未就移交这些人发表任何意见。

然而，此事并未就此结束。囚犯及其律师继续为争取自由而斗争，这次他们指控自己遭到非法再次逮捕，因为逮捕令是由第一特区地方法院签发的，而不是由南市特区地方法院签发的。

取决于南市法院

根据旧的《混合法院协定》（Mixed Court Rendition Agreement），规定由租界警察逮捕的囚犯必须移交给现代法律法院。由于南市法院属于此类，囚犯仅移交给该法院，而不移交给作为警察机构的公安局。在租界外道路逮捕的情况下，过去的逮捕均是依据南市法庭签发的逮捕令执行的，而非第一特区地方法院。

然而，法庭并未积极参与随后关于这一点的讨论。它已经作出了裁决，即由于被捕者居住在中国控制的领土上，因此不存在引渡问题。尽管有此裁决，但移交这些人的事宜尚未解决。

法庭上的警务官员将诉讼程序的转折情况通报给福州路警察总局，并请示指示。据推测，总局回示移交这些人。随后在法庭上宣布了这一点，警方接管了这三人的 custody，结束了诉讼程序。

经过对此点的充分讨论，高等法院承认逮捕令本应由南市法庭签发，因此撤回了再次逮捕的逮捕令。这一举动使李、沈和王三位先生恢复自由身，享有与周一具保释放时相同的地位。

然而，这种情况持续的时间很短。法庭内的租界警官显然是在执行上级的指令，立即接管了这三名男子，并宣布他们将予移交。这一举动引起了旁观者的不满呼喊，但巡捕在几分钟内恢复了秩序。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 25, 1936    17745

SUBVERSIVE

AT the request of the Bureau
of Public Safety of the
Chinese Municipal Government of
Greater Shanghai, the Interna-
tional Settlement and French
Concession police made on Mon-
day the arrest of seven Chinese
persons residing in their respec-
tive areas. The Chinese authori-
ties have requested for their ex-
tradition.

On our part we are confident
that the Bureau of Public Safety
must have acted in the best in-
terest of the community as well as
of the nation and that justice will
be meted out in accordance with
law.

The latest report stated that
the seven arrested—Li Kung-po,
Wong Tsao-shih, Shen Chung-ju,
Sa Chieh-li, Tsao Tao-feng, Tsang
Nai-chi and Miss Sze Liang—have
been formally charged with
plotting against the Chinese
Government. They are alleged to
be guilty of operating illegal
organizations, co-operating with
communists, instigating labor,
student and general strikes and
other subversive activities.

Just as the right-thinking
Chinese are invariably opposed to
internal strife, so are they op-
posed to any subversive activity
which may tend to undermine the
influence of constituted govern-
ment. Confronted by external
aggression China must of neces-
sity preserve every ounce of her
energy in a united struggle for
national existence. Any program
calculated to embarrass the gov-
ernment, however praiseworthy it
may appear to be, is apt to sap
that energy and minimize the
efficiency of the struggle. Thus a
person engaged in subversive
activities must be looked upon as
an enemy of the nation for whom
no sympathy may be entertained.

By this we do not mean that
things in the country are all what
they should be. Of the many
needs for reform and reconstruc-
tion no one is more aware than
the Central Government itself.
Progress must nevertheless be
achieved by degrees and under
unified direction. The most urgent
need today is national defence,
and to it all other things must be
subordinated. When China is rid
of all threats from the outside
world, then may she proceed to
undertake obvious reforms of
minor importance.

《字林西报》，1936年11月25日，星期三    17745

颠覆活动

应大上海市政府公安局的请求，公共租界和法租界警方于周一在其各自辖区内逮捕了七名中国人。中国当局已请求引渡他们。

我方相信，公安局必然是出于社区以及国家的最大利益行事，正义将依法得到伸张。

最新报告称，被捕的七人——李公朴、王造时、沈钧儒、沙千里、曹道丰、章乃及及史良女士——已被正式指控阴谋反对中国政府。据称他们犯有运作非法组织、与共产党合作、煽动劳工、学生及总罢工以及其他颠覆活动的罪行。

正如思想端正的中国人一贯反对内乱一样，他们也反对任何可能削弱既定政府影响力的颠覆活动。面对外部侵略，中国必然要保存每一分力量，进行团结一致的民族生存斗争。任何旨在使政府陷入困境的计划，无论其看起来多么值得称赞，都往往会消耗这种力量，降低斗争的效率。因此，从事颠覆活动的人必须被视为国家敌人，不应对其抱有任何同情。

这并不意味着国内的一切都尽如人意。对于许多改革和重建的需求，没有人比中央政府自身更清楚的了。然而，进步必须在统一的指导下逐步实现。当今最紧迫的需求是国防，其他一切事物都必须服从于此。当中国摆脱来自外部世界的所有威胁时，才可以着手进行那些重要性较小的明显改革。

Three Prominent Chinese
Ordered Handed Over
To Chinese Police

WARRANT ISSUED THEN
WITHDRAWN BY JUDGE

Subversive Activities Are
Alleged; No Prima
Facie Case Made

The question of the extradi-
tion of three alleged leaders of
the All-China National Salva-
tion Association, who were
arrested upon the request of
the Bureau of Public Safety
with four others in the early
hours of Monday morning, and
two of whom were re-arrested
at one o'clock yesterday morn-
ing on a warrant issued by
Judge Nyih, was subject of a
heated court hearing lasting
several hours in the Second
Branch of the Kiangsu Higher
Court yesterday afternoon.
Despite the contention of the de-
fence counsel that two of three men
were illegally arrested after being
released on the personal guarantee
of their lawyers, and the point
stressed by the legal representative
of the Shanghai Municipal Police
that a prima facie case had not been
made out against the men, Judge
Nyih, after retiring for consultation
together with the assistant judges
and procurator, pointed out that as
the men were arrested on extra-
Settlement roads there was no ques-
tion of extradition, but the giving of
assistance by one authority to an-
other.
The three men—Shen Chung-ju,
63-year-old Dean of the Shanghai
Law College and member of the
standing committee of the Bar As-
sociation; Wong Tao-shih, 54-year-
old professor of economics at
Kwang Hwa University; and Li
Kung-po, 55-year-old president of
the Liang Tsai Memorial School—
were then led out of the courtroom
by the International Settlement
Police, taken to Bubbling Well
Police Station and from there hand-
ed over to officers of the Bureau
of Public Safety.

Warrant Issued
The re-arrest of Mr. Shen and Mr.
Wong in the early hours of yester-
day morning on an authority of a
warrant issued by Judge Nyih, came
as a complete surprise in view of
the fact that the same judge had,
less than 24 hours earlier, released
the two men on the bond of their
lawyers. The warrant stated that
the men were wanted by the Bur-
eau of Public Safety on a charge of
committing acts with intent to in-
jure the Republic of China. The
legal representative of the Bureau
of Public Safety pointed out in court
yesterday that the warrant had been
issued upon explicit instructions
from Nanking.
The three men were originally
scheduled to be brought up before
the court together with Sa Chien-li,
lawyer, this afternoon. They, to-
gether with the two men and the
woman arrested in the Concession,
have often been described as anti-
Government and alleged to have
been behind many demonstrations
staged locally.

Deny Allegations
The allegations thrown at the
three men, that members of the Sal-
vation Association directed com-
munistic activities, were denied by
them. The Bureau of Public Safety
representative contended that many
an arrested Communist had made
statements to this effect as well as
students arrested during the distur-
bances here on September 18, last.
The defence contended that if com-
munists were members of the Sal-
vation Association, that did not
mean every member and leader was
a Communist.
The other three officers of the All-
China National Salvation Associa-
tion, who were arrested in the
French Concession, were brought up
in the Third Branch Kiangsu High
Court yesterday afternoon for trial.
As a result, Mr. Chou Ta-teng was
detained, the other two, Mr. Chang
Lai-chien and Miss Shih Liang, be-
ing released on bail.

《上海泰晤士报》，1936年11月25日，星期三

关于救国会成员的
激烈法庭听证

三名著名华人
被命令移交
给中国警方

法官先签发逮捕令
随后撤回

涉嫌颠覆活动；
未建立表面证据确凿案件

全中国救国会三名所谓领导人的引渡问题成为昨日下午江苏高等法院第二分院历时数小时的激烈法庭听证的主题。这三人连同另外四人于周一凌晨应公安局请求被捕，其中两人于昨日凌晨1点凭倪法官（Judge Nyih，音译）签发的逮捕令再次被捕。尽管辩护律师坚称，这三名男子中的两人在由其律师具保释放后遭到非法再次逮捕，且上海公共租界工部局警务处的法律代表强调针对这些人尚未建立表面证据确凿的案件（prima facie case），但倪法官在与助理法官和检察官退庭商议后指出，由于这些人是在租界外道路被捕的，因此不存在引渡问题，而是一个当局向另一个当局提供协助的问题。

这三名男子——63岁的上海法学院院长兼律师公会常务委员沈钧儒；54岁的光华大学经济学教授王造时；以及55岁的量才纪念学校校长李公朴——随后被公共租界警察带出法庭，送往静安寺捕房，并从那里移交给公安局官员。

签发逮捕令

沈先生和王先生于昨日凌晨凭倪法官签发的逮捕令再次被捕，鉴于同一位法官在不到24小时前刚凭其律师的保释金释放了这两人，此举完全出人意料。逮捕令称，公安局因指控这些人犯有意图损害中华民国的行为而通缉他们。公安局的法律代表昨日在法庭上指出，逮捕令是根据南京方面的明确指示签发的。

这三名男子原定于今天下午与律师沙千里一同出庭受审。他们以及在法租界被捕的两名男子和一名女子，常被描述为反政府分子，并被指策划了当地举行的许多示威活动。

否认指控

针对这三名男子的指控，即救国会成员指挥共产主义活动，遭到他们的否认。公安局代表辩称，许多被捕的共产党人以及去年9月18日本地骚乱期间被捕的学生都发表了此类声明。辩方主张，即使共产党人是救国会的成员，也不意味着每个成员和领导人都是共产党人。

另外三名在法租界被捕的全中国救国会官员，于昨日下午在江苏高等法院第三分院受审。结果，周达腾先生被拘留，另外两人张莱建（Chang Lai-chien，音译）先生和史良女士获准保释。

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 24, 1936-- 17698
REC
D. 7108
J // 36

7 Prominent
Chinese Face
Secret Court

Alleged Leaders Of China
Salvation Association
Arrested Here

MORE HEARINGS
DUE WEDNESDAY

Law College Dean And
School President
Among Group

Court sessions behind closed doors featured the arrests of six men and one woman, alleged to be leaders of the China National Salvation Association, yesterday. Four of the men, taken into custody, were brought before the 2nd Kiangsu High Court after evidence of arrest had been presented, were given their liberty on personal bonds signed by their defense attorneys. The case is scheduled to come up again on Wednesday.

The two men and one woman, nabbed in the French Concession, were brought before the 3rd Kiangsu High Court in the afternoon where the same treatment was accorded them. Their case was also remanded. At the next sessions, it is expected that the Chinese authorities, who are asking their extradition, will make an effort to establish prima facie cases against them in order to obtain their custody.

Sessions Short

As near as could be learned by a CHINA PRESS reporter, the sessions yesterday were short. Evidence of arrest was submitted by the police but no evidence against the prisoners was presented. The Chinese authorities, who were represented, asked extradition while attorneys for the suspects sought bail.

All seven of the arrested parties are prominent people. Most important perhaps is Mr. Li Kung-po, age 35, President of the Liang Tsai Memorial School, and a returned student from America. He was arrested at House 24, Lane 1375 Yu Yuen Road. The others arrested are:

Mr. Wong Tao-shih, age 34, a returned student from America, Professor of Economics at Kwang Hua University; Mr. Shen Chung-ju, age 63, dean of the Shanghai Law College and a member of the Standing Committee of the Bar Association; Mr. Sa Chien-li, lawyer residing at House 14, Lane 524, Avenue Road; Mr. Tsao Tao-feng, former Editor of the Life Weekly and well-known educator; Dr. Tsang Nai-chi, a returned student from America, formerly Assistant Manager of the Chekiang Industrial Bank, and formerly Vice-Managing Director of the Chinese Bankers' Credit Information Bureau, and Miss Sze Liung, lawyer, affiliated with the offices of Attorney Tung Kong, famous Chinese lawyer now lecturing in Peiping.

Wounded In Demonstration

Miss Sze was once wounded in a demonstration at West Gate. That was in September, 1931, and the demonstration was staged as a protest against the Japanese occupation of Mukden. The last three persons are those arrested by the French.

The seven were arrested on the request of the Bureau of Public Safety. Settlement and French Concession police officials yesterday stated that they knew very little about the case, adding that a prima facie case against them would have to be established before they could be extradited. It is understood that the Chinese authorities expect to have their cases prepared by that time.

Chinese authorities have made public no inkling as to the nature of the cases against the seven. It is understood, however, that they are wanted for agitation, but just what connection has not been definitely revealed.

（批：Sil / 28/8）

《字林西报》，1936年11月24日，星期二 -- 17698
收件
D. 7108
J // 36

七名显赫
华人面对
秘密法庭

 alleged 全国救国会领导人
在此被捕

更多听证会
定于周三举行

法学院院长及
学校校长
在列

昨日，闭门进行的法庭庭审涉及六男一女，他们被指为全国救国会（China National Salvation Association）的领导人。其中四名男子在被捕证据提交后，由江苏高等法院第二分院提审，经辩护律师签署个人保释具结书后获释。该案定于周三再次开庭。

另外两名男子和一名女子在法租界被捕，下午被带至江苏高等法院第三分院，受到同等对待。他们的案件也被延期审理。在下次庭审中，预计要求引渡他们的中国当局将努力建立针对他们的初步案件（prima facie cases），以获得对他们的羁押权。

庭审短暂

据《字林西报》记者了解，昨日的庭审时间很短。警方提交了逮捕证据，但未提出针对囚犯的证据。出庭的中国当局要求引渡，而嫌疑人的律师则寻求保释。

所有七名被捕者均为知名人士。其中或许最重要的是李公朴先生，35岁，良才纪念学校（Liang Tsai Memorial School）校长，美国留学生。他在愚园路1375弄24号被捕。其他被捕者包括：

王造时先生，34岁，美国留学生，光华大学经济学教授；沈钧儒先生，63岁，上海法学院院长，律师公会常务委员；沙千里先生，律师，住爱文义路（Avenue Road）524弄14号；曹道丰先生，前《生活周刊》编辑，著名教育家；章乃器博士，美国留学生，前浙江实业银行副经理，前中国银行家信用调查局副总经理；以及史良女士，律师，隶属于著名中国律师董康（Tung Kong，音译）的事务所，董律师目前在北京讲学。

在示威中受伤

史女士曾在西门的一次示威活动中受伤。那是1931年9月，该次示威是为了抗议日本占领沈阳。最后三人是由法国人逮捕的。

这七人是应公安局的要求被捕的。公共租界和法租界的警务官员昨日表示，他们对案情知之甚少，并补充说，必须确立针对他们的初步案件，才能进行引渡。据悉，中国当局期望届时能准备好他们的案件材料。

中国当局未公开任何关于针对这七人的案件性质的线索。然而，据悉他们因煽动活动而被通缉，但具体关联尚未明确披露。

（批注：Sil / 28/8）

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 24, 1936

BUREAU WANT THREE
CHINESE LAWYERS

Says They Are Concerned in
Political Offences

Declaring that they were concerned in political offences and Communist activities, a representative of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau made an application to the Second Branch Kiangsu High Court in the Settlement yesterday for the handing over of three lawyers, an editor, and a carpenter, who were arrested early yesterday morning at the request of the Bureau authorities.

The application was strongly opposed by the attorneys-at-law for the prisoners and, after a long legal battle, the court adjourned the hearing till to-morrow afternoon when a decision is expected to be given. Except the carpenter, the prisoners were all released on security. Three of the prisoners, namely, Li Kung-pao, editor, Sung Chun-zu, lawyer, and Wong Zau-zu, lawyer, were arrested by Bubbling Well police at 3 a.m. The fourth prisoner, So Chien-li, also a lawyer, was arrested at 2.30 a.m. at House No. 14, Lane No. 524, Avenue Road, by Sinza police, being suspected of being concerned in activities connected with the National Salvation Association. The fifth prisoner was Hu Yih-fong arrested in Carter Road.

（批：S / DBR.）

《北华捷报》，1936年11月24日，星期二

公安局欲要
三名中国律师

称其涉及
政治犯罪

上海公安局代表昨日向租界内的江苏高等法院第二分院提出申请，要求移交三名律师、一名编辑和一名木匠，称他们涉及政治犯罪和共产主义活动。这些人是在昨日清晨应公安局当局的要求被捕的。

囚犯的执业律师强烈反对该申请，经过长时间的法律辩论后，法院将听证会休庭至明天下午，预计届时将作出裁决。除木匠外，所有囚犯均获保释。其中三名囚犯，即编辑李公保（Li Kung-pao，音译）、律师宋春祖（Sung Chun-zu，音译）和律师王造时（Wong Zau-zu，音译），于凌晨3点被静安寺路巡捕房逮捕。第四名囚犯，也是律师的沙千里（So Chien-li，音译），因涉嫌参与与救国会有关的活动，于凌晨2点30分在爱文义路524弄14号被新闸巡捕房逮捕。第五名囚犯胡亦方（Hu Yih-fong，音译）在卡特路（Carter Road）被捕。

（批注：S / DBR.）

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, November 24, 1936 17725
Salvation Trio
Back In Prison
After Release
Three Alleged Chiefs
Enjoy But Brief
Freedom
POLICE PICK UP
MEN AT HOMES
Japanese Circulating
Wild Rumors About
Mass Arrests
After but 12 hours' freedom granted them yesterday when Judge Nylh of the Second Branch Kiangsu High Court released them in the custody of their attorneys, three alleged leaders of the All-China National Salvation Association, described in Chinese government circles as anti-government and subversive, were rearrested early this morning on an authority of a court warrant issued by Judge Nylh.
The men, Mr. Wong Tsao-shih, 34-year-old professor of economics at Kwang Hua University and lawyer, Mr. Shao Chung-ju, dean of the Shanghai Law College and member of the standing committee of the Bar Association, and Mr. So Chine-li, 34-year-old lawyer, were rearrested at their homes at 1 o'clock this morning by Detective-Sergeant Kelly of Bubbling Well Police Station and Detective-Sergeant Haskell of Sinza Station. Mr. Li Kung-po, president of the Tlang Tsai Memorial School, although before the High Court yesterday, was not taken into custody again.
Face Judge Today
All three men were being brought before Judge Nylh this afternoon where an application was being made for their handing over to the Bureau of Public Safety on a charge of committing acts with intent to injure the Republic of China.
Wild rumors concerning the arrest of seven supposed members of the salvation group were circulating about Shanghai this morning with Japanese dailies taking the lead. The Shanghai Nippo advanced the theory that the action of police in arresting the men was precipitated by their activities in the recent strikes in Japanese-owned mills, but this was vehemently denied in official police circles, it being pointed out that the men had simply been arrested at the request of the Bureau of Public Safety and that the Settlement Police had no case against them.
Must Present Case
It was pointed out by members of the legal profession this morning that in order to secure the custody of the three lawyers it would be necessary for the Bureau of Public Safety to present a prima facie case against them and give evidence concerning their supposed participation in subversive activities. If on the other hand, a court dispatch was obtained from the Nanking District Court, such evidence would not be necessary and the men would automatically be handed over.
Claiming that the movements of the National Salvation Association had lately turned from an anti-Japanese character to an anti-Nanking character, the Shanghai Nippo said that the seven leaders arrested yesterday were in some way connected with anti-Japanese terrorist gangs and went on to say that only the arrest of those pulling wires behind a screen of these pulling wires behind a screen of respectability will put an end to the anti-Japanese activities.
Hits F.M.P.
Lashing out against the French authorities, the paper declared that "lukewarm police" made it a paradise for political plotters, members of secret societies and political refugees.
"Connections are maintained between Hongkong and the French Concession here by secret organizations and political groups which have their headquarters in those two areas. In order that these subversive elements may be eliminated, it will be necessary for the French Concession authorities to take drastic suppressive measures.
"Although the Concession authorities seem to be co-operating closely with the S.M.P., the Japanese consular police and the Bureau of Public Safety, they lack determination," the journal charged.
（印：SPECIAL BRANCH SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 25 NOV 1936）
（批：D.B.R. 24/11 Oliver）
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年11月24日，星期二 17725
救国三人组
释放后
重回监狱
三名 alleged 首领
仅享受短暂
自由
警察在家
逮捕这些人
日本人散布
关于大规模逮捕的
荒谬谣言

昨日，江苏高等法院第二分院奈尔赫（Nylh，音译）法官将他们交由律师监管释放，在获得仅12小时的自由后，这三名被指为全中国救国会领导人的男子于今日凌晨再次被捕，依据是奈尔赫法官签发的法院令状。在中国政府圈子里，他们被描述为反政府和颠覆性的。

这些人分别是：王造时先生，34岁，光华大学经济学教授兼律师；沈钧儒先生，上海法学院院长兼律师公会常务委员；以及沙千里先生，34岁，律师。他们于今日凌晨1点在各自家中被静安寺路巡捕房的警长凯利（Kelly）和新闸巡捕房的警长哈斯克尔（Haskell）重新逮捕。良才纪念学校校长李公朴先生虽然昨日曾出庭高等法院，但未被再次收押。

今日面见法官

这三人将于今日下午被带至奈尔赫法官面前，当局将申请以“意图损害中华民国”的罪名将他们移交给公安局。

今晨，上海流传着关于七名所谓救国会成员被捕的荒谬谣言，日本日报对此推波助澜。《上海日日新闻》（Shanghai Nippo）提出一种理论，称警方逮捕这些人的行动是由他们在近期日资工厂罢工中的活动引发的，但这一说法遭到警方官方圈子的强烈否认，指出这些人仅仅是应公安局的要求被捕，租界警方对他们没有任何指控案件。

必须提出案件

法律界人士今晨指出，为了获得对这三名律师的羁押权，公安局必须提出针对他们的初步案件，并提供有关他们涉嫌参与颠覆活动的证据。另一方面，如果从南京地方法院获得法院移送令，则无需此类证据，这些人将被自动移交。

《上海日日新闻》声称，救国会的运动最近已从反日性质转变为反南京性质，并称昨日被捕的七名领导人在某种程度上与反日恐怖团伙有关联，接着又说，只有逮捕那些躲在体面幌子背后操纵的人，才能终结反日活动。

抨击法公董局

该报猛烈抨击法国当局，宣称“冷淡的警察”使这里成为政治阴谋家、秘密社团成员和政治难民的天堂。

“香港与此地的法租界之间通过秘密组织和政治团体保持联系，这些组织的总部设在这两个地区。为了消除这些颠覆分子，法租界当局有必要采取严厉的镇压措施。”

“尽管租界当局似乎与上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）、日本领事警察和公安局密切合作，但他们缺乏决心，”该报刊指责道。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别支部 1936年11月25日）
（批注：D.B.R. 11月24日 Oliver）

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, November 23, 1936
Police Arrest Prominent Leaders Of Local
Salvation Association During Night Raids;
Drag-Net Gets Seven; Court Hearing Slated

Six Men, One
Woman Seized
For Agitation

Publishers, Attorneys
Among Prisoners
Being Held

CHINESE POLICE
ASK EXTRADITION

Sextet Said Warned
Against Activity
Opposing Japan

Seven alleged leaders of the All-China National Salvation Association, described in Chinese official quarters as anti-government, subversive and responsible for the many demonstrations in Shanghai including the agitation for a general strike in Japanese cotton mills, were rounded up by International Settlement and French Concession police early this morning.

The arrests were carried out at the request of the Bureau of Public Safety of the City Government of Greater Shanghai, which is asking the extradition of the seven persons to face possible charges of offenses against the security of the state.

Raids Made Simultaneously
Carrying out the raids simultaneously between 1:30 and 3 o'clock this morning, the police arrested the seven persons in their respective homes. Those arrested in the International Settlement are:

Mr. Li Kung-po, president of the Liang Tsi Industrial School (in charge of Mr. See Liang), publisher of the ... and a returned student from America. He was arrested at his home at 14, Lane 524, Avenue Road. A book in Japanese containing four leaflets, the contents of which were not revealed, was found in his home.

Taken In Frenchtown
The three others arrested in the French Concession are:

Mr. Tsao Tao-feng, formerly editor of the Life Weekly, vernacular magazine which once had the biggest circulation in China and who was forced to be removed from the editorial chair for his anti-government outbursts to make a trip abroad. He was also well-known as an educator. He was arrested at his home at 4, Lane 601, Route Lafayette.

Dr. Tsang Nai-chi, a returned student from America, formerly assistant manager of the Chekiang Industrial Bank and formerly vice-managing director of the Chinese Bankers' Credit Information Bureau. He was arrested at his Rue Delastre home.

Miss Sze Liang, the only woman among the seven. She also is a legal practitioner, being affiliated with the law offices of Attorney Tung Kong, famous Chinese lawyer now lecturing in Peiping and mentioned for membership in the Judicial Committee of the Hopei-Chahar Political Council. She was once wounded in a demonstration at West Gate against the Japanese occupation of Shenyang on September 18, 1931. Officers gained entrance to her home at 1 Lafayette Terrace, Route Lafayette, by climbing over the wall.

All Face Courts
The seven arrested persons, widely known for their agitation for an immediate declaration of war against Japan, today were facing the courts. The four arrested in the Settlement were brought before the Second Branch Kiangsu High Court this morning after the courtroom had been cleared of reporters and persons not directly connected with the case. The hearing was conducted in camera. After a lengthy session, during which the Public Safety Bureau is understood to have requested their extradition, the hearing was adjourned until Wednesday afternoon and the four persons were allowed bail on their personal bonds, signed by their defense attorneys.

The three others, arrested in the French Concession, were facing the Third Branch Kiangsu High Court this afternoon. Similar requests were to be made for their extradition by the Public Safety Bureau, it is understood. Dr. T. Z. Chang was to appear for the defense of Miss Sze Liang and Mr. Tsao Tao-feng.

Movements Watched
Movements of the seven alleged leaders, who also are alleged to be founders of a political party known as the "Popular Front," have long been watched since the outbreak of subversive agitation in Kwangtung and Kwangsi. They are understood to have been repeatedly warned by the Chinese authorities against any anti-Japanese demonstrations in echo of the Kwangtung-Kwangsi demands for war with Japan.

When the labor disputes broke out in Japanese cotton mills, their movements again were kept under close watch. Allegations that they were pouring the oil of political issues into the flames of labor disputes are believed to be the immediate cause for their arrest.

The seven persons also are alleged to be anti-General Chiang Kai-shek, opposing the president of the Executive Yuan and chairman of the Military Affairs Commission with attempting to create a similar regime in China with himself as the dictator.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL 23 NOV 1936）
（批：Del / def. 28/11）
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年11月23日，星期一
警方在夜间突袭中逮捕本地救国会知名领袖；
撒网行动抓获七人；预定举行法庭听证

六男一女
因煽动被捕

出版商、律师
均在被拘押者之列

中国警方
要求引渡

据称六人曾受警告
不得进行
反对日本的活动

全国救国会七名所谓领袖于今日凌晨被公共租界和法租界警方一网打尽。中国官方人士称该组织反政府、颠覆政权，并对上海发生的多次示威活动负责，包括在日本棉纺厂煽动总罢工。

此次逮捕是应大上海市政府公安局的要求进行的，该局要求引渡这七人，以面对可能提出的危害国家安全罪指控。

同时展开突袭
警方于今日凌晨1时30分至3时之间同时展开突袭，在各自的住所逮捕了这七人。在公共租界被捕的人员如下：

李公朴先生，良友工业学校（由施良先生负责）校长，《......》出版商，留美归国学生。他在爱文义路524弄14号的家中被捕。在其家中发现一本日文书籍，内含四份传单，内容未予披露。

在法租界被捕
另外三名在法租界被捕的人员是：

曹大风先生，前《生活周刊》编辑，该白话杂志曾拥有中国最大的发行量，他因发表反政府言论被迫辞去编辑职务并出国游历。他也是一位知名的教育家。他在辣斐德路601弄4号的家中被捕。

章乃器博士，留美归国学生，前浙江实业银行副经理，前中国银行家信用调查局副总经理。他在德拉司特路（Rue Delastre）的家中被捕。

史良女士，七人中唯一的女性。她也是一名法律从业者，隶属于著名中国律师董康（音译）的律师事务所，董律师目前在北京讲学，并被提名为冀察政务委员会司法委员会委员。她曾在1931年9月18日反对日本占领沈阳的西门示威活动中受伤。警官翻墙进入她在辣斐德路辣斐德台1号的住所。

全部面临出庭
这七名被捕人员因广泛宣扬立即对日宣战而闻名，今日面临法庭审理。在公共租界被捕的四人今晨被带至江苏高等法院第二分院，法庭已清退记者及与案件无直接关系的人员。听证会闭门进行。经过长时间的庭审，据悉公安局要求引渡他们，随后听证会休庭至周三下午，四人获准由辩护律师签署个人保释书后保释。

另外三名在法租界被捕的人员将于今天下午面临江苏高等法院第三分院的审理。据悉，公安局也将提出类似的引渡请求。张唐佐（T. Z. Chang，音译）博士将出庭为史良女士和曹大风先生辩护。

行动受到监视
自广东和广西爆发颠覆性煽动活动以来，这七名所谓领袖的行动一直受到监视，他们也被指是一个名为“人民阵线”的政党的创始人。据悉，中国当局曾多次警告他们，不得响应广东和广西对日作战的要求而举行任何反日示威。

当日本棉纺厂发生劳资纠纷时，他们的行动再次受到严密监视。据信，指控他们将政治问题的油浇在劳资纠纷的火上，是他们被捕的直接原因。

这七人还被指控反对蒋介石将军，反对这位行政院院长兼军事委员会委员长，指责其试图在中国建立以自己为独裁者的类似政权。

（印：上海工部局 1936年11月23日）
（批：Del / def. 28/11）

February 8, 1939.
Afternoon Translation.

Morning Leader and other local newspapers (Chungking telegram):

THE CASE AGAINST THE NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS

Following the outbreak of hostilities in 1937,
Sung Chun-dz (沈儒), Wong Zao-dz (王造時), Tsang Nai-
chi (章乃器), Soo Chi-li (沙千里), Li Kung-poh (李公樸),
Tseu Tao-fun (鄒韜奮) and Sz Liang (史良 female), who
were charged by the Procuratorate of the Kiangsu High Court
with endangering the security of the Republic of China,
were released on bail. On the fall of Shanghai and
Nanking, the Kiangsu High Court could not exercise its
authority and the case has been suspended for more than
one year.

Recently, the Supreme Court decided to hand
the case to the Szechuen First Branch High Court. After
examining the documents, the Procurator of the Szechuen
High Court declared that the views of Sung Chun-dz
and the others were appropriate to the present national
policy of the country, so he withdrew the prosecution.
pages.zh:
1939年2月8日。
下午翻译。

《晨导报》及其他本地报纸（重庆电）：

针对救国会领袖的案件

继1937年战事爆发后，
沈钧儒、王造时、章乃
器、沙千里、李公樸、
邹韬奋和史良（女），此前被
江苏高等法院检察处以危害
中华民国安全罪起诉，
已获保释。随着上海和
南京沦陷，江苏高等法院无法行使
职权，该案已暂停一年多。

最近，最高法院决定将
此案移交四川第一分院高等法院。四川
高等法院检察官在审查文件后宣布，沈钧儒
等人的观点符合当前国家的
国策，因此撤销了起诉。

pages.en:
Dec.ber 2, 1937.
Afternoon Translation

Japanese troops in lootung and Chapei were
also transferred to the front on November 30 and December 1.
Units of Japanese soldiers stationed in the
warehouse of the Bank of Communications to the st of
Suchow Road Bridge and in the Foh Sing No. 1 Flour Mill.
West of Sinza Bridge, Chapei, left for the front at 2 p.m.
December 1.

Hwa Lei Wan Pao Morning Edition publishes the following articles:-

MOVEMENTS OF THE SEVEN NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS

The following information has been secured
on the whereabouts and movements of the seven national
salvation leaders, namely, Messrs Sung Chun-dz (沈钧儒),
Tsang Nai chi (章乃器), Tseu Tao-fun (邹韬奋), Wong Zao-
dz (王造时), Li Kung-poh (李公朴) and Soo Chi-lee(沙千里)
and Miss Sz Liang (史良) :-
After their liberation from prison, Mr. Sung
Chun-dz left for Nanking together with Messrs Li Kung-poh
and Soo Chi-lee. Shortly afterwards, Mr. Sung was
appointed member of the National Defence Assembly by the
National Government. Mr. Sung paid three different visits
to Shanghai since the hostilities on August 13 and disseminated
news to strengthen the determination of the people to the
war of resistance. Mr. Soo Chi-lee went to Nanking after
the fall of Shanghai and is assisting Mr. Sung.
Messrs Tsang Nai-chi and Tseu Tao-fun and
Miss Sz Liang left for Hongkong on November 27. Mr. Tsang
is held in high esteem by Mr. T.V. Soong for his profound
knowledge of the science of economics. He undertook
practical propaganda work for the Liberty Bonds Soliciting
Committee. It is said that Mr. Tsang is going to the
south to join the Ministry of Finance. He told friends
that he would continue his efforts for the popular front.
Owing to his connection with the "Livelihood"
(生活) and the "People's Livelihood" (大众生活),
Mr. Tseu Tao-fun is well known to Chinese youths.
Because of this, the "Ti Kong" ("Resistance") (抵抗), a
3-day periodical, had a wide circulation. Mr. Tseu
has already made preparations to publish the "Ti Kong" in
Hankow. The first issue of the "Ti Kong" appeared in
Hankow on the same day that the last issue was published
in Shanghai.
Immediately after the war of resistance
was commenced, Mr. Li Kung-poh proceeded to Shansi and
Suiyuan to make an inspection of the people's movement
there. He is now in Hankow editing a magazine entitled
"Chien Lin Monthly" (全民月刊).
Mr. Tsang Nai-chi is at present in Nanking
working with the People's Training Department. (This is
not the People's Training Department of the Central
Kuomintang Headquarters.)
It is not known what Miss Sz Liang will do
in Hankow.
pages.zh:
1937年12月2日。
下午翻译

驻虹口和闸北的日军也
于11月30日和12月1日调往前线。
驻扎在苏州路桥西侧交通银行仓库
以及闸北新闸桥西侧福新第一面粉厂的
日军部队，于12月1日下午2点
开赴前线。

《华雷晚报》早版刊登以下文章：-

七位救国会领袖的行踪

已获得关于七位救国会领袖，即沈钧儒先生、
章乃器先生、邹韬奋先生、王造时
先生、李公朴先生和沙千里
先生以及史良女士的下落和行踪的
以下信息：-
出狱后，沈钧儒先生与李公朴
先生和沙千里先生一同前往南京。不久之后，沈先生
被国民政府任命为国防参议会成员。自8月13日
战事爆发以来，沈先生三次访问
上海，传播消息以加强民众抗战的决心。沙千里
先生在上海沦陷后前往南京，正在协助沈先生。
章乃器先生、邹韬奋先生和
史良女士于11月27日前往香港。章先生因其深厚的
经济学知识而深受宋子文先生赏识。他承担了
公债劝募委员会的实际宣传工作。据说章先生将
南下加入财政部。他告诉朋友，他将继续为
人民阵线努力。
由于与《生活》
和《大众生活》的联系，
邹韬奋先生为中国青年所熟知。
因此，三日刊《抵抗》发行量很大。邹先生
已准备在汉口出版《抵抗》。《抵抗》的第一期
在汉口出版的那一天，正是最后一期在
上海出版的同一天。
抗战开始后不久，李公朴先生便前往山西
和绥远视察那里的民众运动。他目前在汉口
编辑一份名为《全民月刊》的杂志。
章乃器先生目前在南京
与民众训练部一起工作。（这不是国民党
中央总部民众训练部。）
尚不清楚史良女士将在
汉口做什么。

pages.en:
August 9, 1937

Leaders of local national salvation associations
- movements

Messrs. Sung Chun-dz, Li Kung-poh and Tsang Nai-chi,
three of the seven leaders of local national salvation
associations, who left Shanghai for Nanking on August 2,
to receive instructions from the National Government in
accordance with conditions of their release (Vide I.R.3/8/37)
returned here by train at 7.30 a.m. August 8. At 11 p.m.
the same day, they left the North Railway Station for
Nanking again.
pages.zh:
1937年8月9日

本地救国会领袖
- 行踪

本地救国会七位领袖中的三位，即沈钧儒先生、李公朴先生和章乃器
先生，于8月2日离开上海前往南京，
根据其释放条件接受国民政府的指示（见 I.R.3/8/37），
于8月8日上午7时30分乘火车返回此地。当晚11时，
他们再次离开北站前往南京。

pages.en:
August 9, 1937.
Morning Translation

Shun Pao and other local newspapers .-

LOCAL CULTURAL BODIES GIVE ENTHUSIASTIC WELCOME TO KWOH
MEI-SHU AND THREE NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS

At 2 p.m. yesterday, the Shanghai Cultural
Circles' National Extinction Aversion Association and other
various local cultural bodies held a meeting at the Shang
Wan Primary School (尚文小学) to accord a joint welcome to
Messrs. Kwoh Mei-sheh(郭沫若), Sung Chun-dz (沈钧儒),
Tsang Nai-chi (章乃器) and Li Kung-poh (李公朴). About
1,000 persons were present. Mr. Pan Kung-chan, Commissioner
of the Bureau of Social Affairs, presided.
Mr. Pan Kung-chan delivered an opening
speech, in the course of which he said :- "We are here
to-day to extend our warm welcome to Messrs. Kwoh Mei-sheh,
Sung Chun-dz, Tsang Nai-chi and Li Kung-poh. At this time
when our country is facing an acute alien aggression, every
one of us should cast aside his views and join hands together
to make up a strong body. If we still fail to harmonize
with one another in spirit and action, it will mean suicide
for our country. As our country is now at the cross-roads
of existence or ruin, there is no alternative for us but to
put up a war of resistance. A section of the people is
speculating whether the government will choose war or peace.
Such speculation is entirely out of place. The Chinese
people love peace; not only that, they love peace in the
Far-East as well as in the rest of the world. However, at
present even if we desire peace, others will not permit us
to enjoy it. Moreover, peace can only be assured under
conditions of equality. How can there be peace if there
is still difference? We must keep in mind that the present
war of resistance is to be carried on to the bitter end and
that it will affect all the people. Every one of us should
be prepared for the sacrifice and offer all he has to the
government. The cultural bodies should make the people
understand that the present war is not a childish play; it
is the life and death struggle of our nation. Ordinary
people should not doubt nor interfere with the government
in its handling of the situation or its tactics of war.
We must have full confidence in our government and leader
to handle the delicate situation. The cultural circles
should make preparations to organize and train the people,
so that the people may not be surprised when a great war c
commences."
In reply, Mr. Kwoh Mei-sheh said:- "I am
greatly honoured at the enthusiastic welcome given to me.
It is my opinion that words are unnecessary if a war of
resistance is to be put up. It depends entirely on action.
All of us, the cultural, agricultural, industrial and
commercial circles, should participate in the present war
of resistance. In the past we had no determination because
of our respect for life and property. I can say that we
shall thwart our enemy if all of us will readily sacrifice
our lives and property. We must do our best in the present
war of resistance under the guidance of our highest leader."
Speeches were also delivered by Messrs. Sung
Chun-dz, Tsang Nai-chi and Li Kung-poh, all of whom expressed
the hope that the government would organize the people and
that the people would be united in spirit and movement.
pages.zh:
1937年8月9日。
晨间译件

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

本地文化团体热烈欢迎郭沫若及三位救国会领袖

昨日下午2时，上海文化界救亡协会及其他各本地文化团体在尚文小学举行会议，联合欢迎郭沫若、沈钧儒、章乃器及李公朴诸先生。出席者约1000人。由社会局局长潘公展先生主持。

潘公展先生致开幕词，其间称：“吾人今日在此热烈欢迎各位郭沫若、沈钧儒、章乃器及李公朴先生。当此国家面临外敌侵略危急之秋，我辈均应摒弃成见，携手团结，组成坚强之整体。若在精神与行动上仍不能协和一致，则无异于国家自杀。今我国处于存亡绝续之十字路口，除抗战外别无他途。部分民众揣测政府将选择战或和。此种揣测完全不合时宜。中国人民爱好和平；不仅于此，亦爱好远东乃至世界其他各地之和平。然而，目前即便吾人渴望和平，他人亦不许吾人享受之。况且，和平唯有在平等条件下方能确保。若仍有差异，何来和平？吾人须铭记，此次抗战将进行到底，且将影响全体民众。我辈均应为牺牲做好准备，并将所有贡献予政府。文化团体应使民众明白，当前之战事并非儿戏；此乃我民族之生死搏斗。普通民众不应怀疑或干涉政府处理局势或其战争策略。吾人必须对政府及领袖处理微妙局势充满信心。文化界应着手准备组织并训练民众，以便大战爆发时民众不致惊慌。”

郭沫若先生答称：“承蒙热情欢迎，深感荣幸。鄙见以为，若欲抗战，空言无益。全赖行动。吾人文化、农、工、商各界，均应参与当前之抗战。过去因顾惜生命财产，缺乏决心。敢言若吾人均愿 readily 牺牲生命财产，必能挫败敌人。吾人须在最高领袖指导下，于当前抗战中竭尽全力。”

沈钧儒、章乃器及李公朴诸先生亦发表演说，均希望政府组织民众，并使民众在精神与行动上团结一致。

August 8, 1937. Morning Translation.
China Times and other local newspapers (Nanking Telegram):-

SUNG CHUN-DZ RETURNS TO SHANGHAI, BELIEVES NATIONAL DEFENCE NEED
TO RESIST

Since their arrival in Nanking several days
ago, Sung Chun-dz and the six others have called on
General Chiang Kai-shek, President of the Executive Yuan,
Dr. Wang Ching-wei, Chairman of the Central Political Council,
and other high Government officials to offer their views
on national salvation.

Sung Chun-dz will return to Shanghai on August 7,
but will come to the Capital again shortly. The other six
persons will stay in Nanking in the meantime.

Sung Chun-dz and the six others called on General
Feng Yu-hsiang, Vice Chairman of the Military Affairs
Commissioner, at 6 a.m. August 7 and had a talk with him on
the national salvation question. General Feng asked them
to take breakfast with him. At 4 p.m. the same day the
seven persons interviewed General Yen Hsi-shan, Chairman
of the Shansi Provincial Government, who is now in Nanking.

Sung Chun-dz left for Shanghai by the night
train on August 7 to attend to certain affairs, but will
return to the Capital on the morning of August 8. As
General Chiang Kai-shek last time received Sung Chun-dz
alone, he intends to grant a second interview to all the
seven persons on August 9 or 11.

Prior to his leaving, Sung Chun-dz made the
following statement: " I am favourably impressed with this
visit. All are determined to fight in a war of resistance.
The party, political and military leaders, especially,
are dealing with internal problems with magnanimity and
frankness. I am sure that every person in China will exert
his last ounce of strength to ensure our final victory
in a national war. We need not care too much about isolated
victories or defeats. Consolation should be administered
to those who lose as well as those who win in battles.
Anyone is a hero if he fights to the end."

Cultural Circles to Entertain to-day

The Shanghai Cultural Circles' National Extinction
Aversion Association will hold a tea party at 2 p.m. to-day
at the Shang Wen Primary School (尚文小学), Nantao, in
honour of Sung Chun-dz and Kwoh Mei-sheh (郭沫若), a noted
Chinese writer who recently returned from Japan. Views on
national salvation work will be exchanged.

Members of the Cultural Circles' National
Extinction Aversion Association are scheduled to hold an
informal meeting at the same time and place.

D.7108/17
（批：7108/17 8. 8. 37）

1937年8月8日。晨间译件。
《时事新报》及其他本地报纸（南京电）：-

沈钧儒返沪，认为国防需抵抗

沈钧儒等七人日前抵达南京后，曾拜谒行政院院长兼军事委员会委员长蒋介石将军、中央政治委员会主席汪精卫博士及其他政府高官，就救国事宜陈述意见。

沈钧儒将于8月7日返回上海，但不久将再次来到首都。其余六人届时将留驻南京。

8月7日上午6时，沈钧儒等七人拜谒了军事委员会副委员长冯玉祥将军，并就救国问题与其交谈。冯将军邀其共进早餐。同日下午4时，该七人会晤了时任南京的山西省政府主席阎锡山将军。

沈钧儒于8月7日晚乘夜车赴沪处理若干事务，但将于8月8日上午返回首都。鉴于蒋介石将军上次单独接见沈钧儒，他拟于8月9日或11日再次接见该七人。

临行前，沈钧儒发表如下声明：“此次访问令我印象深刻。各方均决心进行抗战。党、政、军领袖，尤其是以宽宏坦诚之态度处理内部问题。我相信，全中国之人必将竭尽最后之力，以确保民族战争之最终胜利。吾人不必过于计较一城一地之胜负。应对战场上的胜者与败者均予以慰勉。凡战斗到底者，皆为英雄。”

文化界今日设宴招待

上海文化界救亡协会将于今日下午2时在南市尚文小学举行茶话会，以欢迎沈钧儒及近期从日本归来的中国著名作家郭沫若。双方将就救亡工作交换意见。

文化界救亡协会会员计划于同一时间、同一地点举行非正式会议。

NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS CALL ON GENERAL CHIANG KAI -
SHEK AT NANKING

Chieng Kai-shek, President of the Executive Yuan and

救国会领袖在南京拜谒蒋介石将军

应行政院院长兼军事委员会委员长蒋介石将军之邀请，沈钧儒先生及其他六位救国会领袖于8月4日下午5时拜谒蒋将军，请示机宜，并就救国及防止亡国事宜陈述意见。预计他们在8月5日会晤中央宣传部部长赵厉生先生后，将返回上海。

August 4, 1937.
Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Pao (Nanking telegram):

MOVEMENTS OF NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS IN NANKING

Sung Chun-dz (沈儒) and the six other
leaders of national salvation bodies arrived here from
Shanghai at 7 a.m. August 3 and paid calls on the various
authorities and circles at the Capital.
Interviewed, Sung Chun-dz and the others
stated that they came here with a view to offering in the
capacity of citizens of China certain plans for aversion
of national extinction and discussing with the various
circles here steps that were to be taken at various places
in the work of national salvation.

Sung Chun-dz and the others called on Mr. Yih
Chu-shong (葉楚) of the Central Kuomintang Headquarters
on the morning of August 3 and had a long talk. On the
morning of August 4, they will interview General Chiang
Kai-shek asking for instructions.

《新闻报》（南京电）：

救国会领袖在南京之活动

沈钧儒（沈儒）及其他六位救亡团体领袖于8月3日上午7时从上海抵达此地，并拜谒了首都各界当局及人士。

接受采访时，沈钧儒等人表示，他们此行旨在以中国公民身份提出若干防止亡国之方案，并与此地各界讨论在各地开展救亡工作所应采取之步骤。

8月3日上午，沈钧儒等人拜谒了国民党中央总部叶楚伧先生，并进行了长谈。8月4日上午，他们将拜谒蒋介石将军，请示机宜。

August 3, 1937. Morning Translation.

National Herald and other local newspapers :-

IMPROVED MEASURES OF REGISTERING RICSHA COOLIES

The S.M.C. has never before enquired whether the public ricsha coolies registered with it actually engage in ricsha pulling. As a result many persons remained as registered ricsha coolies after they had taken up other professions, and ricsha owners began to find it difficult to get enough men to pull their ricshas.
At the instance of the ricsha owners, the S.M.C. at its last meeting approved a set of new measures for the registration of ricsha coolies. According to a letter sent to Dr. Ying Pei-ling (殷芝齡), Chief of the Special District Office of the Ricsha Owners' Association, by Mr. Phillips, Secretary of the S.M.C., the Council will take a new registration of ricsha coolies beginning from October 1. The coolies, the number of whom will be limited to four men to each ricsha, will be recommended by ricsha owners. Every regular coolie will be required to work at least fifteen shifts in a month, and reports will be made by ricsha owners as to the number of men fulfilling this requirement.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS LEAVE FOR NANKING

Upon receipt of a telegram from General Chiang Kai-shek yesterday, asking them to proceed to Nanking for a personal interview with him, Sung Chun-dz (沈鈞儒) and the six others who were released on bail from the Kiangsu High Court a few days ago left Shanghai for the capital by the 11 p.m. train. The seven persons will call on other high Government officials for instructions in addition to General Chiang. They will return to Shanghai after about a week.
Sung and the others were invited to tiffin at the Dzoh Yu Restaurant (蜀川菜館) by the Cultural Circles' Enemy-Resisting Support Association yesterday, but failed to attend owing to certain reasons.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

SMUGGLED GOODS BOYCOTT COMMITTEE TO DEAL WITH TRAITOROUS MERCHANTS

In compliance with a request of the Chamber of Commerce, the Shanghai Various Circles' Smuggled Goods Boycott Movement Committee will hold a meeting on August 4 to discuss effective measures for applying sanctions against traitorous merchants.

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：-

改进人力车夫登记措施

工部局此前从未核查向其登记之公共人力车夫是否实际从事拉车工作。结果，许多人在转行其他职业后仍保留注册人力车夫身份，导致人力车主开始发现难以招募足够之车夫。

应人力车主之请求，工部局在最近一次会议上批准了一套新的人力车夫登记措施。据工部局秘书菲利普斯先生致人力车主协会特区办事处主任殷芝龄博士的信函称，理事会将从10月1日起对人力车夫进行重新登记。车夫人数将限制为每辆人力车四人，由人力车主推荐。每名正规车夫每月至少需工作十五个班次，人力车主需报告符合此要求之人数。

《立报》及其他本地报纸：-

救国会领袖启程赴南京

昨日收到蒋介石将军电报，邀其前往南京亲自面谈后，数日前获江苏高等法院保释的沈钧儒及其他六人于当晚11时乘火车离开上海前往首都。该七人除拜谒蒋将军外，还将拜谒其他政府高官请示机宜。他们将在约一周后返回上海。

沈钧儒等人昨日受邀参加文化界抗敌后援会在蜀川菜馆举行的午宴，但因故未出席。

抵制私货委员会将处置奸商

Under the direction of the Chung Hwa Seamen's Special

National Salvation Leaders - leave for Nanking

The seven national salvation leaders, who arrived
in Shanghai from Soochow on August 1 (Vide I.R.2/8/37)

Labour

Japanese Cotton Mills - reduce working period

On August 1, 1937, the nine cotton mills of the
Naigai Wata Kaisha and the five Japan-China Cotton Mills
situated in the Western District, because of the hot
weather, commenced operating 6 days and 6 nights a week
instead of 6 days and seven nights a week. These
mills employ a total complement of some 20,000 workers.

Wei Kung Industrial Association (Chinese)
- suspension of operations

The Wei Kung Industrial Association, manufacturing
rubber shoes, 15 Wetmore Road, suspended operations on
July 31 owing to the lack of business. 270 workers are
affected.

中华海员特别党部 - 培训本地海员以备紧急时期服役

在位于南市中华路680号的中华海员特别党部指导下，受雇于各中国轮船公司的本地海员将接受紧急时期服役之训练。中华海员特别党部决定，自今日（8月3日）起，对参加训练之海员进行登记。

救国会领袖 - 启程赴南京

日本棉纺厂 - 缩短工时

National Salvation Movement - local leaders released

The seven national salvation leaders, who have been
under detention at Soochow since November 23, 1936, on a
charge of being reactionaries, were released on bail on
July 31. They arrived in Shanghai from Soochow by rail
on August 1.

A luncheon party to extend a welcome to the seven
leaders was held in the Dinty Moore Restaurant, 35 Ningpo
Road, at 1.15 p.m. August 1, when about one hundred
members of various local national salvation associations
and students of the Liang Zai Supplementary School were
present. During the course of the luncheon, the seven
leaders were called upon to give a speech and recounted
their experiences during their detention in Soochow.

At about 2 p.m. August 1, the luncheon party broke
up and the students of the Liang Zai School withdrew, while
the remainder stayed to dinner in the Restaurant.

救国运动——本地领袖获释

自1936年11月23日以来因被指控为反动分子而在苏州被拘留的七位救国领袖，于7月31日获保释。他们于8月1日乘火车从苏州抵达上海。

8月1日下午1时15分，在宁波路35号的丁蒂摩尔餐厅（Dinty Moore Restaurant）举行了一场欢迎七位领袖的午宴，约有百名当地各救国会成员及良宰补习学校（Liang Zai Supplementary School）的学生出席。午宴期间，七位领袖应邀发表讲话，讲述了他们在苏州被拘留期间的经历。

8月1日下午2时许，午宴结束，良宰学校的学生离去，其余人员则留在餐厅用晚餐。

pages.en:
August 2, 1937.                                  Morning Translation.

China Times and other local newspapers -

SEVEN NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS ARRIVE IN SHANGHAI:
SPEECHES DELIVERED

Sung Chun-dz (沈鈞儒), Li Jung-poh (李公),
Tseu Tao-fun (韜奮), Wong Zao-dz (王造時), Tsang Nai-chi
(章乃器), Soo Chi-li (沙千里) and Sz Liang (史良), who
were released on bail from the detention house of the
Kiangsu High Court at Soochow on July 31, arrived in
Shanghai at about 11 a.m. August 1. The seven national
salvation leaders will take a short rest in Shanghai
before proceeding to Nanking.
The following is a joint statement issued by
the seven persons upon their arrival in Shanghai :-

"Following our release from the detention
house, we sent a telegram to General Chiang Kai-shek
at Nanking asking for instructions. We have come
to Shanghai because we do not want to give our
relatives and friends at Soochow too much trouble.
As soon as we receive a reply from General Chiang, we
will leave for Nanking.
"With regard to the question of politics,
we have always advocated two things; viz., unification,
i.e. a united front formed by the whole Chinese people,
and resistance against Japan. A strong foundation
has now been laid for national unification, and resis-
tance has become the unanimous demand of the nation.
Consequently, we believe that, under the leadership
of the Government, we will be able to wage a
very glorious war of national emancipation, and win
the final victory. We must prepare ourselves to ful-
fill our duties as people of a nation if such a war
should come."

China Times :-

At 2 p.m. yesterday, Lawyer Chang Ts-niong
(張志讓) and more than a hundred others entertained Sung
Chun-dz and the six others to tiffin at Dinty Moore's
Restaurant, in the course of which the following addresses
were delivered:
Sung Chun-dz:- "We are gratified to know that
you have endeavoured to carry on your work despite our
detention. We are not particularly elated at our present
release. We will never change our object, but will
stand on the front of national emancipation as before.
Peiping and Tientsin have been lost and many of our fellow
countrymen have made sacrifices under the iron heels of
our enemy. We must be determined and strive to get back
Peiping and Tientsin. Our people are now strongly united
and everyone, with the exception of traitors, is advocating
resistance against the enemy."
Wong Zao-dz:- "I hope all patriotic youths will
stand together and resist the enemy."
Tseu Tao-fun:- "Only the public receive our
consideration, not the individual. Our national salvation
movement will live on for ever. We will struggle as
long as we are alive."
pages.zh:
1937年8月2日。                                  晨间译件。

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸——

七位救国领袖抵沪：发表演说

沈钧儒、李公朴、邹韬奋、王造时、章乃器、沙千里和史良，这七人于7月31日从苏州江苏高等法院看守所获保释，于8月1日上午11时许抵达上海。这七位救国领袖将在上海稍作休息，随后前往南京。
以下是七人抵达上海时发表的联合声明：

“我们在离开看守所后，曾致电南京的蒋介石将军请示。我们来到上海，是不想给苏州的亲友增添太多麻烦。一旦收到蒋将军的回复，我们将立即启程前往南京。
“关于政治问题，我们一直主张两点：即统一，也就是由全体中国人民组成统一战线；以及抗日。现在国家统一的基础已经奠定，抗日已成为全国一致的要求。因此，我们相信，在政府的领导下，我们将能够进行一场非常光荣的民族解放战争，并取得最终胜利。如果这样的战争爆发，我们必须做好准备，履行作为国民的职责。”

《字林西报》：

昨日下午2时，张志让律师等一百余人在丁蒂摩尔餐厅宴请沈钧儒及其他六人进午餐，席间发表了以下讲话：
沈钧儒：“得知在我们被拘留期间，诸位仍努力开展工作，我们深感欣慰。对于目前的获释，我们并不特别感到高兴。我们的目标绝不会改变，我们将一如既往地站在民族解放的前线。北平和天津已经沦陷，许多同胞在敌人的铁蹄下牺牲。我们必须下定决心，努力收复北平和天津。我国人民现在紧密团结，除了汉奸之外，所有人都在主张抗日。”
王造时：“我希望所有爱国青年团结一致，抵抗敌人。”
邹韬奋：“我们考虑的只有公众，而非个人。我们的救国运动将永存。只要我们还活着，就会奋斗下去。”

August 1, 1937.
Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS BAILED OUT

Sung Chun-dz (沈钧儒), Li Kung-poh (李公朴),
Tseu Tao-fun (邹韬奋), Wong Zao-dz (王造时), Tsang Nai-
chi (章乃器), Sbo Chi-li (沙千里) and Sz Liang (史良),
who had been held in the Kiangsu High Court at Soochow
for some eight months on suspicion of endangering the
Republic of China, were released at 5 p.m. yesterday on
bail of $200 each furnished by Mr. Li Kung-yuan (李根源)
and six other prominent residents in Soochow. The Chief
of the Detention House personally saw them off. A group
of civilians who waited outside the Detention House shouted
slogans welcoming their release and advocating resistance
against Japan for the salvation of the nation.
The seven leaders will proceed to Nanking
at 1 a.m. August 1 by train to receive advice from the
authorities. They will remain in the Capital for a week
after which they will come to Shanghai.
Lo Tsing (罗青), another accused, was also
bailed out yesterday.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

CHINESE WORKERS IN JAPANESE FACTORY LEAVE SERVICE

In view of the attack on the North by the
Japanese and the loss of Peiping and Tientsin, the entire
body of Chinese workers numbering 191 hands in the employ
of the Asia Steel Trade Factory (亚细亚钢业厂), a Japanese
concern, 379 Hochien Road, in the Eastern District, are
not willing to work for the Japanese. On the morning of
July 31, they declared a "tai-kung" strike and later
left the factory.

1937年7月1日。
晨间译件。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

救国领袖获保释

沈钧儒、李公朴、邹韬奋、王造时、章乃器、沙千里和史良，因涉嫌危害中华民国而在苏州江苏高等法院被羁押约八个月，昨日（注：指6月30日）下午5时，由李根源先生及苏州其他六位知名人士各提供200元保金后获释。看守所所长亲自为他们送行。一群在看守所外等候的民众高呼口号，欢迎他们获释，并主张抗日救国。
这七位领袖将于8月1日凌晨1时乘火车前往南京，听取当局的意见。他们将在首都停留一周，之后前来上海。
另一名被告罗青也于昨日获保释。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：

日资工厂华工离职

鉴于日军进攻华北以及北平和天津的沦陷，位于东区河间路379号的日商亚细亚钢业厂雇佣的191名华工全体不愿再为日本人工作。7月31日上午，他们宣布“怠工”罢工，随后离开工厂。

1937年6月28日。

本地救国分子的示威活动
6月27日上午9时30分，约六百名主要由学生和工人组成的人员出现在罗伯特神父路（Rue Pere Robert）附近的中国管辖区域，并排成游行队伍。他们手持党旗和国旗，以及三条写有“上海各界救国联合会”、“和平请愿”和“要求释放目前被拘押的七位救国领袖”字样的白布横幅，向西朝枫林桥方向行进，目的是向当地党部请愿，但在肇嘉浜路（Route de Zikawei）和阿尔贝特国王路（Rue du Roi Albert）交界处附近被中国警察拦阻。随后，他们推选了三名代表向当地党部请愿。其他人则留在原地，唱救国歌曲。

在集会期间，上海法学院的彭文应教授和张定夫教授告知与会者，由于是星期日，当地党部没有负责官员在场，中国警察将转达他们关于

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS SUBMIT SECOND REPLY TO CHARGE :
CASE TO RE-OPEN JUNE 25.

The case against Sung Chun-dz (沈钧儒), Wong
Zao-dz (王造时), Li Kung-poh (李公朴), Soo Chi-li (沙千里),
Tsang Nai-chi (章乃器), Tseu Tao-fun (邹韬奋) and Sz Liang
(史良) will be re-opened at 9 a.m. June 25 at the Kiangsu
High Court. On June 22 the seven accused submitted a second
reply to the charge against them.
The following is the text of the second reply:-
"Whereas the charge of offence against the
State laid against the accused is of a political nature, the
political opinion and advocacy of the accused naturally should
form a subject of attention by the Court. In our first reply,
we have confined our attention to what was said in the text
of the charge, and have consequently failed to deal system-
atically with this point. We therefore submit this reply
now as a supplement to the first one.
"The National Salvation Association was first
promoted at the end of 1935 when North China was in an
extremely serious state and a separation movement was likely
to occur at any time. The general advocacy was then to put a
stop to the separation movement and to unify the people's
front, with the offering of resistance to Japan as the highest
object. The slogan for the 'bringing about of an unified
enemy-resisting authority' was based on these demands. Its
idea was to concentrate the forces of resistance against Japan
under the leadership of the Central Authorities and not to
reorganize the Government. Mere common sense will show that
the accused, who advocated cessation of internal strife and
resistance against alien invasion, could not have had the
intention of extending the internal conflicts and wasting
the national strength by suggesting the reorganization of
the Government.

以下是第二次答辩状的全文：
“鉴于对被告提出的危害国家罪指控具有政治性质，被告的政治观点和主张自然应成为法庭关注的主题。在我们的第一次答辩中，我们仅局限于指控文本中的内容，因此未能系统地处理这一点。因此，我们现在提交此答辩状，作为对第一次答辩的补充。
“救国会最初是在1935年底 promoted（提倡/发起）的，当时华北局势极其严峻，分裂运动随时可能发生。当时的普遍主张是制止分裂运动，统一人民阵线，并以抗日为最高目标。‘促成统一抗敌政权’的口号正是基于这些要求。其理念是在中央当局的领导下集中抗日力量，而非改组政府。常识表明，主张停止内战和抵抗外来侵略的被告，不可能有意通过建议改组政府来扩大内部冲突和浪费国力。

NICHI-NICHI

JAPANESE AUTHORITIES TO SUPPRESS HEROIN DEALERS

The Chinese authorities are adopting effective measures in the suppression of opium smokers and heroin dealers and they are obtaining satisfactory results.

In view of the fact that quite a number of Japanese subjects, mostly Koreans, in the North are engaged in the heroin business, the Japanese authorities are reported to have decided to adopt effective measures to suppress them. As a result, Chinese, White Russians, Koreans and Japanese who are dealing in heroin in the North are retreating to Shanghai. In view of this, the local Japanese Consular Police are reported to have decided to co-operate with the Chinese Police Bureau, the S.M.P. and the French Police to adopt severe repressive measures. At present persons coming to Shanghai by train or steamer are liable to arrest if suspected. The majority of the arrested persons are reported to be Koreans. Persons charged for the first time with dealing in heroin are fined and deported to Korea and persons who have previous convictions on a similar charge are sentenced to imprisonment. However, many of those who were sent to Korea are coming back to Shanghai because they cannot make a living there. Therefore the Japanese authorities are now considering suitable measures to deal with them.

《日日新闻》

日本当局将镇压海洛因贩子

中国当局正在采取有效措施镇压鸦片吸食者和海洛因贩子，并取得了令人满意的结果。

鉴于在华北地区有相当数量的日本臣民（主要是朝鲜人）从事海洛因生意，据报道，日本当局已决定采取有效措施予以镇压。因此，在华北从事海洛因交易的中国人、白俄、朝鲜人和日本人正撤退至上海。鉴于此，据报道，当地日本领事警察已决定与中国警察局、上海公共租界警务处（S.M.P.）及法国警察合作，采取严厉的镇压措施。目前，乘火车或轮船抵达上海的人员若受怀疑，可能会被逮捕。据报道，被捕者中大多数为朝鲜人。首次被控贩卖海洛因者将被罚款并驱逐至朝鲜，而有类似前科者则被判监禁。然而，许多被送往朝鲜的人因无法在那里谋生而返回上海。因此，日本当局目前正在考虑采取适当措施来应对他们。

NIPPO

THE BAN ON JAPANESE FILMS

One named Kawanami contributes
the following article to the Nippo under the above heading:-
I extend my sympathy to the
Towa Theatre which was prohibited from exhibiting a Japanese
news film entitled "8,000 km of national defence line".
I agree with the action taken by the authorities who fear
that trouble might take place on the exhibition of such
a film, in view of the international situation in the
Settlement, but I am very sorry that we Japanese residents
are unable to view such a suitable film as we need a
knowledge of defence at this time of crisis.
I am displeased with the Municipal
administrative policy in connection with the ban placed on
the above mentioned film and the question of the film
entitled "New Earth". I do not know whether or not the
Chinese authorities asked the S.M.C. to interfere with
the exhibition of Japanese films, but we Japanese suffer
loss of dignity because although we enjoy extraterritorial
rights in the International Settlement, exhibition of
Japanese films at a Japanese theatre is interfered with.
In Chinese controlled territory films or plays which
instigate anti-Japanism, I believe, have been exhibited
and staged. Some may suggest that we should show the
magnanimous attitude of a great nation. In that case the
Chinese people should show a similar attitude. However
it is now not a question of attitude but of dignity. I
do not declare that the S.M.C. is deliberately supporting
the Chinese people and listening to their every want,
nevertheless the S.M.C. is in a position to request the
Chinese people to reflect.
Our Japanese authorities need
to pay attention to this matter. Why are we residents
unable to view our own film which is produced as part of
our national policy?

NICHI-NICHI

SANCTITY OF LAW SHOULD BE OBSERVED IN DEALING WITH
CASE OF NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS

The Nichi-Nichi publishes
the following comment:-
The attention of foreigners
as well as Chinese is now focussed on the trial of the
seven arrested leaders of the national salvation movement.
The Chinese people regard these men as heroes because of

they are now undergoing trial on a serious charge.
The members of the National
Salvation Association, under the leadership of the prisoners,
directed the strike of the Japanese cotton mills last year,
thereby rendering heavy damage to the mills, disturbing public
peace and order and injuring Sino-Japanese relations. For

《日本日报》

禁止日本电影

一位名为川浪（Kawanami）的人士在《日本日报》上以上述标题 contributed 以下文章：
我对东和剧场被禁止放映题为《八千公里国防线》的日本新闻片表示同情。
我赞同当局出于对租界国际局势的考量，担心放映此类影片可能引发事端而采取的行动，但我非常遗憾，我们日本居民在此危机时刻亟需了解国防知识，却无法观看如此合适的影片。
我对工部局在上述影片禁令以及题为《新土》的影片问题上的行政政策感到不满。我不知道中国当局是否要求工部局（S.M.C.）干涉日本电影的放映，但我们日本人的尊严受损，因为尽管我们在公共租界享有治外法权，但在日本剧院放映日本电影却受到干涉。
我相信，在中国控制的领土上，煽动反日情绪的电影或戏剧一直在上映和上演。有人可能建议我们应该展现大国的宽宏大量。如果是那样，中国人民也应表现出类似的态度。然而，现在的问题不是态度问题，而是尊严问题。我并非宣称工部局故意支持中国人民并听从他们的每一个要求，尽管如此，工部局处于可以要求中国人民反思的地位。
我们日本当局需要关注此事。为何我们居民无法观看作为我们国家政策一部分而制作的属于我们自己的电影？

June 14, 1937. Morning Translation

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

PROCEEDINGS IN NATIONAL SALVATION TRIAL STAYED : ACCUSED
ASK FOR CHANGE OF JUDGES

Proceedings in the case against Sung Chun-dz
(沈鈞儒), Tsang Nai-chi (章乃器), Tseu Tao-fun (鄒韜奮),
Wong Zao-dz (王造時), Li Kung-poh (李公樸), Soo Chi-li
(沙千里) and Sz Liang (史良), which were to have been
resumed on the afternoon of June 12, were stayed as a result
of an application made by the accused for the withdrawal of
the presiding judge and two other judges. Announcement of
the stay was made by Presiding Judge Fang (方) at 2 p.m.
June 12, and the accused were ordered to be returned to
their detention house pending a ruling to be handed down
by the Kiangsu High Court.
The following is the text of the application made
by Sung Chun-dz and the others :-
"We, the applicants, are charged with offences
against the Republic. The case commenced on June 11.
"Prior to the hearing, the Court placed strict
restrictions on persons who desired to attend, each of them
being questioned, registered and then issued with a ticket.
These measures should have been quite sufficient to preserve
good order in Court, yet the Court later prohibited all
persons from attending the hearing, and although the Presiding
Judge announced after the commencement of the hearing that
the reason for the prohibition was to prevent any possible
harm to peace and order, he did not point out any concrete
fact the occurrence of which after the issuance of the
tickets might have given rise to the apprehension. It
might have been reasonably suspected, therefore, that the
hearing of the case was to be conducted in such a way as
to render it necessary to prevent the public from having
knowledge of the proceedings.
"Following the questioning of the accused by the
Presiding Judge in regard to the facts of the case, the
accused and their defending counsel raised more than twenty
points advantageous to the accused in regard to the facts
mentioned in the charge, and requested the Court to
investigate them. Presiding Judge Fang looked at the
other two Judges, Wang (王) and Cheng (鄭), as if to give
them a hint, and immediately overruled the request without
giving any consideration to it. In some cases he even made
no reply, but waved his hand as a sign. When the defence
counsel requested the Court to give the matter careful
consideration, they were prevented from speaking on the
ground of insufficient time. Such an attitude and method
of hearing cannot be regarded as compatible with the
provisions of Article 8 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
"Cases of offences against the Republic, according
to law, come under the jurisdiction of the High Court;
consequently this is in fact the only chance for the accused
to defend themselves. Prior to the institution of the
prosecution, the procurator conducted enquiries for four
months and submitted as many as ten items of evidence. The
Court, however, takes utterly no notice of any items of
evidence submitted by the accused which would be of importance

1937年6月14日。晨间译件

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

救国会审判程序中止：被告申请法官回避

针对沈钧儒、章乃器、邹韬奋、王造时、李公朴、沙千里和史良的案件原定于6月12日下午恢复审理，但因被告申请主审法官及另外两名法官回避，审理程序中止。方姓主审法官于6月12日下午2时宣布中止审理，并命令将被告送回看守所，等候江苏高等法院作出裁决。
以下是沈钧儒等人提交的申请书全文：
“我们申请人被指控犯有危害民国罪。本案于6月11日开始审理。
“在开庭前，法庭对希望旁听的人员实施了严格限制，每人均需经过询问、登记，然后发给旁听证。这些措施本应足以维持法庭秩序，但法庭后来禁止所有人旁听庭审。虽然主审法官在开庭后宣布，禁止旁听是为了防止任何可能危害和平与秩序的行为，但他并未指出在发出旁听证之后发生的任何具体事实足以引起这种担忧。因此，有理由怀疑，本案的审理方式使得有必要防止公众了解诉讼过程。
“在主审法官就案件事实讯问被告后，被告及其辩护律师就起诉书所述事实提出了二十多项有利于被告的意见，并请求法庭进行调查。方姓主审法官看向另外两名法官，即王姓法官和郑姓法官，似乎在给他们暗示，随即未经任何考量便驳回了该请求。在某些情况下，他甚至不予答复，仅以挥手示意。当辩护律师请求法庭仔细考虑此事时，他们以时间不足为由被禁止发言。此种态度和审理方法不能被视为符合《刑事诉讼法》第八条之规定。
“根据法律，危害民国罪案件由高等法院管辖；因此，这实际上是被告自我辩护的唯一机会。在提起公诉之前，检察官进行了为期四个月的调查，并提交了多达十项证据。然而，法庭完全无视被告提交的任何对其辩护重要且

and advantage to the accused in their defence and which
are not difficult to investigate. This shows that the
Court is prejudiced and will only accept the opinions
contained in the charge which are disfavouable to the
accused. A lawful and just judgment under such circumstances
is impossible.
"As there now exist the circumstances mentioned in
Article 18, Section 2, of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
application is made in accordance with Article 20, Section
1 of the Code for the withdrawal of Presiding Judge Fang
and Judges Wang and Cheng. In accordance with Section 2
of the same Article, the overruling of the request for
investigations to be made, as mentioned in the record of
proceedings at the hearing on June 11, is hereby submitted
as the reason for this application. The Court is also
requested to stay the proceedings of the case in accordance
with Article 22 of the Code of Criminal Procedure."

Statement by President of Kiangsu High Court.

In an interview with newspaper reporters, Mr. Chu
Zu-sung (朱樹聲), President of the Kiangsu High Court, made
the following statement :-
"The proceedings in the case, in which Sung Chun-dz
and six others are charged with offence against the Republic,
have been suspended since the receipt of the application made
by the seven accused for the withdrawal of the Judges. The
application will be deliberated and decided upon by the
Judges conducting the case. If the Judges, as a result of
their deliberation, consider that the accused's application
is justified, other Judges will then be appointed to try the
case. If the Judges, as a result of their deliberation,
regard the application as unreasonable, the matter will be
referred for further deliberation by other Judges who will
make a final decision. The proceedings against Loo Tsing
(羅青), Oo Zoong-kao (伍頌高) and Koo Liu-ching (顧聲)
have also been suspended. The matter will probably be
decided in about three days after which a date will be
fixed for hearing of the case."

A Sidelight of the events at the trial.

The trial of the case against Sung Chun-dz and
others was resumed at 2 p.m. June 12. The accused were
brought to the Court from their detention house by motor
car in the forenoon and the streets through which they
passed were heavily guarded by gendarmes and police. Owing
to the rain, very few people attended the Court to watch
the trial. There was no one present in the seats reserved
for the lawyers.
The Presiding Judge first ordered the Court clerk
to read out the notes of the statements taken at the hearing
of the preceding day. When this was done, Sung Chun-dz
requested to be allowed to read the notes. He asked for
many corrections of his statement.
The Court retired at 3.20 p.m.

且不难调查的证据。这表明法庭存在偏见，只接受起诉书中对被告不利的观点。在这种情况下，不可能作出合法公正的判决。
“鉴于目前存在《刑事诉讼法》第十八条第二款所述情形，现依据该法第二十条第一款申请方姓主审法官以及王姓和郑姓法官回避。依据同条第二款，现将6月11日庭审记录中提到的驳回调查请求一事，作为本次申请的理由。同时请求法庭依据《刑事诉讼法》第二十二条中止本案诉讼程序。”

江苏高等法院院长的声明。

江苏高等法院院长朱树声先生在接受记者采访时发表如下声明：
“沈钧儒等七人被控危害民国罪一案，自收到七名被告提出的法官回避申请以来，诉讼程序已暂停。该申请将由审理本案的法官审议并作出决定。如果法官经审议认为被告的申请合理，则将指派其他法官审理此案。如果法官经审议认为该申请不合理，则将提交其他法官进一步审议，由他们作出最终决定。针对罗青、伍颂高和顾声的诉讼程序也已暂停。此事可能在约三天后作出决定，随后将确定开庭审理日期。”

审判事件的侧面报道。

沈钧儒等人案件的审判于6月12日下午2时恢复。被告于上午由汽车从看守所押送至法院，沿途街道由宪兵和警察严密守卫。由于下雨，前往法院旁听审判的人很少。律师席上无人就座。
主审法官首先命令书记官宣读前一天庭审记录的笔录。宣读完毕后，沈钧儒请求允许他阅读笔录。他要求对自己的陈述进行多处更正。
法庭于下午3时20分休庭。

June 12, 1937.
Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers:

CASE AGAINST NATIONAL SALVATION ASSOCIATION LEADERS
OPENS

At 2 p.m. June 11, the Kiangsu High Court commenced the hearing of the case against Sung Chun-dz (沈鈞儒), Tsang Nai-ohi (章乃器), Tseu Tao-fun (鄒韜奮), Wong Zao-dz (王造時), Li Kung-poh, (李公樸), Soo Chi-li (沙千里) and Sz Liang (史良), who were arrested by the Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government with the assistance of the Police of the International Settlement and French Concession in November last on a charge of endangering the internal security of the Republic of China.
Strict precautionary measures were adopted during the hearing of the case and in all about 300 gendarmes and policemen were on duty inside and outside the Court. With the exception of newspaper reporters and two relatives of each of the seven accused, nobody was permitted to witness the proceedings.
Messrs. Eugene Y.B. Kiang (江一平), Zing Lien-kwei (秦聯奎), Chen Ding-sai (陳霆銳) and sixteen other lawyers representing the seven accused were present.
After the reading over of the text of the charge sheet by the Procurator, Mr. Fang Ven (方聞), the Presiding Judge, ordered six accused to withdraw from the Court and commenced to interrogate Sung Chun-dz.

Sung Chun-dz's Statement

The following questions were put by the Presiding Judge to Sung Chun-dz:-
Q. How was the National Salvation Association formed?
A. After consideration had been given to local conditions in the various districts, steps were taken to organize University Professors' National Salvation Associations, Students' National Salvation Associations and Various Circles National Salvation Federations. This being done, the Various Circles National Salvation Federations in the various districts again appointed delegates to form a Various Circles National Salvation Federation.
Q. What was the procedure to become a member of the Association?
A. All those who were willing to resist Japan could participate.
Q. To which national salvation association did you belong?
A. The Cultural Circles National Salvation Association.
Q. When was the All-China National Salvation Association inaugurated?
A. It was inaugurated on May 31 last year.
Q. How many district delegates participated?
A. About 70 delegates from various districts in North China, South China and the Yangtsze Valley.
Q. How was the All-China National Salvation Association formed?
A. It had an Executive Committee of 41 members who, however, had not yet been appointed at that time. The Executive Committee in turn appointed a Standing Committee.

1937年6月12日。
晨间译件。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

救国会领袖案开庭

6月11日下午2时，江苏高等法院开始审理沈钧儒、章乃器、邹韬奋、王造时、李公朴、沙千里和史良一案。上述七人于去年十一月在上海市政府警察局以及公共租界和法租界警方的协助下被捕，罪名是危害中华民国内部安全。
庭审期间采取了严格的预防措施，法院内外共有约300名宪兵和警察执勤。除新闻记者及七名被告各自的两位亲属外，任何人不得旁听诉讼程序。
代表七名被告出庭的有江一平、秦联奎、陈霆锐等律师共十九人。
检察官宣读起诉书全文后，主审法官方闻命令六名被告退庭，并开始讯问沈钧儒。

沈钧儒的陈述

主审法官向沈钧儒提出以下问题：
问：救国会是如何成立的？
答：在考虑了各地区的地方情况后，采取了组织大学教授救国会、学生救国会和各界救国联合会的步骤。在此基础上，各地区的各界救国联合会又推选代表组成全国各界救国联合会。
问：成为会员的程序是什么？
答：所有愿意抗日的人均可参加。
问：您属于哪个救国会？
答：文化界救国会。
问：全国救国会何时成立？
答：于去年5月31日成立。
问：有多少地区代表参加？
答：来自华北、华南和长江流域各地区的约70名代表。
问：全国救国会是如何组成的？
答：它有一个由41名成员组成的执行委员会，但当时尚未任命。执行委员会随后任命了一个常务委员会。
