November 24, 1936.
Morning Translation.

"At about 10 a.m. yesterday (November 19)
a pedestrian, an old man of more than 70 years of age,
was knocked down at the corner of Pingliang and Glen
Roads by a motor car (licence number unknown) which
was moving at a high speed. Upon finding that he had
caused an accident, the driver drove off at a high
speed. Later, a post duty policeman conveyed the
injured man to the Sacred Heart Hospital where the man
succumbed to his injuries soon after arrival."
It is known to everybody that there is a Police
Station at the corner of Pingliang and Glen Roads. Moreover,
the accident occurred opposite the Station. The place is
not an isolated locality. It is customary to have a
policeman on duty at the front gate of Police Station; the
accident happened at about 10 o'clock in the morning; yet
the motor car was driven off unnoticed after the accident.
I am of the opinion that an explanation should
be demanded from the Police authorities. We should not
overlook the matter just because the deceased was a poor
old man, for it is a case that concerns not only the
deceased but the general public as well.

上午译件。

“昨天（11月19日）上午10点左右，
一名70多岁的老年行人，
在平凉路（Pingliang Road）与格兰路（Glen Road）拐角处，
被一辆高速行驶的汽车（车牌号不详）撞倒。司机发现
造成事故后，高速驾车逃离。随后，一名执勤警察将伤者
送往圣心医院（Sacred Heart Hospital），该男子抵达医院后不久
便因伤身亡。”
众所周知，平凉路与格兰路拐角处有一个警察局。此外，
事故发生在警察局对面。该地并非偏僻之处。警察局
前门通常有警察执勤；事故发生在上午10点左右；然而
肇事汽车却在无人注意的情况下驶离。
我认为应向警方当局要求解释。我们不应
因为死者是一位贫穷的老人而忽视此事，因为这不仅关系到
死者，也关系到广大公众。

Nov mber 25, 1936. Morning Translation.

Li Kuo Tseng (李國珍), Ngoh Soong (鄂森), Li Vung Chi
(李文杰) and Chen Tse Keo (陳克皋), lawyers for the defence,
were present.
The case against Messrs Li Kung Pu, Sung Chun
Shih and Wang Chao Shih was first dealt with. Presiding
Judge You stated that the case had originally been fixed
for hearing in the afternoon of November 25, but the present
hearing was being held because of the discovery of new facts.
The representative of the Public Safety Bureau
requested the extradition of these three accused.
The Procurator requested the Judges to decide
the application according to law.
The Court then retired to consider the
application. When the Judges resumed their seats in Court,
they handed down a ruling that as Messrs Li Kung Pu, Sung
Chun Shih and Wang Chao Shih did not live within the limits
of the International Settlement, the question of extradition
did not arise; therefore, the Public Safety Bureau should
take up the matter with the S.M.C.
The three accused were then taken back by the
Settlement Police.
The case against Mr. Soo Chi Lien was next
heard. The Court remanded the case to 2 p.m. November 25
and ordered that he be temporarily detained at the Police
Station.

Proceedings in the Third Branch of High Court

In the meantime, the Third Branch of the
Kiangsu High Court had also immediately issued summons for
the appearance of Miss Sze Liang, Messrs Chow Tao Feng and
Chang Nan Chi before midnight November 24/25.
The case was heard at 6 p.m. by Presiding Judge
Wu Ting Chi (吳廷璣) and Judges Wong (王) and Liao (廖) in
the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court. Mr. Chow Tao
Feng appeared in company with Mr. Sung Tso Chi (孫祖基),
his lawyer, Miss Sze Liang and Mr. Chang Nan Chi did not
appear but were represented by Mr. Tong Hwa (唐華) and Mr.
Chang Tse Niang (張子讓).
After questioning Mr. Chow Tao Feng about his
age and native place, Presiding Judge Wu ordered him to
be temporarily detained at the office of the Judicial Police.
Lawyers Tong and Chang were ordered by the Court to produce
the accused Miss Sze and Mr. Chang Nan Chi before midnight.
At about midnight, the Third Branch of the
Kiangsu High Court held a special session when Mr. Chow
Tao Feng appeared in company with Mr. Sung Tso Chi, his
lawyer. Mr. Chang Nan Chi also was present with his two
lawyers, Mr. Chang and Mr. Tong.
As the arrangements for shop security have
not yet been completed, Mr. Chow Tao Feng was ordered to
be detained for the time being.
The Court then questioned Mr. Chang Nan Chi.
Owing to insufficient time, Mr. Chang could find only one
shop security and as he could not find another shop security
he was also detained.
As Miss Sze Liang was at Soochow attending
to certain legal affairs, the Judge instructed two lawyers
Mr. Chang and Mr. Tong to produce her before 4 p.m. November 25.
The Court rose at 12.30 a.m. November 25.
The accused Chang and Chow are being temporarily held in
the Detention House.

接下来审理针对沙千里先生的案件。法庭将案件延期至11月25日下午2点，并命令将其暂时拘押在警察局。

To ... and other local newspapers :-

WITHIN THE CAUTIONARY MEASURES IN CHINESE CONTROLLED TERRITORY

Fearing that unlawful elements may take
advantage of the bandit suppression campaign in Suiyuan
Province to spread rumours and disturb the peace and order,
the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters,
the Peace Preservation Corps, the Public Safety Bureau and
the Force Maintenance Committee have issued instructions
that winter precautionary measures be adopted immediately.
The Branches and the Police Stations
of the Public Safety Bureau have been ordered to search
all suspicious-looking pedestrians. Special attention
will be paid to ships in the Whangpoo River and to boats
in the Soochow Creek. Co-operation will be effected
with the Chinese Authorities in districts adjacent to
Shanghai.
According to information secured by our
reporter from local Chinese Authorities, cases of robbery
and theft in Chinese controlled territory have decreased
by 80% as compared with last year.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE ARREST OF MR. SUNG CHUN SHIH AND OTHERS

On December 1, Messrs Sung Chun Shih (沈鈞儒),
Wong Chao Shih (王造時), Chow Tao Peng (鄒奮), Cheng Nan
Chi (章乃器), Li Hung Pu (李樸) and Soo Chi Lien (沙千里)
were still detained at the Public Safety Bureau.
On the evening of November 30, Mr. Li Dah
Chao (李大釗), Chief of the First Department of the Shanghai
City Government, and Mr. Huang Hwa (黃華), Chief of the
Third Department of the Public Safety Bureau, had a
conversation with the six men.
Miss Sze Liang (史良) is still at large and
no information has been obtained as to her whereabouts.
It is reported that her mother has been sick for two days.
Lawyers Chang Tse Niang (張志讓) and Tong Hwo
(唐豪), the guarantors of Miss Sze Liang, were summoned
to the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court yesterday
afternoon. The Judge ordered them to furnish security
pending investigation.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao :-

On the morning of December 1, the Public
Safety Bureau held a conference to discuss certain affairs.
As the rooms in which Messrs Sung Chun Shih, Wong Chao
Shih and four others are being held are close to the
conference room, General Tsai, Commissioner of the Public
Safety Bureau, prohibited visitors that morning. The
Public Safety Bureau is still investigating the case against
the men.
On the afternoon of December 1, Mr. Tu Yuet
Sen (杜月笙), Chairman of the Shanghai District Association,
Mr. Wong Shiao Lai (王曉籟), Chairman of the Chinese Chamber
of Commerce, Mr. Loh Ching Sz (陸京士) and others interviewed
the six men. It is reported that Messrs Wong and Tu
are soliciting assistance from various authorities on
behalf of the men. As the authorities have now a better
understanding of the activities of the six prisoners,
good treatment is being accorded to them and it is hoped
that they will repent.
During the interview on December 1, Messrs
Wong Shiao Lai and Tu Yuet Sen advised the six men to
proceed to Mokanshan or Pootoo for a rest after their case
has been settled.
The six men rise at six o'clock every morning
and have breakfast at 7 a.m. The meal consists of bread,
milk and black tea or congee. Tiffin is served at noon
and five courses and a soup are provided. Supper is
served at 6 p.m. They go to bed at 9 p.m. They spend
their time in playing chess and reading newspapers and books.
As the weather is becoming cold, they are provided with
two electric stoves.
On Sunday evening, General Tsai took supper
with the six men and had a conversation with them for an
hour and a half.
On the morning of November 30, some 110
persons visited Mr. Sung Chun Shih and the others. About
100 persons applied to the Public Safety Bureau for
permission to call on the six men between 2 and 4 p.m.
December 1.

Ta Kung Pao (Editorial) :-

Mr. Sung Chun Shih and five others are at
present in the custody of the Shanghai Bureau of Public
Safety. We have refrained from commenting on this case
because no particulars are known, furthermore, the case is
sub judice.
(1) Mr. Sung Chun Shih and the others are all
well known writers in Shanghai. Their case has attracted
much attention among cultural circles. Every Chinese
citizen should observe the law and any person who is
suspected of a crime will incur the penalty of the law,
but this must be carried out according to legal procedure.
This should be strictly observed, particularly in cases to
which the community is paying much attention. When the
authorities made the arrests, they must have a suspicion
that the six persons had committed some offence. In that
event, why have they not been referred to Court to be dealt
with instead of being detained at the Bureau for so many
days already? According to law, the Police must arraign
an arrested man before a Court within 24 hours. Why has
this procedure not been observed in the present case?
(2) The six persons are writers on social
conditions. Their speeches and activities have a certain
effect among a section of the community. So far as we
know, the body which these six persons organized this year
has not been registered with the authorities. In the view
of the authorities, this is an offence. The authorities
had not interfered with their activities in the past because
they did not suspect their motives.
Now, this case happened at a time when the
Government is leading the country in national salvation
work. According to a brief communique issued by the local
authorities, new developments in the case seem to have
taken place. If this is true, the case should be
immediately referred to the Court for investigation and
a charge can be filed so that the truth might be revealed.
These men should be immediately restored to freedom if the
Court, after holding an inquiry, decides against a
prosecution.
(3) We hope the Government will be lenient
to these men. If a person is simply under a suspicion
which can be explained away or if the matter arose through
a misunderstanding, he should be allowed to argue his case.
If the facts in the present case admit of such
explanation or pleading, the Court should rule that no
prosecution should be instituted. We think this step is
desirable because we are of the opinion that, in order to
save the country, it is important that the country be free
of internal troubles, and to accomplish this there must be
sincerity and good will between the Government and the
people. This sincerity and good will should first be
shown by the Government.
The China of the past, or even the China
of six months ago, cannot be compared with the China of
to-day, for China is now a united country. In fact, our
Government is at this very moment directing the whole
country in the struggle against alien aggression. To

《大公报》（社论）：

沈钧儒先生等五人目前由上海公安局羁押。我们此前未对此案发表评论，因为详情不明，且该案正在审理中。
(1) 沈钧儒先生等人均为上海知名作家。他们的案件在文化界引起了广泛关注。每个中国公民都应遵守法律，任何涉嫌犯罪的人都将受到法律的惩罚，但这必须依照法定程序进行。这一点应严格遵守，特别是在社会广泛关注的案件中。当局实施逮捕时，必定是怀疑此六人犯有某种罪行。既然如此，为何不将他们移交法庭处理，而是将其拘押在局内多日？根据法律，警察必须在逮捕后24小时内将被捕者提堂受审。为何本案未遵循此程序？
(2) 此六人是评论社会状况的作家。他们的言论和活动在社会部分群体中产生了一定影响。据我们所知，此六人今年组织的团体并未向当局注册。在当局看来，这是一种违法行为。当局过去未干涉他们的活动，是因为未怀疑其动机。
现在，此案发生在政府领导全国进行救国工作之际。根据地方当局发布的简短公报，案件似乎出现了新进展。如果属实，应立即将案件移交法庭调查并提出指控，以便查明真相。如果法庭经讯问后决定不予起诉，则应立即恢复这些人的自由。
(3) 我们希望政府对此等人从宽处理。如果一个人仅处于嫌疑状态且该嫌疑可以解释清楚，或者此事因误解而起，应允许其申辩。如果本案事实允许此类解释或申辩，法庭应裁定不予起诉。我们认为这一步骤是可取的，因为我们认为，为了救国，国家必须免于内部纷扰，而要实现这一点，政府与人民之间必须有诚意和善意。这种诚意和善意应首先由政府表现出来。
过去的中国，甚至是六个月前的中国，都无法与今日之中国相比，因为中国现在是一个统一的国家。事实上，我国政府此刻正领导全国对抗外来侵略。为了

December 2, 1936.
Morning Translation.

save the country, every bit of national power, visible and invisible, should be put together to make a united power. We must bear in mind that the power possessed by a section of the literary class can be used as a part of national power if properly utilized.
(4) We wish also to make a few remarks to members of literary circles. All persons engaged in the national salvation movement should make their organization and activities conform to law. This is particularly important at the present moment. In plain words, apart from upholding the Government, all other activities are quite unnecessary. Organizations of the people are necessary only when the political situation is in a state of confusion and the Government has become powerless. But such is not the case in China to-day. While it must be admitted that a great deal of reconstruction work and improvement has yet to be accomplished in political and financial matters, we must not overlook the great improvements that have already been achieved during the past six months. At a time when a new situation has arisen, it is the duty of patriotic persons to place their trust in the Government and not to confuse the situation by their acts. We trust the literary circles will recognize this. Mistaken notions should be corrected immediately. As to liberty of speech, we are confident that it will be permitted by the Government so long as military secrets are not divulged.

Lih Pao :-

ALLEGATIONS BY RELEASED CONGEE HAWKER

Interviewed by our reporter yesterday, Chang Yung Woo (張榮和), the congee hawker, who was arrested by the Police on suspicion of being connected with the murder of a Japanese marine named Taminato and released on November 30, made the following statement:-
"When I was arrested and taken to the Japanese Marine Post on Chapoo Road, I was assaulted and my face and body became swollen as a result of the assault. At 8 o'clock, I was again taken there and beaten and interrogated until 2 a.m. after which I was sent to the Japanese Marine Headquarters. Subsequently, I was escorted to a Police Station. When I left the Headquarters, a doctor examined my injuries and gave me two injections."

晨间译稿。

救国，每一分有形和无形的国力都应汇聚起来，形成统一的力量。我们必须牢记，如果加以适当利用，文学界部分人士所拥有的力量可以作为国力的一部分。
(4) 我们也希望向文学界人士说几句话。所有参与救国运动的人都应使其组织和活动符合法律。这在当前时刻尤为重要。简言之，除了拥护政府外，其他活动都是完全不必要的。只有在政治局势混乱、政府无力之时，民众的组织才是必要的。但今日之中国并非如此。虽然必须承认，在政治和财政方面仍有大量的重建和改进工作有待完成，但我们不可忽视过去六个月已取得的巨大进步。在新局势出现之际，爱国者的责任是信任政府，而不是以其行为混淆局势。我们相信文学界会认识到这一点。错误的观念应立即纠正。至于言论自由，我们有信心，只要不泄露军事机密，政府将予以允许。

《立报》：

获释粥贩的指控

本报记者昨日采访了张荣和，这名粥贩此前因涉嫌与一名名为Taminato（音译）的日本海军陆战队员谋杀案有关而被警方逮捕，并于11月30日获释，他作了如下陈述：
“当我被捕并被带到乍浦路日本海军陆战队哨所时，我遭到殴打，面部和身体因殴打而肿胀。8点钟时，我再次被带到那里，遭受殴打和审讯直至凌晨2点，随后我被送往日本海军陆战队总部。之后，我被护送至一个警察局。离开总部时，一名医生检查了我的伤势，并给我打了两针。”

December 2, 1936. Morning Translation.

NIPPO

PRO-SOVIET CHINESE PARTY ACTIVELY WORKING TO
SAVE CHANG NAN CHI

Six Chinese named Sung Chun
Shih, Ma, Chao Shih, Sse Chi Lien, Li Kung Fu, Chang
Nan Chi, and Chow Tao Feng, important officers of the
Chinese National Salvation Association, who were arrested
for reactionary activities, are still being detained at
the Headquarters of the Bureau of Public Safety.
The Chinese National Salvation
Associations have started a movement among anti-Japanese
and Pro-Soviet elements among the officials of the Nanking
Government to effect the release of these six prisoners.
National Salvation Associations have 700,000 members
all of whom have become highly indignant over the arrest
of their leaders.
General Feng Yu Hsiang and Mr.
Yu Yue Jen, members of the Pro-Soviet Party, have secretly
informed the National Salvation Associations that if the
Associations could secure the signatures of 100,000 persons
in favour of the release of the prisoners, the Government
would release them. For this reason, the officers of
the National Salvation Associations are now actively
engaged in securing signatures. The work will take at
least a month.
The Japanese-German Anti-communist
Co-operative Agreement has caused consternation among the
members of the Chinese Pro-Soviet Party. They are
reported to have approached the Nanking Government to
conclude a Sino-Soviet Co-operative Agreement with a view
to opposing Japan. Consequently, they will assist the
activities of the National Salvation Associations.
The Far Eastern Political Bureau
of the Soviet Government is endeavouring to secure
co-operation between Soviet officers in Shanghai and
Nanking and pro-Soviet Chinese officials.

《日本日报》

亲苏中国政党积极活动以营救章乃器

六名中国人，即沈钧儒、马（音译）、赵时（音译）、沙千里、李公朴（音译）、章乃器和邹韬奋（音译），系“中华民族救国会”的重要官员，因反动活动被捕，目前仍被拘押于公安局总部。
“中华民族救国会”已在南京政府官员中的反日和亲苏分子中发起运动，以促成释放这六名囚犯。
“中华民族救国会”拥有70万会员，其领导层被捕令所有会员极为愤慨。
亲苏党成员冯玉祥将军和余岳仁（音译）先生秘密告知“中华民族救国会”，如果该会能征集到10万人签名支持释放囚犯，政府将会释放他们。因此，“中华民族救国会”的官员们现在正积极从事征集签名的工作。这项工作至少需要一个月时间。
《德日反共协定》引起中国亲苏党成员的恐慌。据报，他们已接触南京政府，旨在缔结《中苏合作协定》以对抗日本。因此，他们将协助“中华民族救国会”的活动。
苏联政府远东政治局正努力促成在上海和南京的苏联官员与亲苏中国官员之间的合作。

THE TRIAL OF MR. YAO SZ YEN

MR. Yao Sz Yen (姚士彥), age 24 a native
of Chekiang, residing at No.6 Mei Hwa Li (美華里), Route
Depleix, French Concession, is a member of the staff of the
Bankers' Co-operation Credit Service, Ltd., 133 Yuen Ling
Yuen Road. He was arrested at his residence on November 26
by the Public Safety Bureau with the assistance of the
French Police on suspicion of being a communist.

At 2 p.m. yesterday Presiding Judge Wu Ting
Chi (吳廷琪) of the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court
held a hearing of the case, after which the Judge ordered
the accused to be detained at the Police Station pending
the production of evidence by the Public Safety Bureau.

Mr. Koo (顧 ), the lawyer defending the accused,
declared that the accused had not committed any offence
and that it was unfair to detain him at the Police Station.

The Judge then ordered the accused to be
held at the Detention House of the Court.

Red Cross Society, the Shanghai Orphans Institute, the
Chinese Women and Children Relief Association, the China
Leper Relief Association etc. were present.
Mr. Choeh Wen Loh, who presided, made the
following report:- "Fighting has broken out in Suiyuan.
Numerous wounded soldiers and refugees in the war devastated
areas have become homeless and many have lost their lives.
For this reason, this new Association is being formed for
the purpose of affording them relief. The Famine Relief
Committee has promised to issue bonds to the value of
$100,000 to assist the Association."
Dr. H.H. Kung, Minister of Finance, was
appointed Chairman of the new Association with the following
gentlemen as Vice Chairmen: Mayor Wu Te Chen, Dr. C.T. Wang,
Messrs Pan Kung Chan, Tu Yuet Sen, Wong Yih Ding, Tsu Ts Jao
(朱子橋), Yih Tao Chong (叶楚傖), Choeh Wen Loh and
Hsiung Hsi Ling (熊希齡).

November 19, 1936.
Formal Translation.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

MESSRS. CHANG NAN CHI AND CHOW TAO FENG HANDED OVER
TO BUREAU OF PUBLIC SAFETY

In connection with the case in which Messrs.
Sung Chun Shih (沈鈞儒), Li Hung Ju (李公樸) and
others were arrested, Miss Sze Liang (史良), a female
lawyer, had up to 2 p.m. yesterday failed to put in an
appearance in Court.
On the morning of November 28, lawyers
Tong Hwo (唐豪) and Chang Tse Ning (張志讓) and
guarantor Wu Yin Ding (吳蔭庭) (owner of the Tien Zung
Ziang Zang Kee & Co Shop (天順祥記綢莊), No. 417 Rue
Lafayette) were summoned to the 3rd Branch of the Kiangsu
High Court. Mr. Jau Van Sien (趙萬選) Chief - Procurator,
held a session.
The two lawyers said that despite all
their efforts, they could not locate Miss Sze Liang.
Lawyer Tong Hwo declared that on Nov. 28,
he received a letter from Miss Sze Liang from an outport.
The letter was handed to the Court.
After opening and reading over the letter,
the Procurator made the following statement to the two
lawyers and the guarantor: "You cannot do anything to
Miss Sze Liang in Court. Furthermore, according to her
letter, she says that she has absconded, therefore it
is a fact that she has run away."
The Court then ordered the issue of a
warrant for the arrest of Miss Sze Liang and the two
lawyers and the guarantor Wu were instructed to undertake
to produce her in Court.
At 7 p.m. yesterday, Messrs. Chang Nan Chi
and Chow Tao Feng were handed over to the Bureau of Public
Safety. They are being detained in the same room with
Messrs. Sung Chun Shih, Wong Chao Shih and Li Hung Pu.

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：-

章乃器与邹韬奋两先生移交公安局

在沈钧儒、李公朴等人被捕一案中，女律师史良小姐直至昨日下午2时仍未出庭。
11月28日上午，律师唐豪和张志让以及担保人吴荫庭（天顺祥记绸庄业主，地址拉斐特路417号）被传唤至江苏高等法院第三分院。首席检察官赵万选主持庭审。
两位律师表示，尽管他们尽力寻找，但仍无法找到史良小姐。
律师唐豪声明，他于11月28日收到史良小姐从外地寄来的一封信。该信已提交法庭。
检察官拆阅信件后，向两位律师和担保人发表如下声明：“你们在法庭上对史良小姐无能为力。此外，根据她的信件，她说自己已经潜逃，因此她逃跑已成事实。”
法庭随即下令签发逮捕史良小姐的 warrant（逮捕令），并指示两位律师和担保人吴先生承担将其提堂的责任。
昨晚7时，章乃器和邹韬奋两先生被移交公安局。他们与沈钧儒、王造时和李公朴诸先生被关押在同一房间。

律师唐豪声明，他于11月28日收到史良小姐从外地寄来的一封信。该信已提交法庭。
检察官拆阅信件后，向两位律师和担保人发表如下声明：“你们在法庭上对史良小姐无能为力。此外，根据她的信件，她说自己已经潜逃，因此她逃跑已成事实。”
法庭随即下令签发逮捕史良小姐的 warrant（逮捕令），并指示两位律师和担保人吴先生承担将其提堂的责任。
昨晚7时，章乃器和邹韬奋两先生被移交公安局。他们与沈钧儒、王造时和李公朴（李公）诸先生被关押在同一房间。

November 28, 1936. Morning Translation.

T Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

MESSRS CHANG NAN CHI AND CHOW T.O FENG HANDED OVER TO
SHANGHAI DISTRICT COURT

Miss Sze Liang (史良), a lawyer residing
in the French Concession, Mr. Chang Nan Chi (章乃器), an
economist, and Mr. Chow Tao Feng (周韬奋), publisher of
the "Livelihood Weekly" (生活周刊), were arrested during
the night of November 22/23 by the Public Safety Bureau
with the assistance of the French Police on a charge of
inciting labour unrest. On November 23, they were arraigned
before the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court and
were allowed bail.
On November 24, only Messrs Chang and Chow
appeared in the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court.
Miss Sze failed to attend. The Court ordered them to
be detained.
On November 25, Messrs Chang and Chow were
again brought before the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High
Court. An order was issued that the case be investigated
by the Procurator of the Court. In the meantime, the
Court ordered the lawyers defending Miss Sze Liang to
produce her in Court.
After she was bailed out, Miss Sze Liang
left Shanghai on the following morning. Up to 5 p.m.
yesterday, she had still failed to appear in Court.
The French Police has detailed officers to her residence
and to railway stations and wharves in an endeavour to
effect her arrest.
Holding the view that both Messrs Chang Nan
Chi and Chow Tao Feng had committed acts that are harmful
to peace and order, the Shanghai District Court on November
27 sent Procurator Wong Chia Mei (王家楣) to the Third
Branch of the Kiangsu High Court to request their
extradition.
At 5.45 p.m. yesterday, Presiding Judge Wu
Ting Chi (吴廷祺), Judges Wong (王) and Liao (廖) and
Procurator Tung (董) held a hearing of their case in the
Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court. Mr. Yuen Chia Wang
(袁家望), the Municipal Advocate, the lawyers for the
defence, and Procurator Wong of the Shanghai District Court
were present.
Presiding Judge Wu ordered that Messrs Chang
Nan Chi and Chow Tao Feng be handed over to the Shanghai
District Court.
So far, Miss Sze Liang, a lawyer, has failed
to appear. Detectives from the Chinese and Foreign Police
have been sent to Soochow to locate and arrest her. It
is believed that she has gone to the North. More detectives
and policemen have been detailed to keep a watch at the
wharves and railway stations.
Our reporter made enquiries at the residence
of Miss Sze Liang in Lafayette Terrace, French Concession.
Her mother declared :- "The members of her family are
very much anxious over the whereabouts of Miss Sze Liang.
We do not know when she will return to Shanghai. Neither
her relatives nor her intimate friends know where she has
gone. She has a case for hearing at 9 a.m. November 26.
She may return before noon that day".

1936年11月28日。晨间译件。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：-

章乃器先生与周韬奋先生被移交上海地方法院

居住于法租界的律师史良女士、经济学家章乃器先生，以及《生活周刊》出版人周韬奋先生，于11月22/23日夜间，由公安局在法国警察的协助下，以煽动劳工骚乱的罪名逮捕。11月23日，他们在江苏高等法院第三分院受审，并获准保释。
11月24日，仅章乃器和周韬奋两位先生出庭江苏高等法院第三分院。史良女士未到庭。法院下令将其拘留。
11月25日，章乃器和周韬奋两位先生再次被提至江苏高等法院第三分院。法院发布命令，由该院检察官对案件进行调查。同时，法院命令为史良女士辩护的律师将其带至法庭。
史良女士获保释后，于次日清晨离开上海。截至昨日下午5时，她仍未出庭。法国警察已派遣警员驻守其寓所以及各火车站和码头，试图将其逮捕归案。
上海地方法院认为章乃器和周韬奋两位先生的行为有害于和平与秩序，遂于11月27日派遣检察官王家楣前往江苏高等法院第三分院，请求引渡二人。
昨日下午5时45分，审判长吴廷祺、王姓法官、廖姓法官及董姓检察官在江苏高等法院第三分院开庭审理此案。市公廨律师袁家望、辩护律师以及上海地方法院检察官王某均在场。
审判长吴廷祺下令将章乃器和周韬奋两位先生移交上海地方法院。
截至目前，律师史良女士仍未出庭。中外警探已被派往苏州搜寻并逮捕她。据信她已北上。更多警探和警察已被部署在码头和火车站进行监视。
本报记者在法租界拉斐特路（Lafayette Terrace）史良女士寓所进行了查询。其母表示：“家人对史良女士的下落非常焦虑。我们不知道她何时返回上海。她的亲属和密友都不知道她去了哪里。她原定于11月26日上午9点出庭。她可能会在那天中午前回来”。

November 27, 1936.
Afternoon Translation.

Society Evening News dated November 26 (comment) :-

ARREST OF MR. SUNG CHUN SHIH AND OTHERS

Messrs. Sung Chun Shih (沙鈞儒), Li
Kung Pu (李公樸), Wang Chao Shih (王造時), Chang
Nan Chi (章乃器), Chow Tao Feng (鄒奮) and Soo Chi
Lien (沙千里) and Miss Sze Liang (史良) were
recently arrested "on suspicion of instigating strikes."
These seven learned scholars are the leaders of the
national salvation movement and their arrest came as a
shock to us, especially in view of the fact that victories
are being gained in Suiyuan, a strong attitude is being
adopted in dealing with foreign affairs and the moment
seems opportune for the establishment of a popular front.
Messrs. Sung, Wang and Soo and Miss Sze
are well known lawyers and as such they have acted as
protectors of the people's rights. Inspired by a
spirit of righteousness, they have been undertaking
national salvation work. Their actions may have gone
beyond the limit, but we are confident that their motive
is proper.
Messrs. Li, Chow and Chang are respectively
the editors of such authoritative publications as the
"Livelihood" (生活), the "Intelligence" (讀書生活) etc.
Their articles have been well received by the public.
Their writings may appear to be inflammatory, but they
contained nothing that is malicious; they write what
every citizen of China wishes to say. They are not being
instigated by others. The spirit of nationalism that has
seized hold of the people at present is largely due to
their writings.
It is to be hoped that the authorities will
take these facts into consideration when dealing with these
three persons.
The authorities should conduct an
investigation into the case as soon as possible and release
the seven persons if there is no proof against them. The
arrest of these seven persons may please our enemy, but it
is distressing for us to witness such an event so soon
after the release from gaol of Mr. Doo Zung Yuen (杜重遠)
who was imprisoned in connection with the case of the
"New Life Weekly" (新生).

1936年11月27日。
午后译件。

11月26日《社会晚报》（评论）：-

沈钧儒先生等人被捕

沈钧儒、李公樸、王造时、章乃器、邹奋（音译）和沙千里诸先生以及史良女士，近期因“涉嫌煽动罢工”而被捕。这七位学者是救国运动的领袖，他们的被捕令我们震惊，特别是考虑到绥远正取得胜利，当局在处理外交事务上采取强硬态度，且此刻似乎是建立统一战线的良机。
沈、王、沙三位先生及史良女士均为知名律师，作为人民权利的维护者而闻名。出于正义感，他们一直从事救国工作。他们的行为可能有些过激，但我们相信其动机是正当的。
李、邹、章三位先生分别是《生活》、《读书生活》等权威刊物的编辑。他们的文章深受公众欢迎。他们的文字看似具有煽动性，但并无恶意；他们写出了每个中国公民想说的话。他们并非受人指使。目前笼罩在民众心中的民族主义精神，很大程度上归功于他们的文章。
希望当局在处理这三人的案件时能考虑这些事实。
当局应尽快调查此案，若无确凿证据，应释放这七人。逮捕这七人或许会取悦我们的敌人，但在杜重远先生因《新生》周刊案出狱后不久便目睹此类事件，令我们感到痛心。

November 27, 1936. Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers publish the following telegraphic reports :-

GENERAL SUNG CHEH YUAN HOLDS CONFERENCE.

On the evening of November 25, General Sung Cheh Yuan, Chairman of the Hopei-Chahar Political Council, had a conference with Generals C.ang Shih Tsong, Lieu Shu Ming, Feng S.u An and Chao Teng Yu, the four Divisional Commanders of the 29th Army, at which they discussed the maintenance of peace and order in Charhar, Peiping and Tientsin.

General Sung Cheh Yuan Consults General Chiang Kai Shek

At 10 .m. November 26, General Sung Cheh Yuan flew to Loyang and had a conference with General Chiang Kai Shek. He returned to Peiping at 3 p.m.

Open Letter To Bandit Forces

General Chiang Kai Shek and General Yen Hsi Shan issued on November 26 a joint open letter addressed to the soldiers of the bandit and "Manchukuo" forces advising them not to be used by others to fight their fellow countrymen and urging them to come to their senses and join the Chinese army.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE ARREST OF MESSRS SUNG CHUN SHIH, CHANG NAN CHI AND FIVE OTHERS

Messrs Sung Chun Shih (沈钧儒), Li Ling Fu (李公樸), Wang Chao Shih (王造时) and Soo Chi Lien (沙千里) have been handed over to the Public Safety Bureau. They are being well treated and are permitted to receive relatives and friends; They have been provided with magazines and newspapers.

Messrs Chang Nan Chi and Chow Tao Peng are still being held in the Detention House of the Second Shanghai Special District Court and are also being well treated. As the residences of the families of Mr. Chang and Mr. Chow are not far from the Detention House, food is being sent to them privately.

The whereabouts of Miss Sze Liang (史良) are not clear. Detectives of the French Police are watching her residence. It is reported that Miss Sze has proceeded to Peiping by aeroplane to call on Dr. Tung Kung, her uncle, a former Minister of Justice. Another report says that she has proceeded to Nanking. Mr. Tong Hwo (唐豪) declares that Miss Sze will appear in Court before November 28.

3

1936年11月27日。晨间译件。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸刊登如下电讯报道：-

宋哲元将军举行会议。

11月25日晚，冀察政务委员会委员长宋哲元将军与第二十九军四位师长张自忠、刘汝明、冯治安和赵登禹将军举行会议，讨论维持察哈尔、北平和天津的和平与秩序。

宋哲元将军咨询蒋介石将军

11月26日上午10时，宋哲元将军飞抵洛阳，与蒋介石将军举行会谈。他于下午3时返回北平。

致匪军公开信

蒋介石将军和阎锡山将军于11月26日发表联合公开信，劝告伪军及“满洲国”部队士兵不要被人利用来攻打同胞，敦促他们醒悟并加入中国军队。

《立报》及其他本地报纸：-

沈钧儒、章乃器等六人被捕

沈钧儒、李公樸、王造时和沙千里诸先生已被移交给公安局。他们受到良好待遇，并被允许会见亲友；当局还为他们提供了杂志和报纸。

章乃器和周韬鹏（音译）两位先生仍被关押在上海第二特区地方法院看守所，同样受到良好待遇。由于章、周二位的家属住所离看守所不远，私下有人给他们送食物。

史良女士的下落不明。法国警察正在监视其寓所。据报道，史女士已乘飞机前往北平拜访其叔父、前司法总长董康博士。另有消息称她已前往南京。唐豪先生宣称，史女士将在11月28日前出庭。

November 27, 1936.
Morning Translation.

Arrest of Mr. Yao Sz Yen

Mr. Yao Sz Yen (姚士彥), age 24, residing at
No. 6, Mei Hwa Li (美華里), Route Dupleix, French Concession,
is a member of the staff of the Bankers' Co-operation
Credit Service, Ltd, 133 Yuen Ming Yuen Road,
On the morning of November 26, officers of
the Public Safety Bureau, with the assistance of the
French Police, arrested Mr. Yao at his residence.
Mr. Yao was arraigned before the Third Branch
of the Kiangsu High Court at 2 p.m. yesterday. Mr. Yuen
Chia Wang (袁家汪), the Municipal Advocate, stated that
the man had been arrested at the request of the Public
Safety Bureau and requested the Court to remand the case
for four days to permit of further investigations.
At this stage, the Judge cleared the Court
of spectators. The case was subsequently remanded to
November 30. The accused is being detained in custody.

Lih Pao :-

Liang Tsai Circulating Library & Supplementary School
Reorganized

At a meeting held by members of the Board
of Directors of the Liang Tsai Circulating Library &
Supplementary School on the evening of November 25, it
was resolved that the resignation of Mr. Li Kung Pu from
the post of President of the Circulating Library &
Supplementary School be approved and that Mr. Li Tsoo Sun
(李祖申), Chairman of the Board of Directors, act
currently as President.
Yesterday the Supplementary School posted
up a notice directing the students to pay attention to
their studies and to remain calm.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

REPORTED ARREST OF MADAME SUN Y T SEN UNTRUE

"The Shanghai Mainichi", a local Japanese
newspaper, on November 26 published a report to the effect
that Madame Sun Yat Sen was arrested in the French
Concession on the morning of November 25 on a charge of
Communism.
On November 26, our reporter made enquiries
at Madame Sun's residence on Rue Moliere, French Concession
and learned that the report was absolutely groundless.
Yesterday, Madame Sun issued a manifesto,
in which she called attention to the fact that Japanese
newspapers were in the habit of spreading rumours.
The Japanese report that she had been arrested was untrue.
She declared that the motive of the Japanese newspapers
in publishing such reports was to bring about a split
between the Chinese Government and the people, but
contrary to their hopes, such reports would result in a
consolidation of the country.

1936年11月27日。
晨间译件。

姚士彦先生被捕

姚士彦，24岁，居住在法租界辣斐德路（Route Dupleix）美华里6号，系圆明园路133号银行合作信贷服务有限公司职员。
11月26日上午，公安局官员在法国警察的协助下，在其寓所逮捕了姚先生。
姚先生于昨日下午2时在江苏高等法院第三分院受审。市公廨律师袁家汪（音译）陈述称，此人是应公安局要求被捕的，并请求法院将案件延期四天，以便进一步调查。
此时，法官清退了旁听人员。随后案件被延期至11月30日审理。被告目前被羁押。

《立报》：-

量才流通图书馆及补习学校改组

在11月25日晚举行的量才流通图书馆及补习学校董事会会议上，决议批准李公樸先生辞去流通图书馆及补习学校校长职务，并由董事会主席李祖申先生暂代校长。
昨日，补习学校张贴告示，要求学生专心学业并保持冷静。

《立报》及其他本地报纸：-

谣传孙夫人被捕不实

本地日文报纸《上海每日新闻》于11月26日报道称，孙逸仙夫人于11月25日上午在法租界因涉嫌共产主义被捕。
11月26日，本报记者在法租界莫利爱路（Rue Moliere）孙夫人寓所查询，获悉该报道毫无根据。
昨日，孙夫人发表宣言，指出日本报纸惯于散布谣言。关于她被捕的日本报道是不实的。她声明，日本报纸发布此类报道的动机旨在造成中国政府与民众之间的分裂，但与他们的愿望相反，此类报道将导致国家的团结巩固。

The Star Daily News (明星日報) :-

COMMENT ON ECONOMY REPORT

Most of our fellow-countrymen,
especially those in Shanghai, are in the habit of paying
high tribute to foreigners. They eat or dress in the
foreign style; they prefer to seek employment with foreign
companies. But the more we look up to foreigners, the
more are we regarded with contempt by them. Take, for
instance, the retrenchment measures recently approved by
the J.M.C.

沈钧儒先生等人被捕

经济报告评论

我国同胞，尤其是上海居民，习惯于对外国人推崇备至。他们吃穿洋式；更喜欢在外商公司求职。但我们越是仰视外国人，就越是被他们轻视。例如，工部局最近批准的紧缩措施。

November 27, 1936. Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers publish the following telegraphic reports :-

GENERAL SUNG CHEH YUAN HOLDS CONFERENCE.

On the evening of November 25, General Sung Cheh Yuan, Chairman of the Hopei-Chahar Political Council, had a conference with Generals Chiang Shih Tsong, Lieu Shu Ming, Feng Shu An and Chao Teng Ya, the four Divisional Commanders of the 29th Army, at which they discussed the maintenance of peace and order in Charhar, Peiping and Tientsin.

General Sung Cheh Yuan Consults General Chiang Kai Shek

At 10 a.m. November 26, General Sung Cheh Yuan flew to Loyang and had a conference with General Chiang Kai Shek. He returned to Peiping at 3 p.m.

Open Letter To Bandit Forces

General Chiang Kai Shek and General Yen Hsi Shan issued on November 26 a joint open letter addressed to the soldiers of the bandit and "Manchukuo" forces advising them not to be used by others to fight their fellow countrymen and urging them to come to their senses and join the Chinese army.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE ARREST OF MESSRS SUNG CHUN SHIH, CHANG NAN CHI AND FIVE OTHERS

Messrs Sung Chun Shih (沈钧儒), Li Ming Pu (李公朴), Wang Chao Shih (王造时) and Soo Chi Lien (沙千里) have been handed over to the Public Safety Bureau. They are being well treated and are permitted to receive relatives and friends; They have been provided with magazines and newspapers.

Messrs Chang Nan Chi and Chow Tao Feng are still being held in the Detention House of the Second Shanghai Special District Court and are also being well treated. As the residences of the families of Mr. Chang and Mr. Chow are not far from the Detention House, food is being sent to them privately.

The whereabouts of Miss Sze Liang (史良) are not clear. Detectives of the French Police are watching her residence. It is reported that Miss Sze has proceeded to Peiping by aeroplane to call on Dr. Tung Kong, her uncle, a former Minister of Justice. Another report says that she has proceeded to Nanking. Mr. Tong Hwo (唐豪) declares that Miss Sze will appear in Court before November 28.

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸刊登如下电讯报道：-

宋哲元将军举行会议。

11月25日晚，冀察政务委员会委员长宋哲元将军与第二十九军四位师长张自忠、刘汝明、冯治安和赵登禹将军举行会议，讨论维持察哈尔、北平和天津的治安秩序问题。

宋哲元将军谒见蒋介石将军

11月26日上午10时，宋哲元将军飞抵洛阳，与蒋介石将军举行会谈。他于下午3时返回北平。

致匪军公开信

蒋介石将军与阎锡山将军于11月26日发表联合公开信，致匪军及“满洲国”部队士兵，劝告他们不要被他人利用来攻打同胞，敦促他们迷途知返，加入中国军队。

沈钧儒、章乃器等七人被捕

沈钧儒、李公朴、王造时和沙千里先生已被移交给公安局。他们受到良好待遇，并获准会见亲友；当局还为他们提供了杂志和报纸。

章乃器和邹韬奋先生仍被关押在上海第二特区地方法院拘留所，也受到良好待遇。由于章、周二人的家属住所离拘留所不远，有人私下给他们送食物。

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE ARREST OF MESSRS SUNG CHUN SHIH, CHANG NAN CHI AND FIVE OTHERS

In connection with the arrest of Messrs Sung Chun Shih (沈鈞儒), Li Kung Pu (李公樸), Wang Chao Shih (王造時), Soo Chi Lien (沙千里), Chow Tao Feng (鄒韜奮), and Chang Nan Chi (章乃器) and Miss Sze Liang (史良), the following information was obtained yesterday :-

At 2 p.m. yesterday, Presiding Judge Yeu (郁) of the Second Branch of the Kiangsu High Court held a session and ordered that Mr. Soo Chi Lien be handed over to the Public Safety Bureau.

Mr. Tsa Chi Feng (查化風), the Advocate of the Public Safety Bureau, then proceeded to the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court to request the extradition of Mr. Chang Nan Chi and others.

At 6 p.m. yesterday, Messrs Chang Nan Chi and Chow Tao Feng were again brought before Presiding Judge Wu Ting Chi (吳廷璂), Judges Wong (王) and Liao (廖) and Procurator Tung Chi Min (董其鳴) in the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court. The Presiding Judge said :-
"As a question regarding bail for the accused has arisen, the present hearing is being held. Lawyers Chang (張) and Tong (唐), the guarantors of Miss Sze Liang, should produce her in Court immediately".

Lawyers Chang and Tong gave an assurance that Miss Sze Liang would appear in Court before November 28.

On the basis of the documents produced by the Public Safety Bureau, Presiding Judge Wu interrogated Messrs Chang Nan Chi and Chow Tao Feng up to 7.30 p.m. The Presiding Judge afterwards retired to consider his decision. When he resumed the hearing, he ordered that the case against Messrs Chang Nan Chi and Chow Tao Feng be investigated by the Procurator of the Court in an endeavour to ascertain whether or not they had committed the offences charged to them. Messrs Chang and Chow are still under detention.

Messrs Sung Chun Shih, Wang Chao Shih and Li Kung Pu were extradited to the Public Safety Bureau at 5 p.m. November 24. The Bureau opened a temporary detention house on the Second Floor of the Bureau, where three beds were placed. Good treatment is being accorded to the accused. Several policemen and detectives are keeping a watch day and night outside the house. Only members of their families and their lawyers are allowed to see the prisoners.

November 25, 1936.
Afternoon Translation

The Shanghai Public Daily News(市民日報) publishes the following leading article :-

THE ARREST OF LI KUNG FU AND OTHERS.

Between 2 and 3 a.m. on November 23, Messrs Li Kung Pu(李公樸), Wang Chao Shih(王造時), Soo Chi Lien(沙千里), Sung Chun Shih(沈鈞儒), Chow Tao Feng(韜奮), Chang Nan Chi(章乃器) and Miss Szo Liang(史良), seven patriotic leaders, were placed under arrest. The affair created a consternation among the public who were ignorant of the cause of this drastic action.

The following report was issued by the Central News Agency and published by the local newspapers yesterday :-

"Mr. Li Kung Pu and six others are being charged with operating illegal organizations, co-operating with communists, instigating strikes of workers and students and a general strike and other subversive activities with the object of overthrowing the Government. They were arrested by the authorities with the assistance of the Police of the Foreign Settlements on a charge of having committed offences against the internal security of the State."

We cannot help asking: "Have they really been arrested on such a charge?"

Nobody will excuse a person who betrays his nation under the cloak of patriotism. However, the seven persons under arrest are prominent leaders of the National Salvation Association and their thoughts, character and patriotism deserve sympathy and support. Moreover, they are all engaged in proper professions.

It has been said that there is a limit to patriotism; it is possible that their patriotism has been too fiery. Still, we cannot believe that any person who loves his country too strongly can be arrested and punished by the authorities. However, as the matter has been referred to the Courts, an explanation will be forthcoming.

The Holmes (福爾摩斯) :-

THE HARDSHIPS OF HAWKERS

It is not easy for a hawker to sell his wares in Shanghai. If he operates on the streets without a licence, he is liable to be taken to the Police Station where he will be fined and asked to take out a licence. This will require all the money earned during the past few days. Even if a hawker is in possession of a licence, he has to move away at the approach of a policeman, otherwise he is liable to be deprived of his licence.

1936年11月25日。
下午译件

《市民日報》刊登如下社论：-

李公樸等人被捕。

11月23日凌晨2时至3时之间，七位爱国领袖李公樸先生、王造時先生、沙千里先生、沈鈞儒先生、鄒韜奮先生、章乃器先生及史良女士被捕。此事在公众中引起惊惶，因为人们不了解采取这一严厉行动的原因。

中央通讯社发布了以下报道，并于昨日由当地报纸刊登：-

“李公樸先生等六人被指控经营非法组织，与共产党合作，煽动工人和学生罢工及总罢工，以及其他旨在推翻政府的颠覆活动。他们在外国租界警方的协助下被当局逮捕，罪名是犯有危害国家内部安全之罪。”

我们不禁要问：“他们真的是因这样的罪名被捕的吗？”

没有人会原谅披着爱国外衣背叛国家的人。然而，这七名被捕者是全国救国会的著名领袖，他们的思想、品格和爱国精神值得同情和支持。此外，他们都从事正当的职业。

November 25, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

MAINICHI

SECRET MEETING HELD BY NATIONAL SALVATION ASSOCIATIONS

The arrest of Chang Nan Chi came as a
great shock to the Cultural Circles National Salvation
Association, the Women's National Salvation Association,
the National Salvation Association of University Professors
and the Students National Salvation Association, etc.
He has been endeavouring to extend the communist movement
and it was he who directed/anti-Chiang Kai Shek movement
and organized the people's front.
Members of these Associations held a
secret meeting at a certain place in Chinese controlled
territory on the night of November 25 to consider counter-
measures.
It is reported that they will submit
a petition asking for the immediate release of Chang
Nan Chi and the other six persons now in custody. They
are also planning a demonstration and may adopt violent
measures to achieve their end.

MAINICHI AND OTHER LOCAL NEWSPAPERS :

TROUBLE BETWEEN KOREANS AND CHINESE

At about 1.10 p.m. November 24, a Korean
named Ken Nei-boku, 21, residing at No. 7 Yung Fu Li off
Woosung Road, visited another Korean named Kim Yu-toku,
a toy dealer, at No. 120 Kiengse Road. Whilst they were
talking, several Chinese outside Kim's house used abusive
language towards the Koreans. Kim became angry and asked
the Chinese why they had used abusive language towards
them. A large crowd of Chinese soon gathered and a big
fight took place.
Foreign and Chinese Police officers from
Louza Station (?) soon settled the trouble. The Japanese
Consular Police are conducting an investigation into the
affair.

1936年11月25日。下午译件。

《每日新闻》

全国救国会举行秘密会议

章乃器的被捕令文化界救国会、妇女救国会、大学教授救国会和学生救国会等大为震惊。他一直致力于扩展共产主义运动，是他指挥了反蒋介石运动并组织了人民阵线。
这些协会的成员于11月25日晚在华界某地举行秘密会议，商讨对策。
据报道，他们将提交请愿书，要求立即释放章乃器及其他六名在押人员。他们还计划进行示威，并可能采取暴力手段以达到目的。

《每日新闻》及其他当地报纸：

韩人与华人之间的纠纷

11月24日下午1点10分左右，居住在吴淞路永福里7号的21岁韩国人Ken Nei-boku（音译），前往江西北路120号拜访另一位韩国人Kim Yu-toku（音译），后者是一名玩具商。当他们交谈时，Kim家外面的几名中国人对韩国人使用辱骂性语言。Kim感到愤怒，质问中国人为何对他们使用辱骂性语言。很快聚集了大量中国人，并发生了一场大规模斗殴。
老闸捕房（?）的外国和中国警官很快平息了这起纠纷。日本领事警察正在对此事进行调查。

November 25, 1936.
Afternoon Translation

The Shanghai Public Daily News(市民日報) publishes the following leading article :-

THE ARREST OF LI KUNG PU AND OTHERS.

Between 2 and 3 a.m. on November 23, Messrs Li Kung Pu(李公), Wang Chao Shih(王造時), Soo Chi Lien(沙千里), Sung Chun Shih(沈鈞儒), Chow Tao Feng(鄒韜奮), Chang Nan Chi(章乃器) and Miss Szo Liang(史良), seven patriotic leaders, were placed under arrest. The affair created a consternation among the public who were ignorant of the cause of this drastic action.

The following report was issued by the Central News Agency and published by the local newspapers yesterday :-

"Mr. Li Kung Pu and six others are being charged with operating illegal organizations, co-operating with communists, instigating strikes of workers and students and a general strike and other subversive activities with the object of overthrowing the Government. They were arrested by the authorities with the assistance of the Police of the Foreign Settlements on a charge of having committed offences against the internal security of the State."

We cannot help asking: "Have they really been arrested on such a charge?"

Nobody will excuse a person who betrays his nation under the cloak of patriotism. However, the seven persons under arrest are prominent leaders of the National Salvation Association and their thoughts, character and patriotism deserve sympathy and support. Moreover, they are all engaged in proper professions.

It has been said that there is a limit to patriotism; it is possible that their patriotism has been too fiery. Still, we cannot believe that any person who loves his country too strongly can be arrested and punished by the authorities. However, as the matter has been referred to the Courts, an explanation will be forthcoming.

The Holmes (福爾摩斯) :-

THE HARDSHIPS OF HAWKERS

It is not easy for a hawker to sell his wares in Shanghai. If he operates on the streets without a licence, he is liable to be taken to the Police Station where he will be fined and asked to take out a licence. This will require all the money earned during the past few days. Even if a hawker is in possession of a licence, he has to move away at the approach of a policeman, otherwise he is liable to be deprived of his licence.

李公樸等人被捕。

November 25, 1936.    Morning Translation.

"At about 10 a.m. yesterday (November 19)
a pedestrian, an old man of more than 70 years of age,
was knocked down at the corner of Pingliang and Glen
Roads by a motor car (licence number unknown) which
was moving at a high speed. Upon finding that he had
caused an accident, the driver drove off at a high
speed. Later, a post duty policeman conveyed the
injured man to the Sacred Heart Hospital where the man
succumbed to his injuries soon after arrival."
It is known to everybody that there is a Police
Station at the corner of Pingliang and Glen Roads. Moreover,
the accident occurred opposite the Station. The place is
not an isolated locality. It is customary to have a
policeman on duty at the front gate of Police Station; the
accident happened at about 10 O'clock in the morning; yet
the motor car was driven off unnoticed after the accident.
I am of the opinion that an explanation should
be demanded from the Police authorities. We should not
overlook the matter just because the deceased was a poor
old man, for it is a case that concerns not only the
deceased but the general public as well.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE ARREST OF MESSRS SUNG CHUN SHIH, CHANG NAN CHI AND
FIVE OTHERS

In the early morning of November 23, Messrs Li
Kung Pu (李公樸), Sung Chun Shih (沈鈞儒), Wang Chao Shih
(王造時), Soo Chi Lien (沙千里), Chow Tao Feng (鄒韜奮)
and Chang Nan Chi (章乃器) and Miss Sze Liang (史良),
all prominent members of the Federation of National
Salvation Associations, were arrested by the S.M.P. and
the French Police at the request of the Public Safety
Bureau. Some were arraigned before the Second Branch
and others before the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High
Court on that day and all were released on bail.
On the evening of November 23, the Second
Branch and the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court
each received a dispatch from the Public Safety Bureau,
stating that fresh evidence had since been found against
the prisoners and fear was expressed that they might
abscond.
Upon receipt of the dispatch, the Second Branch
of the Kiangsu High Court immediately issued warrants of
arrest and at 2 a.m. November 24, deputies of the Public
Safety Bureau with the assistance of officers from Bubbling
Well and Sinza Stations visited the houses of Messrs Li
Kung Pu, Sung Chun Shih, Wang Chao Shih and Soo Chi Lien
to effect their arrest. With the exception of Mr. Li
Kung Pu, who was absent at the time, the other three men
were again arrested.
They were taken before Mr. Yeu Hwa (郁華),
Presiding Judge, and Judges Nyi (聶) and Siao (蕭) in the

Mr. Li Kung Pu, who had in the meantime received a Court

Mr. Tsa Chi Feng (查記鳳), the Advocate of

Advocate, and Messrs Chang Yao Tseng (張耀曾), Kuo Wei (郭衛),

1936年11月25日。上午译件。

“昨天（11月19日）上午10点左右，一名70多岁的老年行人在平凉路与格兰路（Glen Road）转角处被一辆高速行驶的汽车（车牌号不详）撞倒。司机发现造成事故后，高速驾车逃逸。随后，一名执勤警察将伤者送往圣心医院，该男子抵达后不久即因伤去世。”
众所周知，平凉路与格兰路转角处有一个警察局。此外，事故发生在警察局对面。该地并非偏僻之处。通常在警察局前门会有警察执勤；事故发生在上午10点左右；然而，肇事汽车在事故后未被察觉便驶离。
我认为应向警方当局要求解释。我们不应因为死者是一位贫穷的老人而忽视此事，因为这不仅关系到死者，也关系到广大公众。

《大公报》及其他当地报纸：-

沈鈞儒、章乃器及其他五人被捕

11月23日凌晨，全国救国会联合会的重要成员李公樸先生、沈鈞儒先生、王造時先生、沙千里先生、鄒韜奮先生、章乃器先生及史良女士，应公安局请求，被上海公共租界工部局警务处和法国警察逮捕。部分人当天在江苏高等法院第二分院受审，部分人在第三分院受审，均获保释。
11月23日晚，江苏高等法院第二分院和第三分院分别收到公安局来函，称此后发现了针对囚犯的新证据，并表示担心他们可能会潜逃。
收到来函后，江苏高等法院第二分院立即签发逮捕令，11月24日凌晨2点，公安局探员在静安寺捕房和新闸捕房警员的协助下，前往李公樸、沈鈞儒、王造時和沙千里先生的住所实施逮捕。除当时外出的李公樸先生外，其他三人再次被捕。
昨日下午2点，他们被带至江苏高等法院第二分院，由审判长郁华先生以及聶法官和蕭法官审理。在此期间收到法院传票的李公樸先生也到庭出席。
公安局律师查記鳳先生、市律师金士康（King S. Kum，音译）先生，以及张耀曾先生、郭衛先生，

November 25, 1936. Morning Translation.

Li Kuo Tseng (李國珍), Ngoh Soong (吳森), Li Vung Chi
(李文杰) and Chen Tse Kao (陳志高), lawyers for the defence,
were present.
The case against Messrs Li Kung Pu, Sung Chun
Shih and Wang Chao Shih was first dealt with. Presiding
Judge Yeu stated that the case had originally been fixed
for hearing in the afternoon of November 25, but the present
hearing was being held because of the discovery of new facts.
The representative of the Public Safety Bureau
requested the extradition of these three accused.
The Procurator requested the Judges to decide
the application according to law.
The Court then retired to consider the
application. When the Judges resumed their seats in Court,
they handed down a ruling that as Messrs Li Kung Pu, Sung
Chun Shih and Wang Chao Shih did not live within the limits
of the International Settlement, the question of extradition
did not arise; therefore, the Public Safety Bureau should
take up the matter with the S.M.C.
The three accused were then taken back by the
Settlement Police.
The case against Mr. Soo Chi Lien was next
heard. The Court remanded the case to 2 p.m. November 25
and ordered that he be temporarily detained at the Police
Station.

Proceedings in the Third Branch of High Court

In the meantime, the Third Branch of the
Kiangsu High Court had also immediately issued summons for
the appearance of Miss Sze Liang, Messrs Chow Tao Feng and
Chang Nan Chi before midnight November 24/25.
The case was heard at 6 p.m. by Presiding Judge
Wu Ting Chi (吳廷熾) and Judges Wong (王) and Liao (廖) in
the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court. Mr. Chow Tao
Feng appeared in company with Mr. Sung Tso Chi (孫祖基),
his lawyer. Miss Sze Liang and Mr. Chang Nan Chi did not
appear but were represented by Mr. Tong Hwa (唐華) and Mr.
Chang Tse Niang (張子良).
After questioning Mr. Chow Tao Feng about his
age and native place, Presiding Judge Wu ordered him to
be temporarily detained at the office of the Judicial Police.
Lawyers Tong and Chang were ordered by the Court to produce
the accused Miss Sze and Mr. Chang Nan Chi before midnight.
At about midnight, the Third Branch of the
Kiangsu High Court held a special session when Mr. Chow
Tao Feng appeared in company with Mr. Sung Tso Chi, his
lawyer. Mr. Chang Nan Chi also was present with his two
lawyers, Mr. Chang and Mr. Tong.
As the arrangements for shop security had
not yet been completed, Mr. Chow Tao Feng was ordered to
be detained for the time being.
The Court then questioned Mr. Chang Nan Chi.
Owing to insufficient time, Mr. Chang could find only one
shop security and as he could not find another shop security
he was also detained.
As Miss Sze Liang was at Soochow attending
to certain legal affairs, the Judge instructed two lawyers
Mr. Chang and Mr. Tong to produce her before 4 p.m. November 25.
The Court rose at 12.30 a.m. November 25.
The accused Chang and Chow are being temporarily held in
the Detention House.

1936年11月25日。晨间译件。

辩护律师李国珍、吴森、李文杰和陈志高到庭。
首先处理针对李公朴、沈钧儒和王造时三位先生的案件。主审法官叶（音译）指出，该案原定于11月25日下午开庭，但因发现新事实，故举行此次庭审。
公安局代表请求引渡这三名被告。
检察官请求法官依法裁定该申请。
随后法庭退庭审议该申请。法官重返法庭席位后，作出裁决：鉴于李公朴、沈钧儒和王造时三位先生并不居住在国际租界范围内，因此不涉及引渡问题；故公安局应与工部局接洽处理此事。
随后，三名被告由租界警察带回。
接下来审理针对沙千里先生的案件。法庭将案件延期至11月25日下午2点，并命令将其暂时羁押于警察局。

江苏高等法院第三分院诉讼程序

与此同时，江苏高等法院第三分院也已立即发出传票，要求史良女士、邹韬奋先生和章乃器先生在11月24/25日午夜前出庭。
该案于下午6点在江苏高等法院第三分院由主审法官吴廷炽以及王法官和廖法官进行审理。邹韬奋先生在其律师孙祖基先生的陪同下出庭。史良女士和章乃器先生未出庭，但由唐华先生和张子良先生代表。
主审法官吴在询问了邹韬奋先生的年龄和籍贯后，命令将其暂时羁押于司法警察办公室。法庭命令唐律师和张律师在午夜前带被告史女士和章乃器先生到庭。
约在午夜时分，江苏高等法院第三分院召开特别庭审，邹韬奋先生在其律师孙祖基先生的陪同下出庭。章乃器先生也与其两位律师张律师和唐律师一同到庭。
由于店铺保释手续尚未办妥，命令暂时羁押邹韬奋先生。
随后法庭讯问章乃器先生。由于时间不足，章先生仅找到一名店铺保人，因无法找到另一名店铺保人，他也被羁押。
由于史良女士正在苏州处理某些法律事务，法官指示张律师和唐律师两名律师在11月25日下午4点前将其带到庭。
法庭于11月25日凌晨12点30分休庭。被告章和周正被暂时关押在看守所。

Nov.mber 24, 1936.                                          Morning Translation.

Hwa Mei 'an Fao dated Nov.23:

SEVEN PROMINENT RESIDENTS ARRESTED ON GRAVE CHARGES

Mr. Sung Chun Shih (沈儒), native of
Kashing, age 63, residing at House No.51, Lane No.1292 Yu
Yuen Road, member of the Standing Committee of the Shanghai
Bar Association, Mr. Wang Chao Shih (王造時), native of
Kiangsi Province, age 34, residing at House No.7 Tifeng
Road, and Mr. Soo Chi Lien (沙千里), native of Huchow, age
33, both lawyers and members of the Bar Association,
and Mr. Li Kung Pu (李公樸), native of Zangchow, age 35,
residing at House No.24, Lane No.1736, Yu Yuen Road, President
of the Liang Tsai School (量才學校), are all prominent
members of the Federation of National Salvation Associations.
On November 22, members of the Bureau of Public
Safety called at the Bubbling Well Police Station of the
International Settlement, produced an official dispatch and
requested assistance to effect the arrest of these four
persons for some political offence. Warrants of arrest
were obtained from the Shanghai First Special District Court
by the Bubbling Well Police Station. Messrs. Sung Chun
Shih, Wang Chao Shih and Li Kung Pu were arrested in Bubbling
Well district late at night by a party of detectives and
uniformed policemen under Foreign Detective Sub-Inspector
"Caley". Lawyer Soo Chi Lien who lives in Sinza District
was arrested with the assistance of Sinza Police Station.
The four arrested persons were arraigned before
Judge Nyi Chung Nee (聶重義) of the Second Branch of the
Kiangsu High Court at 9 a.m. November 23. The proceedings
were held in camera. Only Mr. King S. Kum, the Municipal
Advocate, the lawyers for the defence and the police officers
in charge of the case were present.
After a lengthy interrogation, Judge Nyi allowed
the accused to be released on bail furnished by their
respective lawyers. Messrs. Chang Yi Fan (張以藩),
Ngoh Goong (吳森) and Chen Tse Kao (陳志皋) are
appearing for Mr. Li Kung Pu; Messrs. Yu Chung Loh (俞鍾輅)
and Li Vung Chi (李文池) for Mr. Wang Chao Shih; Messrs.
Chang Yao Tseng (張耀曾) and Chen Tse Kao for Mr. Sung
Chun Shih; Messrs. Tsai Loh Zung (蔡天東), Yang Tien Sung
(楊天遜) and Waung Pao Chi (汪葆楫) for Mr. Soo Chi Lien.
All the guarantors were instructed to produce the accused
at the next hearing which will take place at 2 p.m.
November 25. The representatives of the Bureau of Public
Safety requested the extradition of the accused.
At the request of the Bureau of Public Safety,
the French Municipal Police have arrested Miss Sze Liang
(史良), a lawyer, Mr. Chow Tao Feng (鄒韜奮), Editor-
in-Chief of the "Livelihood Sunday Weekly", and Mr. Chang
Nan Chi (章乃器), an economist, on a similar charge.
The arrested persons were arraigned before
the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court at 3 p.m.
November 23. Messrs. Chang Tse Niang (張志讓) and Tong Hwa
(唐豪) are appearing for Mr. Chang Nan Chi and Miss Sze
Liang; Mr. Sung Tso Chi (孫祖基) for Mr. Chow Tao Feng.
It is learned that they will likewise be released on bail.
The following information was secured from the
families of the various accused by a reporter of this paper:-

1936年11月24日。                                          晨间译件。

《华美晚报》11月23日讯：

七名知名居民因严重指控被捕

沈钧儒先生，嘉兴人，63岁，住愚园路1292弄51号，上海律师公会常务委员；王造时先生，江西省人，34岁，住提篮桥路7号；沙千里先生，湖州人，33岁，均为律师及律师公会会员；李公朴先生，常州人，35岁，住愚园路1736弄24号，量才学校校长，均为全国救国会联合会的重要成员。
11月22日，公安局人员前往国际租界静安寺警察局，出示官方公文，请求协助逮捕这四人，罪名涉及某种政治犯罪。静安寺警察局从上海第一特区地方法院获得了逮捕令。沈钧儒、王造时和李公朴三位先生深夜在静安寺区由外籍侦探副巡官“Caley”率领的一队便衣侦探和制服警察逮捕。居住在闸北区的律师沙千里在闸北警察局的协助下被捕。
四名被捕者于11月23日上午9点在江苏高等法院第二分院聂重义法官面前受审。庭审不公开进行。仅有市政检察官金士奎（音译）、辩护律师以及负责此案的警官在场。
经过长时间讯问，聂法官允许被告由各辩护律师提供保释后释放。张以藩、吴森和陈志皋为李公朴先生出庭辩护；俞钟輅和李文池为王造时先生出庭辩护；张耀曾和陈志皋为沈钧儒先生出庭辩护；蔡天东、杨天逊和汪葆楫为沙千里先生出庭辩护。所有保人均被指令在下一次听证会（将于11月25日下午2点举行）时带被告到庭。公安局代表请求引渡被告。
应公安局请求，法租界公董局警务处逮捕了律师史良女士、“生活星期刊”主编邹韬奋先生和经济学家章乃器先生，指控罪名类似。
被捕者于11月23日下午3点在江苏高等法院第三分院受审。张志让先生和唐豪先生为章乃器先生和史良女士出庭辩护；孙祖基先生为邹韬奋先生出庭辩护。据悉，他们也将获准保释。

November 24, 1936. Morning Translation.

Mr. Wang Chao Shih resides at No. 7
Tifeng Road. When our reporter called, only Mr. Wang's
mother and his six-year old son were at home. Mr. Wang
was arrested at 3 a.m. November 23. He offered no
objection to his arrest after he was shown an official
document by the three police officers who had come to
arrest him.

The home of Mr. Sung Chung Shih is
located at No. 51, Tao Yuen Villa (桃源村), Yuyuen Road.
When the five police officers called on the morning of
November 23, he was fast asleep. The officers were
admitted into the house by a servant. One of the officers
remained on guard outside the house, one in the hall, while
the other three followed the servant upstairs. Upon
learning of the arrest, the elder son of Mr. Sung Chung
Shih, who lives at house No. 53 in the same alleyway,
immediately called at his father's home. Both the father
and the son were shown the official despatch from the
Bureau of Public Safety. After a brief consultation with
his son, Mr. Sung Chung Shih left with the officers.

Mr. Li Kung Fu resides at No. 24 Han
Chong Li (亨昌里) off Yuyuen Road. When the police
officers arrived at 2 a.m. November 23, Mr. Li happened
to be out with friends. The officers remained in the
house until about 2.30 a.m. when Mr. Li returned and was
placed under arrest.

The residence of lawyer Soo Chi Lien is
situate at No. 14, Lane No. 524, Avenue Road. When the
police officers arrived, he was in bed.

Mr. Chang Nan Chi resides at No. 24
Shih Wei Li (施卫里) off Route Delastre, French Concession.
Officers of the French Police, accompanied by members of
the Bureau of Public Safety, arrived at the place at 2 a.m.
November 23. They climbed over a short bamboo fence
outside the front gate and were admitted into the house
by the inmates. They immediately proceeded upstairs and
showing Mr. Chang the official document, they placed him
under arrest.

Lawyer Sze Liang lives at No. 1 Lafayette
Villa, Rue Lafayette. At first the foreign and Chinese
detectives could not effect an entrance either from the
front or the back gate, because the inmates refused to
open the door for fear of robbers. The officers then
climbed over the short wall in front of the main gate and
effected an entry into the main hall from where they
immediately proceeded upstairs. Upon being shown
the official document, lawyer Sze Liang at once dressed
herself and left with the officers.

Mr. Chow Tao Feng lives at No. 1, Lane
No. 601, Rue Lafayette. The police officers were admitted
by himself. One of the members of the Bureau of Public
Safety then said to him: "I have been shadowing you for
three days and saw you returning home in a ricksha at about
11 p.m. November 22. I immediately notified the French
Police and we have now come to arrest you." The police
officers then seized several English books which they took
to the station for examination.

李公朴先生住愚园路亨昌里24号。11月23日凌晨2点警察到达时，李先生碰巧与朋友外出。警察在屋内等候至约凌晨2点30分，李先生返回后即被捕。

律师沙千里的住所位于爱文义路524弄14号。警察到达时，他正卧床。

章乃器先生住法租界德拉司脱路施卫里24号。11月23日凌晨2点，法国警察会同公安局人员到达该处。他们翻过前门外的一道矮竹篱笆，由住户放入屋内。他们随即上楼，向章先生出示官方文件后，将其逮捕。

Nov. mber 24, 1936.
Morning Translation.

Hwa Mei an Pao dated Nov.23:

SEVEN PROMINENT RESIDENTS ARRESTED ON GRAVE CHARGES

Mr. Sung Chun Shih (沈儒), native of
Kashing, age 63, residing at House No.51, Lane No.1292 Yu
Yuen Road, member of the Standing Committee of the Shanghai
Bar Association, Mr. Wang Chao Shih (王造時), native of
Kiangsi Province, age 34, residing at House No.7 Tifeng
Road, and Mr. Soo Chi Lien (沙千里), native of Huchow, age
33, both lawyers and members of the Bar Association,
and Mr. Li Kung Pu (李公樸), native of Zangchow, age 35,
residing at House No.24, Lane No.1736, Yu Yuen Road, President
of the Liang Tsai School (量才學校), are all prominent
members of the Federation of National Salvation Associations.
On November 22, members of the Bureau of Public
Safety called at the Bubbling Well Police Station of the
International Settlement, produced an official dispatch and
requested assistance to effect the arrest of these four
persons for some political offence. Warrants of arrest
were obtained from the Shanghai First Special District Court
by the Bubbling Well Police Station. Messrs. Sung Chun
Shih, Wang Chao Shih and Li Kung Pu were arrested in Bubbling
Well district late at night by a party of detectives and
uniformed policemen under Foreign Detective Sub-Inspector
"Caley". Lawyer Soo Chi Lien who lives in Sinza District
was arrested with the assistance of Sinza Police Station.
The four arrested persons were arraigned before
Judge Nyi Chung Nee (聶重義) of the Second Branch of the
Kiangsu High Court at 9 a.m. November 23. The proceedings
were held in camera. Only Mr. King S. Kum, the Municipal
Advocate, the lawyers for the defence and the police officers
in charge of the case were present.
After a lengthy interrogation, Judge Nyi allowed
the accused to be released on bail furnished by their
respective lawyers. Messrs. Chang Yi Fan (張以藩),
Ngoh Goong (吳森) and Chen Tse Kao (陳志皋) are
appearing for Mr. Li Kung Pu; Messrs. Yu Chung Loh (俞鍾輅)
and Li Yung Chi (李文池) for Mr. Wang Chao Shih; Messrs.
Chang Yao Tseng (張耀曾) and Chen Tse Kao for Mr. Sung
Chun Shih; Messrs. Tsai Loh Zung (蔡天東), Yang Tien Sung
(楊天遜) and Aung Pao Chi (汪葆楫) for Mr. Soo Chi Lien.
All the guarantors were instructed to produce the accused
at the next hearing which will take place at 2 p.m.
November 25. The representatives of the Bureau of Public
Safety requested the extradition of the accused.
At the request of the Bureau of Public Safety,
the French Municipal Police have arrested Miss Sze Liang
(史良), a lawyer, Mr. Chow Tao Feng (鄒奮), Editor-
in-Chief of the "Livelihood Sunday Weekly", and Mr. Chang
Nan Chi (章乃器), an economist, on a similar charge.
The arrested persons were arraigned before
the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court at 3 p.m.
November 23. Messrs. Chang Tse Niang (張志讓) and Tong Hwa
(唐豪) are appearing for Mr. Chang Nan Chi and Miss Sze
Liang; Mr. Sung Tso Chi (孫祖基) for Mr. Chow Tao Feng.
It is learned that they will likewise be released on bail.
The following information was secured from the
families of the various accused by a reporter of this paper:-

1. Executive of the Y.W.C.A. of Shanghai, 999 Bubbling
Well Road.

Mr. Lieu Ts-hsiang (劉世翔), Chief of the Receiving
and Despatching Section received and signed the summons on
behalf of the executive committee.

meetings held by members of National Salvation Associations.
These reports were forwarded to the Legal Department on
January 12, 1937.

Summons received and signed by him. He appeared
before the Court on January 30, 1937 when after questioning
was instructed to appear at the Procurator's Office, Kiangsu
High Court, Soochow at 2 p.m. February 3, 1937 for interrogation.

Made by D.S. Lockwood    Forwarded by
At 3.20 p.m. January 27 members of the Special
Branch accompanied by detectives from Wayside Station
visited the premises of the Jung Zun Primary School,
East Seward Road to serve summons No.2532 issued by
Judge Yoen of the 2nd Branch Kiangsu High Court on
Tsang Tzoonf Te.
The principal when questioned stated that no such
person had been employed as a teacher or enrolled as a
student in the school.
At 5 p.m. members of the Special Branch accompanied
by detectives from Central Station proceeded to the Ants
Training School, 300 Nanking Road to serve summons No.2532
on one named Zung Tsauh. On arrival it was found that the
school was closed. A visit was paid to the Ants' Club,
4th floor, Continental Emporium Building, Nanking Road
when it was learned that no such person existed.
D. S. Lockwood.
D. S.
D.C. (Special Branch).

1月27日下午3时20分，特别支部成员在韦尔斯利巡捕房（Wayside Station）侦探的陪同下，前往东熙华德路荣尊小学，送达江苏高等法院第二分院Yoen法官签发给Tsang Tzoonf Te的第2532号传票。
校长在接受询问时表示，该校未曾雇佣此人担任教师，也未招收其为学生。

制作人：D.S. Lockwood。转呈人 [签名]

上午11时15分，副督察 Cady, C.D.C. 279 (静安寺路)，在副督察 Lockwood 和探员 Pan Lien-pih（特别支部）的陪同下，向静安寺路999号上海基督教女青年会负责人送达了江苏高等法院第二分院Nyih法官签发的第1225号传票。该会秘书兼代理总干事 Tsang Ts Yoh( ) 女士接收并签署了传票。
上午11时40分，副督察 Smith, C.D.S. 164 (老闸)，在副督察 Lockwood 和探员 Pan Lien-pih（特别支部）的陪同下，向虞洽卿路宁波同乡会负责人送达了江苏高等法院第二分院Nyih法官签发的第1225号传票。该会收发处处长 Lieu Ts Hsiang( ) 先生代表执行委员会接收并签署了传票。
下午2时20分，副督察 Bader, C.D.C. 260 (中央)，在副督察 Lockwood 和探员 Pan Lien-pih（特别支部）的陪同下，向圆明园路中国基督教女青年会全国委员会负责人送达了江苏高等法院第二分院Nyih法官签发的第1225号传票。秘书 Sih Tsung-bei(薛 增 佩) 小姐接收并签署了传票。
（印：B / 1937年1月7日）
J. D. Lockwood.
D. S.

S.1, Special Branch
November 13, 1936.

Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation Federation
- convenes meetings in celebration of the birthday of
the late Kuomintang Leader.

The Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation
Federation convened a meeting of members of local national
salvation associations in the Chinese Y.W.C.A., 999 Bubbling
Well Road, at 1 p.m. November 12, ostensibly to celebrate the
birthday of the late Kuomintang leader Dr. Sun Yat-sen.

A large number of Chinese consisting of students,
labourers and shop assistants proceeded to the Ningpo Fellow
Countrymen's Association, 480 Yu Ya Ching Road, between 12
noon and 1 p.m. November 12, but upon arrival there were
informed by pickets that the Police and officials of the
Association had forbidden the meeting there, and were instructed
to proceed to the Chinese Y.W.C.A., the second meeting place.
By 2 p.m. about 800 persons had entered the compound of the
Y.W.C.A. and at that time the meeting was formally opened.
A presidium consisting of the following persons was formed :-

Li Kung-poh (李公樸), Principal of the Liang Zai
Supplementary School, Continental Emporium
Building, Nanking Road, and one of the leading
members of the Vocational Circles National
Salvation Association.

Tsang Mai-chi (章乃器), ex-Sub-Manager of the Chekiang
Industrial Bank, and a leading member of the
Cultural Circles National Salvation Association.

Wong Chao-dzu (王造時), a lawyer by profession,
living at 7B Tifeng Road, a leading member of the
Cultural Circles National Salvation Association.

Sung Chun-dzu (沈鈞儒), a lawyer by profession, living
at 5 Tao Yuan Fang, Yu Yuen Road, and concurrently
Dean of the Shanghai Law College, Kiangwan Road. He
is a leading member of the Cultural Circles National
Salvation Association.

Sz Liang (史良), a female lawyer, living at 1
Lafayette Terrace, Rue Lafayette. A leading member
of the Women's Circles National Salvation Association.

Soo Chien-li (沙千里), a lawyer by profession with
an office at the Tsung Chen (宗誠) Building,
Kiukiang Road. A committee member of the Ants' Club
(Ants' Club), Room 420 Continental Emporium Building,
Nanking Road, and concurrently a leading member of
the Vocational Circles National Salvation Association.
pages.zh:
S.1，特别支部
1936年11月13日。

上海各界救国联合会
- 召开会议庆祝已故国民党领袖诞辰。

上海各界救国联合会于11月12日下午1时，在静安寺路999号中国基督教女青年会召集各地救国会成员开会，名义上是为了庆祝已故国民党领袖孙中山博士的诞辰。

11月12日中午12时至下午1时之间，大量由学生、劳工和店员组成的中国人前往虞洽卿路480号宁波同乡会，但到达后被告知，纠察队称警察和同乡会官员禁止在此开会，并指示他们前往第二个会场，即中国基督教女青年会。到下午2时，约有800人进入女青年会大院，会议随即正式开幕。成立了由以下人员组成的主席团：-

李公樸 (Li Kung-poh)，良才补习学校校长，校址位于南京路大陆商场，职业界救国会主要成员之一。

章乃器 (Tsang Mai-chi)，前浙江实业银行副经理，文化界救国会主要成员。

王造時 (Wong Chao-dzu)，律师，居住于提篮桥路7B号，文化界救国会主要成员。

沈鈞儒 (Sung Chun-dzu)，律师，居住于愚园路桃源坊5号，兼任江湾路上海法学院院长。他是文化界救国会主要成员。

史良 (Sz Liang)，女律师，居住于辣斐德路辣斐德新村1号。妇女界救国会主要成员。

沙千里 (Soo Chien-li)，律师，办公地点位于九江路宗誠大楼。蚁社俱乐部（Ants' Club）委员，地址为南京路大陆商场420室，同时兼任职业界救国会主要成员。

pages.en:
- 2 -

Yang Ching-sai (楊經才), a supervisor in the Tien Yih
(天一) Insurance Company, 255 Peking Road. A
leading member of the Vocational Circles National
Salvation Association.

After the formal opening of the meeting, those
present sang two songs entitled "March of Volunteer Armies
(義勇軍進行曲) and "Beat them back home" (打回老家去)
(the latter song is anti-Japanese in nature). Li Kung-poh
then made a speech eulogizing the deeds and spirit of the late
Dr. Sun Yat-sen. He stated that the object of the meeting
apart from celebrating the anniversary was to induce the
authorities to cease concluding secret agreements with Japan
and advocated that the nation should be saved in accordance
with the instructions of the late leader.

The second speaker was Tsang Hai-chi, who stated
that China should unite with Great Britain, the United States,
France and Soviet Russia and form a group to ensure the safety
of China against Japan.

Wong Chao-dzu followed, and made a speech stating
that the late Kuomintang leader advocated that a treaty should
be concluded with Soviet Russia, that the Communist Party
should be allowed in China, and agriculture and industry should
be developed. He continued to say that the present Chinese
Government had ignored these instructions and therefore China
suffered from foreign aggression.

Sung Chun-dzu (沈鈞儒) was the next speaker. He
also advocated the policies mentioned above as the means to
save China from ruin. He also remarked that Dr. Sun Yat-sen
had praised Lenin and as conditions in Soviet Russia were
had
excellent, Dr. Sun Yat-sen/been right. He said that no power
in the world could break Soviet Russia. He concluded that
China should unite with the Communist Party in compliance
with the instructions of Dr. Sun. He was of the opinion that
the Government should forthwith suspend the anti-Communist
campaign.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

杨经才（Yang Ching-sai），北京路255号天一（Tien Yih）保险公司监理员。职业界救国会主要成员。

会议正式开始后，与会者合唱了两首歌曲，题为《义勇军进行曲》和《打回老家去》（后者具有反日性质）。随后李公朴发表演讲，颂扬已故孙中山博士的事迹和精神。他指出，此次会议的目的除了纪念诞辰外，还旨在促使当局停止与日本缔结秘密协定，并主张应按照已故领袖的指示来拯救国家。

第二位发言者是章乃器（Tsang Hai-chi，音译），他表示中国应与英国、美国、法国和苏俄联合，组成一个团体，以确保中国免受日本的侵害。

接着王造时（Wong Chao-dzu，音译）发言，他在演讲中指出，已故国民党领袖主张与苏俄缔结条约，允许共产党在中国存在，并发展农业和工业。他继续说，现任中国政府忽视了这些指示，因此中国遭受了外国侵略。

下一位发言者是沈钧儒（Sung Chun-dzu）。他也主张将上述政策作为挽救中国免于灭亡的手段。他还提到，孙中山博士曾赞扬列宁，鉴于苏俄的状况良好，孙中山博士是正确的。他说，世界上没有任何力量能够摧毁苏俄。他总结道，中国应按照孙中山博士的指示与共产党联合。他认为政府应立即停止反共运动。

pages.en:
- 3 -

Sz Liang was the fifth speaker. She stated that the
Chinese Government should not prohibit the people from taking
part in the national salvation movement at the present
critical time and that all the Chinese irrespective of parties
should unanimously resist Japan. She remarked that according
to the instructions of Dr. Sun, the Government should protect
the people in the national salvation movement but the present
government, she continued, not only refrained from protecting
the people, but oppressed them.

At this point, an invitation was issued to those
present to deliver speeches. Two female workers named Fang
Dzu (方 氏) and Liu Tsao-dee (劉招弟), claiming to be in the
employ of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill, accepted the invitation.
Fang Dzu reported that the workers of Japanese cotton mills
had gone on strike to demand an increase in wages and that some
workers had been taken to a small room by the Japanese
management. She described that one of these workers had been
killed by the Japanese and her body put in a sack and thrown
into the Wangpoo. At this juncture, the audience commenced
to shout slogans including "Overthrow the Japanese Imperialists"
and "Assist the Strikers." Liu Tsao-dee, the next speaker,
made another speech depicting how the workers were cruelly
exploited by the capitalists and requested the attendance to
render assistance to the workers.

Tsang Kai-chi again took the platform and informed
the crowd that Madame Sun Yat-sen had intended to be present
to deliver a speech, but was prevented by illness. He read
the following speech written by her.

"In commemoration of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen, brethren
throughout the nation should continue to struggle for the
emancipation of the Chinese race. At present, we should
realize that our greatest enemies are the Japanese
Imperialists and Chinese traitors."
pages.zh:
- 3 -

史良（Sz Liang，音译）是第五位发言者。她表示，在当前危急时刻，中国政府不应禁止人民参加救国运动，所有中国人无论党派如何，都应一致抗日。她指出，根据孙中山博士的指示，政府应保护参与救国运动的民众，但她接着说，现任政府不仅没有保护民众，反而压迫他们。

此时，邀请在场人士发表演讲。两名自称受雇于大康纱厂的女工，方氏（Fang Dzu）和刘招弟（Liu Tsao-dee），接受了邀请。方氏报告说，日本纱厂的工人罢工要求增加工资，一些工人被日本管理层带进一个小房间。她描述说，其中一名工人被日本人杀害，尸体被装入麻袋扔进黄浦江。此时，观众开始高呼口号，包括“打倒日本帝国主义”和“援助罢工工人”。下一位发言者刘招弟发表了另一篇演讲，描绘了工人如何受到资本家的残酷剥削，并请求在场人士向工人提供援助。

章乃器（Tsang Kai-chi，音译）再次上台，告知群众宋庆龄女士原打算出席并发表演讲，但因病未能前来。他宣读了她撰写的以下演讲稿。

“为纪念已故孙中山博士，全国同胞应继续为中华民族的解放而斗争。目前，我们应认识到，我们最大的敌人是日本帝国主义者和中国汉奸。”

pages.en:
- 4 -

"We should unite with all nations who are lovers of
peace and form an international league against invasion,
especially by allying with Great Britain, U.S.A., France,
and Soviet Russia to ensure collective safety on the Pacific
and to oppose the Japanese imperialists. We should ally
with the peace-loving masses of Japan, Korea and Formosa
and form a united international battle line to overthrow the
Fascist militarists of Japan. We should unite all parties
and classes to form a united battle line for the purpose of
overthrowing the Japanese imperialists.

"The three policies of Dr. Sun indicate the above
plans. We should go forward bravely. Steel and blood
will certainly accomplish the glorious enterprise for the
emancipation of the race."

Tsang Nai-chi concluded by saying that the people
should of their own accord rise and save their nation despite
obstruction from the Government.

Wong Chao-dz then took the platform and read the
following proposals to the crowd, which were duly passed :
1) That the attendance should contribute money to support
the strikers of Japanese cotton mills.
2) That the Government be requested to cease concluding secret
agreements with Japan, but to send troops to the North
to assist the anti-Japanese troops at Suiyuan.
3) That a delegation be appointed to proceed to the North
and to convey good wishes to the anti-Japanese armies at
Suiyuan.
4) That the Government be requested to unite with Great
Britain, United States of America, France and Soviet Russia
and form an international league against Japan.
pages.zh:
- 4 -

“我们应与所有爱好和平的国家联合，组成反侵略的国际联盟，特别是通过与英国、美国、法国和苏俄结盟，以确保太平洋地区的集体安全，并对抗日本帝国主义者。我们应与日本、朝鲜和台湾的爱好和平的民众结盟，组成统一的国际战线，以推翻日本的法西斯军国主义者。我们应团结各党派和各阶层，组成统一战线，旨在推翻日本帝国主义者。

“孙中山博士的三大政策指明了上述计划。我们要勇敢前进。钢铁和鲜血必将完成民族解放的光荣事业。”

章乃器（Tsang Nai-chi，音译）最后说，尽管受到政府的阻挠，人民仍应自觉起来拯救自己的国家。

随后王造时（Wong Chao-dz，音译）上台，向群众宣读以下提案，并获得通过：
1) 与会者捐款支持日本纱厂罢工工人。
2) 请求政府停止与日本缔结秘密协定，并派兵北上，援助绥远的抗日部队。
3) 指派代表团前往北方，向绥远抗日军队传达慰问之意。
4) 请求政府与英国、美利坚合众国、法国和苏俄联合，组成反日国际联盟。

pages.en:
- 5 -

5) That a circular telegram be despatched informing
the people throughout China of the minutes of this
meeting.
Wong Chao-dzu then submitted to the meeting the
following proposals made by the Shanghai Municipality
Students Circles National Salvation Association :-
1) That the Government release all students arrested
in connection with the national salvation Movement.
2) That the authorities of various universities be
induced to take back those students dismissed in
connection with the national salvation movement.
3) That the Government be urged to enforce special
education during times of national crisis.
The following resolutions proposed by members
of the audience were then discussed and passed :-
1) That funds be raised by public subscription on behalf
of the strikers in a three days' campaign commencing
on November 13.
2) That Groups be formed to sympathize with the strikers
in Japanese cotton mills.
3) That a demand be submitted for the release of workers
arrested in connection with the strike in Japanese
cotton mills, failing which a general strike be
declared.
4) That the General Labour Union be requested to call
for a strike of all labourers in Shanghai, in sympathy
with the Japanese cotton mill strikers.
5) That a "Japanese Mill Strikers' Support Committee" be
formed consisting of two representatives from each local
public body.
pages.zh:
- 5 -

5) 发出通电，将本次会议纪要告知全中国人民。
随后，王造时向会议提交了上海市学生界救国会提出的以下提案：
1) 政府释放因救国运动被捕的所有学生。
2) 促使各大学当局收回因救国运动被开除的学生。
3) 敦促政府在国家危机时期实施特种教育。
随后讨论并通过了由与会成员提出的以下决议：
1) 从11月13日开始，开展为期三天的公众募捐活动，为罢工工人筹集资金。
2) 成立团体，同情日本纱厂罢工工人。
3) 提出释放因日本纱厂罢工而被捕工人的要求，否则宣布总罢工。
4) 请求总工会号召上海所有劳工罢工，以声援日本纱厂罢工工人。
5) 成立“日厂罢工工人后援会”，由各地方公共团体各派两名代表组成。

pages.en:
- 6 -
6. That a circular telegram be despatched asking Chinese
at home and abroad to render assistance to the strikers
in Japanese cotton mills.
7. That anti-Japanese propaganda groups be formed in
connection with the strike of the Japanese cotton mills.
8. That the anti-Communist campaign undertaken by the
National Government be opposed.
Finally it was decided to refer all these regulations
to the members of the presidium for execution. The meeting
was concluded at 4 p.m. when the following slogans were shouted:-
1. Support the anti-Japanese troops in Suiyuan.
2. Urge the government to issue a general mobilization
order at once in order to resist Japan.
3. Oppose the co-operation of China and Japan in the anti-
communist campaign, and demand the immediate suspension
of the communist suppression campaign.
4. Ally with Great Britain, U.S.A., France and Soviet Russia
to ensure collective safety on the Pacific.
5. Unite various parties in the country to resist foreign
aggression.
6. Let Chinese and Japanese masses unite and overthrow the
Japanese Imperialists.
7. Urge the Kuomintang to restore the National revolutionary
spirit of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen.
8. Oppose the Government's connivance at the Japanese
invasion into North China.
9. The revolutionary spirit of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen
is immortal !
10. Long live the emancipation of the Republic of China.
pages.zh:
- 6 -
6. 发出通电，呼吁海内外华人援助日本纱厂罢工工人。
7. 结合日本纱厂罢工，成立反日宣传团体。
8. 反对国民政府进行的反共运动。
最后决定将所有这些规章移交主席团成员执行。下午4时会议结束，当时高呼了以下口号：
1. 支援绥远抗日部队。
2. 敦促政府立即发布总动员令以抵抗日本。
3. 反对中日在反共运动中的合作，并要求立即停止剿共运动。
4. 与英国、美国、法国和苏俄结盟，以确保太平洋地区的集体安全。
5. 团结国内各党派以抵抗外国侵略。
6. 让中日民众联合起来，推翻日本帝国主义者。
7. 敦促国民党恢复已故孙中山博士的革命精神。
8. 反对政府纵容日本入侵华北。
9. 已故孙中山博士的革命精神永垂不朽！
10. 中华民国解放万岁。

pages.en:
- 7 -

While the crowd which towards the close of the
meeting numbered approximately 1,000 persons was dispersing,
persons were posted at an inner gate of the Y.M.C.A. premises
and collected subscriptions in support of the strikers of
Japanese cotton mills. A total sum of $200 was raised.

During the proceedings, copies of two kinds of
literature were distributed among the attendance. One is
entitled "Special Issue of the National Salvation Intelligence
in commemoration of the birthday of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen."
It contains the speech of Madame Sun Yat-sen and the ten slogans
referred to above. The other, a handbill, contains a
manifesto purporting to emanate from the Shanghai Municipality
Students Circles National Salvation Association bearing on the
commemoration of the birthday of the late Kuomintang leader.
This handbill advocates that the Government should

1. Carry out Dr. Sun's revolutionary policies.
2. Assist the anti-Japanese troops at Suiyuan.
3. Enforce "Too Yuan" (?) diplomacy.
4. Protect the freedom of patriotic movements.

Also present at the meeting were ten plain-clothes
members of the Bureau of Public Safety and Mr. and Mrs. Max
Granich. Max Granich is the editor of the reactionary
publication entitled "Voice of China."
pages.zh:
- 7 -

当会议接近尾声、人群（约1000人）开始疏散时，有人在青年会（Y.M.C.A.）场所的内门处设点，募集捐款以支持日本纱厂罢工工人。共筹集善款200元。

在活动过程中，向与会者分发两种文献。一种题为《纪念已故孙中山博士诞辰救国情报特刊》。其中包含宋庆龄女士的演讲以及上述十条口号。另一种是传单，包含一份据称出自上海市学生界救国会的宣言，内容涉及纪念已故国民党领袖诞辰。该传单主张政府应

1. 实行孙中山博士的革命政策。
2. 援助绥远抗日部队。
3. 推行“Too Yuan” (?)（原文不清）外交。
4. 保护爱国运动的自由。

出席会议的还有十名便衣公共安全局成员，以及马克斯·格拉尼奇（Max Granich）夫妇。马克斯·格拉尼奇是反动刊物《中国之声》（Voice of China）的编辑。

Extract from Intelligence Report dated February 10, 1936
--------------

Employees of local Chinese banks to form national
salvation association

About three hundred Chinese employees of local
Chinese banks held a meeting in the Ningpo Fellow
Countrymen's Association, 480 Thibet Road, at 10.45 a.m.
February 9 and decided to organize a national salvation
association. Speeches denouncing the weakness of the
Nanking Government and Japanese imperialism in general
were delivered by the following persons :-

Pan Niang-yao (潘仰), Chief of the Guidance
Department of the Chung Hwa Vocational Education
Institute, 80 Route Voyron, and a senior employee
of the Joint Savings Society, 170 Bubbling Well
Road.

Li Kung-poh (李公樸), principal of the Liang Zai
Supplementary School, Continental Emporium
Building, Nanking Road.

Sung Chun-su (沈儒), Dean of the Shanghai College
of Law.

Weng Zao-da (王造時), ex-professor of the Kwong Hwa
University.

The meeting terminated at 12.15 p.m.
